description.title: Avatar: The Way of Water (2022) | Nattosheru Review [ENG/SPA]
description.body: /></center>\n\n<div class=\
>\n<div class=\

>\n\nHello, cinema fans. Today we’re back with more films from one of the greatest and most iconic directors of the century. This time, I’m bringing you the sequel to a famous film that made history both at the box office and in the film world for over a decade. A sequel that, while it doesn’t quite match the magnificence of its predecessor, did manage to expand a world that was already enormous in its own right. Co-written, produced, and directed by the great

>James Cameron, Avatar: The Way of Water stars Sam Worthington, Zoe Saldaña, Stephen Lang, Sigourney Weaver, among others. Discover what was, at the time, the most anticipated sequel of the entire century.

>
Hola, fanáticos del cine. Hoy regresamos con más películas de uno de los directores más grandes y de culto del siglo. Esta vez les traigo la secuela de una famosa película que hizo historia tanto en taquilla como en el mundo del cine durante más de una década. Una secuela que, si bien no consigue igualar la magnificencia de su antecesora, sí logró expandir un mundo que ya era enorme de por sí. Coescrita, producida y dirigida por el gran James Cameron, Avatar: The Way of Water está protagonizada por Sam Worthington, Zoe Saldaña, Stephen Lang, Sigourney Weaver, entre otros. Conoce la que fue en su momento la secuela más esperada de todo el siglo.
/>\n\n
/><strong><em></br><s5>Source: <a href=\
>FilmAffinity.\n\n
/></center>\n\n<div class=\
>\n<div class=\

>

Plot

The film opens with breathtaking views of the beautiful and majestic world of Pandora. We then hear a monologue from our protagonist, Jake Sully, who tells us that in the Na’vi clan known as the Omaticaya, there is a tradition for mothers to sing a “necklace of songs,” each representing the birth of a new life. As we listen to Neytiri sing, we see in a sequence of flashbacks how she and Jake have had several children over the 16 years that have passed since the first human invasion we saw in the previous film. In addition to Neteyam and Lo’ak, they have a younger daughter named Tuk and also adopt the daughter of Dr. Grace’s inert avatar, Kiri.

>

Trama

La película inicia mostrándonos vistas impresionantes del hermoso y grandioso mundo de Pandora, luego escuchamos un monólogo de nuestro protagonista, Jake Sully, quien nos cuenta que en el clan de los Na’vi llamado Omaticaya hay una tradición para las madres que la de cantar un “collar de cánticos” que representan cada uno el nacimiento de una nueva vida. Mientras escuchamos a Neytiri cantar vemos en una secuencia de recuerdos cómo ella y Jake tienen varios hijos durante los 16 años que pasaron, luego de la primera invasión humana que vimos en la película anterior. Aparte de Neteyam y Lo’ak, tienen una hija menor llamada Tuk y adoptan también a la hija del avatar inerte de la Dra. Grace, Kiri.

/>

Trailer & Review

/> Here is the movie trailer: https://youtu.be/d9MyW72ELq0?si=aWgOVKy-uKUZZiy4

By:
>Avatar.\n\n
/>
>\n<div class=\
>\n\nBefore I tell you about this sequel, which has been eagerly awaited by everyone who saw <strong><a href=\
>Avatar when they were very young—like me—I’d like to explain why I’m not reviewing one of the films that came before the one I’m discussing today. The reason is that I already wrote a

>review for this community two years ago, when I was just starting out here on Hive and my approach to reviewing movies wasn’t the same as it is now. Honestly, I’d like to be able to correct some details in that review I wrote, mostly to add several details I overlooked and that I think are worth mentioning regarding
>Avatar.\n\nBecause as much as it might not seem like it based on what you can read in that review I wrote back then, now that I’ve rewatched
>Avatar to catch up so I can watch The Way of Water, I’ve realized that it is—without a doubt—a masterpiece of science fiction cinema that stands in a league of its own.

>Avatar is, in short, a magnificent work that stands perfectly on its own as a story of adventure, drama, science fiction, romance, action, betrayal, redemption, war, and so much more. Talking about this first installment of James Cameron’s most beloved film saga is like telling you a fantastic story with many themes and nuances to explore.

>
<blockquote>

Antes de hablarles de ésta secuela tan esperada por todos los que vieron <strong><a href=\
>Avatar desde muy pequeños -como yo-, quisiera mencionarles el por qué no les hablo de una de dicha película que antecedió la que les traigo hoy. La razón es porque ya le he hecho una

>reseña para esta comunidad hace ya dos años, cuando apenas estaba empezando aquí en Hive y mi forma de reseñar películas no era igual a como es ahora. De verdad, me gustaría poder corregir algunos detalles de dicha reseña que hice, más que nada para agregar varios detalles que he pasado por alto y que considero que merecen la pena hablar de
>Avatar.\n\nPorque por mucho que no lo parezca con lo que pueden leer en aquella reseña que le hice en aquel entonces, ahora que he vuelto a ver
>Avatar para ponerme al día y así ver The Way of Water, me he dado cuenta de que -definitivamente- es una obra maestra del cine de ciencia ficción que no tiene ningún punto de comparación.

>Avatar es, en definitiva, una obra magnífica que sirve perfectamente como una historia independiente de aventura, drama, ciencia ficción, romance, acción, traición, redención, guerras y muchas cosas más. Hablar de esta primera entrega de la saga de películas más querida de James Cameron es como hablarles de una historia fantástica con muchos temas y matices por tocar.
/>\n\n
alt=\
><strong><em></br><s5>Source: <a href=\
>Tenor.\n\n
/></center>\n\n<div class=\
>\n<div class=\

>\n\nWhile its story isn’t all that different from what we’ve seen in other action, adventure, and science fiction films—like the typical protagonist who becomes a hero and all that—in <strong><a href=\

>Avatar we discover that it’s so much more than that. A protagonist who goes from being the enemy to becoming the savior of the world—a world very different from anything we know, yet one that shares many similarities and boasts a magnificent natural beauty that gives us pause for thought. And as if that weren’t enough, there’s the redemption and growth of a warrior who chose to betray his own kind for the sake of the people he loves. All of this is just a small glimpse of what

>Avatar represents. Even so, I believe that its long-awaited sequel, titled “The Way of Water,” is something that significantly changes everything we saw in its predecessor. To that end, I remind you that this film serves more as a standalone story; it’s more like the beginning of a new story set years after everything we saw and discussed about Avatar at the time. We meet the children of Jake Sully and Neytiri, each of whom stands out in their own way. We also see a human boy named Spider who grows up and interacts with them—he is none other than the son of Colonel Miles Quaritch. A strange combination, if you think about it, especially given that Kiri is Dr. Grace’s daughter.

>
<blockquote>

Si bien su historia no se aleja mucho a lo que ya hemos visto en otras películas de acción, aventura y ciencia ficción como lo es el típico protagonista que se convierte en héroe y todo eso; en <strong><a href=\

>Avatar podemos descubrir que es muchísimo más que eso. Un protagonista que pasa de ser el enemigo a ser el salvador del mundo, un mundo muy distinto a todo lo conocido, pero que a su vez tiene muchas similitudes y una naturaleza magnífica que nos ponen a reflexionar. Y por si no fuera suficiente, la redención y el desarrollo de un guerrero que decidió traicionar a su propia especie por la gente que ama. Todo esto es solo un pequeño atisbo de lo que representa

>Avatar. Aún así, considero que su tan esperada secuela titulada “The Way of Water” es algo que cambia en gran medida todo lo que llegamos a ver de su antecesora. Para esto les recuerdo que esta película sirve más como una historia aparte, es más como el inicio de una nueva historia de años después de todo lo visto y hablado de Avatar en su momento. Conocemos a los hijos de Jake Sully y Neytiri, quienes se destacan cada uno a su manera. También vemos que hay un niño humano que crece y se relaciona con ellos llamado Spider quien es hijo ni más ni menos que del coronel Miles Quaritch. Una extraña combinación, si se ponen a pensar, sobre todo por Kiri quien es hija de la Dra. Grace.
/>\n\n
alt=\
><strong><em></br><s5>Source: <a href=\
>Tenor.\n\n
/></center>\n\n<div class=\
>\n<div class=\

> Let’s remember that she is the daughter of her avatar, who became pregnant after losing her life at the end of the previous film, and that body has remained lifeless ever since. So the fact that her body became pregnant is a very… spiritual miracle, we might say. We can already see certain spiritual and divine influences in this film, something we’ve seen before in the previous movie with Eywa, but here it’s emphasized more than ever with this particular character. It’s as if James Cameron drew inspiration from a very popular religious source to develop Kiri’s origin and her importance to the future of the story itself. But anyway, this is just one of many details that left me thinking quite a bit throughout the film’s three-hour runtime. Another thing that really caught my attention is that the screenwriters decided to make several changes to the original plot, starting with the expulsion of Jake Sully’s family from the Omaticaya clan. We also see the unexpected and unwelcome return of Captain Miles Quaritch, but this time as a Na’vi hybrid with DNA from his original body. This last detail blew my mind at the beginning of the film, and honestly, I didn’t end up liking it at all.

>
Recordemos que es hija de su avatar, quien quedó embarazada luego de perder la vida al final de la película anterior y dicho cuerpo quedó inerte desde entonces. Así que el hecho de que su cuerpo haya quedado embarazado es un milagro muy… espiritual, podríamos decir. Ya por este lado podemos notar ciertas influencias espirituales y divinas en esta película, cosa que ya hemos visto antes en la película anterior con Eywa, pero aquí se acentúa más que nunca con este personaje en particular. Es como si James Cameron se hubiera inspirado en una fuente religiosa muy popular para desarrollar el origen de Kiri y su importancia en el futuro de la misma historia. Pero bueno, esto es solo uno de muchos detalles que me dejaron pensando bastante a lo largo de las tres horas de duración que tiene esta película. Otra cosa que me llamó mucho la atención es que los guionistas decidieron hacer varios cambios en la trama original, empezando con la expulsión de la familia de Jake Sully del clan Omaticaya. También podemos ver el regreso inesperado e indeseado del capitán Miles Quaritch, pero esta vez como un Na’vi mestizo con ADN de su cuerpo original. Esto último es algo que me voló la cabeza al principio de esta película y que, sinceramente, no me terminó gustando la verdad.
/>\n\n
alt=\
><strong><em></br><s5>Source: <a href=\
>Tenor.\n\n
/></center>\n\n<div class=\
>\n<div class=\

> To throw in a Plot Twist like that, after all the turmoil in the previous movie, is completely crazy. But then again, generally speaking, you’d expect something like this from a race as stubborn and resourceful as humanity, which loves to experiment with things in search of “immortality” and all that. In fact, if we think about it right now, after having seen the movie, it makes more sense that humanity in this not-too-distant future has ended up depending on the resources offered by certain wild species on Pandora to achieve immortality and thus stave off its impending extinction. From here, we connect all of this to human survival and how the irony of their own self-destruction forced them to migrate and invade planets, bringing their evils and catastrophes to other intelligent species. The more I reflect on the plot of these films, the more convinced I am that James Cameron is trying to give us a clear message about how miserable we humans are as a “civilization.” The way he weaves real-life elements into this story—such as warfare, oppression, xenophobia, and the hunting of endangered species—is fascinating. I can’t deny that some of these themes strike a deep chord in the heart, especially when we see how they’re portrayed in this film.

>
Que metan un Plot-Twist así, luego de toda la odisea que hubo en la película anterior, es una locura total. Pero bueno, en reglas generales es de esperarse algo así de una raza tan terca y ocurrente como lo es la humanidad que le gusta experimentar con cosas en busca de la “inmortalidad” y todo eso. Incluso, si nos ponemos a pensar en esto ahora mismo, luego de haber visto la película, tiene más sentido que dicha humanidad en este futuro no lejano haya terminado dependiendo de dichos recursos que ofrecen ciertas especies salvajes de Pandora para conseguir la inmortalidad y así mantenerse lejos de su próxima extinción. De aquí ligamos todo esto con la supervivencia humana y cómo la ironía de su propia autodestrucción los obligó a migrar e invadir planetas, llevando sus males y catástrofes a otras especies inteligentes. Cada vez que reflexiono más y más sobre la trama de estas películas, más convencido estoy de que James Cameron busca darnos un mensaje claro de lo miserables que somos los seres humanos como “civilización”. La forma en la que mezcla cosas de la vida real en esta historia como lo son las guerreras, la opresión, la xenofobia y la caza de especies en extinción es fascinante. No niego que pega muy hondo en el corazón algunos de estos temas, sobre todo al ver cómo nos lo muestran en esta película.
/>\n\n
alt=\
><strong><em></br><s5>Source: <a href=\
>Tenor.\n\n
/></center>\n\n<div class=\
>\n<div class=\

> The various scenes in which we see the clans suffering from oppression, abuse, and torture at the hands of humans armed with firearms are portrayed by the film itself as cruel—a portrayal that is entirely accurate. We also see humanity’s utter disbelief and malice as the captain’s avatar clone learns about Na’vi culture with his team in order to use them to his advantage for the hunt and future destruction of those very clans. But something that didn’t quite convince me was the captain’s abrupt change in this film, after seeing how cold, cruel, and ruthless he was toward the Na’vi in the previous film. Here, on the other hand, we see him as more emotional, vulnerable, and considerate of others, though something tells me there’s a specific reason for this, and that’s the presence of his son. I still don’t find that detail entirely convincing, especially given the unfortunate ending they give us in this movie regarding this character. I mean, after EVERYTHING that scum of a human being caused, they give him that ending… why, for what? I don’t understand a thing, honestly. But well, on one hand, this might be somewhat understandable if we consider the number of losses and/or casualties we had here compared to the terrible massacre we saw at the end of the previous movie.

>
Las distintas escenas donde vemos a los clanes sufrir de la opresión, el abuso y la tortura de los humanos con sus armas de fuego es algo que la propia película nos la hacen ver como algo cruel, cosa que es más que acertado. También vemos la total incredulidad y malicia de la humanidad al ver cómo el clon avatar del capitán aprende sobre la cultura Na’vi con su equipo para así utilizarlos a su favor para la cacería y futura destrucción de los mismos clanes. Pero algo que no me terminó de convencer fue el cambio abrupto que tuvo el capitán en esta película, luego de ver lo frío, cruel y despiadado que era en la película anterior con los Na’vi. Aquí, en cambio, lo vemos más emotivo, convaleciente y considerado con los demás, aunque algo me dice que hay un cierto motivo por esto y es por la presencia de su hijo. Considero que dicho detalle igual no me termina de convencer, sobre todo por el lamentable final que nos dan en esta película con respecto a este personaje. O sea, luego de TOOOOOODO lo que ocasionó esta escoria de ser vivo, le dan ese final… ¿por qué, para qué? No entiendo nada, de verdad. Pero bueno, por un lado esto puede ser un poco comprensible si consideramos la cantidad de pérdidas y/o bajas que tuvimos aquí en comparación con la terrible masacre que vimos en el final de la película anterior.
/>\n\n
alt=\
><strong><em></br><s5>Source: <a href=\
>Tenor.\n\n
/></center>\n\n<div class=\
>\n<div class=\

> Also, another point worth mentioning about this film is how slow—or “boring”—the plot became over the course of its three-hour runtime, compared to the previous film. But I think this is mostly because it serves as the first part or the introduction to a much larger story, one that’s spread across several subsequent films. Even so, this makes many scenes or moments in the film feel somewhat long or drawn-out. Don’t get me wrong, though—I was thoroughly entertained, and the scenes and story arcs we see in this film really help us get to know the new characters in this story better, especially Jake and Neytiri’s children. It’s as if, this time, not only would Jake be the protagonist of this story—which, I remind you, isn’t the same as the previous film, but a very different and more extensive one—but rather that his children will play a more prominent role in what will come to pass in the future. Or at least that’s what we come to see throughout this film and in the way each of these characters develops. Especially with Lo'ak and Kiri, who seem to have had the most prominence in this film. Oh, and Spider too, although his role was different in a way that doesn’t quite convince me whether he’s a protagonist or an antagonist.

>
También, esto es otro detalle a mencionar de esta película y es lo lenta o “aburrida” que llegó a ser su trama a lo largo de sus tres horas de duración, en comparación con la película anterior. Pero considero que esto se debe más a que es como la primera parte o la introducción de una historia mucho más grande, pero dividida por varias películas posteriores. Aún así, esto hace que veamos muchas escenas o momentos de la película un tanto largos o sobre-extendidos. Aunque no me malentiendan, me entretuvo bastante y dichas escenas y arcos que vemos en esta película nos ayudan bastante a poder conocer mejor a los nuevos personajes de esta historia, especialmente a los hijos de Jake y Neytiri. Es como si, esta vez, no solo Jake sería el protagonista de esta historia que, les recuerdo, no es la misma que la película anterior, sino una muy diferente y más extensa. Sino más bien que sus hijos tendrán un papel más protagónico en lo que llegará a suceder en un futuro. O al menos eso es lo que llegamos a ver a lo largo de esta película y con la forma en la que se desarrollan a cada uno de estos personajes. Sobre todo con Lo'ak y Kiri, quienes parecen ser los que más protagonismo tuvieron en esta película. Ah, y el Spider también, aunque lo tuvo de otra forma que no me termina de convencer si es protagónico o antagónico.
/>\n\n
alt=\
><strong><em></br><s5>Source: <a href=\
>Tenor.\n\n
/></center>\n\n<div class=\
>\n<div class=\

> Another thing I didn't really like about this great Avatar sequel is the role Jake was given throughout the film. After all the heroic deeds he performed back then—and especially given how well he knows his own kind—our protagonist decides to flee with his family right from the start, abandoning the clan where they grew up, all out of fear. I understand that here he took on a more paternal and protective role toward his family, and that the fear of losing them in the war motivated him even more to make that decision. But after everything they go through in this movie, it’s clear that it wasn’t one of the best decisions he’s ever made—and that’s saying something, considering he’s made plenty of bad decisions in the past. Still, what happened happened; they gave us that tragic, sad, painful, and discouraging ending that I didn’t like at all. But that doesn’t mean I’d call this movie trash, especially given the spectacular audiovisual work it features. I mean, the main reason it took over a decade to release this second installment of the saga is due to the technical work involved with the computer-generated visual effects, the motion capture, and their functionality and visual quality in environments with a lot of water, since a large part of the movie takes place in the sea, both on the surface and underwater as well.

>
Otra cosa que no me gustó mucho de esta gran secuela de Avatar es el papel que le dieron a Jake a lo largo de la película. Luego de todas las hazañas que hizo en su momento y más al conocer tan bien a su propia especie, nuestro protagonista decide huir con su familia antes que nada al principio, abandonando el clan donde crecieron y todo por miedo. Entiendo que aquí asumió más un papel más paterno y protector para con su familia, además de que el temor de perderlos en la guerra lo motivó más a tomar dicha decisión. Pero luego de todo lo que viven en esta película, es evidente que no fue de las mejores decisiones que ha tomado y eso que tomó muchas malas decisiones en su pasado. Aún así, pasó lo que pasó, nos dieron ese final todo trágico, triste, doloroso y desalentador que no me gustó para nada. Pero no por eso lo calificaría como una basura a esta película, mucho menos al ver el trabajo súper espectacular que tiene a nivel audiovisual. O sea, la razón principal por la que duraron más de una década para sacar esta segunda entrega de la saga es debido al trabajo técnico con lo que respecta a los efectos visuales hechos por computadora, las capturas de movimiento, su función y calidad visual en ambientes con bastante agua, ya que gran parte de la película ocurre es en el mar, tanto encima como en el fondo también.
/>\n\n
alt=\
><strong><em></br><s5>Source: <a href=\
>Tenor.\n\n
/></center>\n\n<div class=\
>\n<div class=\

> And they certainly did a spectacular job, as you can see how they maintain those details, fluidity, realism, and contrast with the various blue characters we see in the film and how they look in the water. The way they blend these scenes with light and shadow, the composition of each scene, and the way they transition from being on the surface to being in the sea in different ways, with various shots and angles, is spectacular. Another thing I really liked is the character design, especially that of the Na’vi from the Metkayina clan, who are the ones living on the reef, in the sea. Their design is noticeably different from that of the Omaticaya clan, as they are a more greenish blue, their arms are thicker with a fin-like shape on one side, and their tails are more than twice as thick. I liked this because, unlike what we saw at the end of the previous film, we see a distinction between the Na’vi races and clans (which in turn allows us to notice certain differences between their cultures and customs). Another thing that fascinated me was the design of the various sea creatures, especially the ones called Tulkun, which resemble whales.

>
Y vaya que hicieron un trabajo espectacular ya que se puede notar cómo mantienen dichos detalles, fluidez, realismo y contraste con los diferentes personajes azules que vemos en la película y cómo se ven en el agua. La forma en la que mezclan estás escenas con luces, sombras, la composición de cada escena, la forma en la que pasan de verse en la superficie y justo luego en el mar de distintas maneras, planos y formas es espectacular. Otra cosa que me gustó mucho es el diseño de los personajes, sobre todo de los Na'vi del clan Metkayina, quienes son los que viven en el arrecife, en el mar. Su diseño es notablemente distinto al del clan Omaticaya ya que son de un azul más verdoso, sus brazos son más gruesos con una forma de aleta entre un costado y sus colas son más del doble de gruesas. Me gustó esto ya que, a diferencia de lo que notamos al final de la película anterior, vemos una distinción entre las razas y los clanes de los Na'vi (lo cual a su vez podemos notar también ciertas diferencias entre sus culturas y costumbres). Otra cosa que me fascinó también es el diseño de las distintas criaturas marinas, sobre todo de unas llamadas Tulkun que tienen un parecido a las ballenas.
/>\n\n
alt=\
><strong><em></br><s5>Source: <a href=\
>Tenor.\n\n
/></center>\n\n<div class=\
>\n<div class=\

> I was also fascinated by how James Cameron showcases different cinematographic styles, camera work, and shots in this film. And not only that, but he uses various styles of camera movement, transitions, and visual effects to capture the viewer’s attention. The sound effects are also excellent, especially when bringing Pandora’s vast ocean to life. But what fascinated me most of all is the film’s soundtrack. I don’t know who was in charge of it, but what a spectacular job they did with that soundtrack. It was an audiovisual marvel to watch the entire film with that soundtrack, especially at the end. And speaking of the ending, I’m not going to say I liked it entirely, since I mentioned above that I didn’t. I’ll just say that when it comes to chase sequences, action, combat, destruction, and explosions, this movie is an absolute audiovisual marvel. Although, of course, it doesn’t compare to its predecessor due to the incredibly high standard that one set, naturally. Perhaps it’s because of that lack of spectacular explosions and destruction we saw in the first movie that I felt this second installment was a bit “milder” in terms of action. But still, that ending ultimately won me over in part because, as I told you, it’s just the beginning of something bigger.
Personally, I give it a rating of 9.5/10 in terms of the science fiction, action, and drama genres.

>
Me fascinó también cómo James Cameron se luce con los distintos estilos de fotografía, uso de cámaras y planos en esta película. Y no solo eso, sino que utiliza distintos estilos de movimientos, transiciones y efectos visuales para llamar la atención del espectador. Los efectos de sonido también son excelentes, sobre todo al momento de darle vida al enorme océano de Pandora. Pero lo que más me llegó a fascinar de todo esto es también la banda sonora que tiene esta película. No sé quién estuvo a cargo, pero vaya trabajo tan espectacular el que hizo con dicha banda sonora. Una maravilla audiovisual fue ver toda esta película con dicha banda sonora, sobre todo al final. Y hablando de su final, no voy a decir que me gustó del todo ya que mencioné arriba que no es así. Solo diré que en lo que respecta a secuencias de persecuciones, acción, combates, destrucción y explosiones es una completa maravilla audiovisual esta película. Aunque, claro, no se le compara con su antecesora debido al altísimo nivel que esta tiene, claro está. Tal vez y es debido a esa falta de explosiones espectaculares y destrucción que vimos en la primera película que sentí esta segunda entrega como algo un poco más “suave” en cuanto a acción se refiere. Pero igual, me terminó de convencer en parte dicho final ya que, como les dije, es solo el inicio de algo más grande.
Personalmente, le doy una calificación de 9.5/10 en lo que respecta al género de ciencia ficción, acción y drama.

description.title: El valor de un abrazo a tiempo: Por qué celebrar la vida (y a mamá) mientras estamos aquí. [Esp/Eng]
description.body: \n\n<div class=\

>

***
***

A veces la rutina nos hace vivir en automático. Guardamos los \

, postergamos las visitas y asumimos que la gente que amamos siempre va a estar ahí, sentada a la mesa, esperando nuestro tiempo libre. Pero la vida se pasa en un parpadeo, y la verdadera sabiduría no está en recordar con nostalgia a los que ya se fueron, sino en amar con intensidad a los que caminan hoy a nuestro lado.

>Sometimes routine causes us to go through life on autopilot. We hold back our “I love yous,” put off visits, and assume that the people we love will always be there, sitting at the table, waiting for us to find the time. But life passes in the blink of an eye, and true wisdom lies not in nostalgically remembering those who are gone, but in loving deeply those who walk beside us today.


![1001230114.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/lorennys/EpA25s8eBk26Vhq6yn16xmrE59todPTjFpjZKqCb3aCau8NENkBoNZRtCV5tKspZ9EY.jpg)



Celebrar la vida no es solo soplar las velas de una torta una vez al año; es una postura ante el día a día. Es decidir, conscientemente, dar ese abrazo apretado hoy, decir \

hoy y demostrar cuánto nos importa alguien mientras podemos mirar a esa persona a los ojos. >Celebrating life isn't just about blowing out the candles on a cake once a year; it's an attitude toward everyday life. It's about consciously choosing to give that tight hug today, to say “thank you” today, and to show someone how much they mean to us while we can still look them in the eye. ![1001230105.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/lorennys/EoGwzvwmfiCS9Yfsb4DNECwGr328DNCaKvfJKbCEmM9Z2KsRaHnZssE1rPy1nj7uT7q.jpg) El milagro de celebrar a mamá Si celebrar la vida de cualquiera que amamos ya es un regalo, festejar el cumpleaños de mamá es tocar las fibras más profundas de nuestra existencia. >The Miracle of Celebrating Mom If celebrating the life of anyone we love is already a gift, celebrating Mom’s birthday touches the deepest fibers of our being. ![1001230115.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/lorennys/Ep5kEJvk9Tx7EUFLypHnR6jXJXUzvAMV2kqEJa3PEc3Jk1AV9om6GxVVxcRx39ZcLw4.jpg) Pensémoslo un segundo: ella es el origen. Nos amó desde antes de conocernos, cuando éramos solo una promesa, y ha puesto su corazón en cada paso que damos. Celebrar su cumpleaños no es solo festejar que cumple un año más; es agradecer el tiempo, los desvelos, los consejos y ese amor incondicional que no pide nada a cambio. >Let’s think about it for a second: she is the source. She loved us even before we met, when we were just a promise, and she has poured her heart into every step we take. Celebrating her birthday isn’t just about marking another year; it’s about giving thanks for her time, her sleepless nights, her advice, and that unconditional love that asks for nothing in return. ![1001230112.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/lorennys/EpGPHDmcDeZ2gfzAPDFCtUVjrSPAsuoca5kF1JP9KN2EVjrYd8gL9igQvN6yqo816i3.jpg) No esperemos al último abrazo. No dejemos las palabras más bonitas para cuando el silencio sea el que responda. El momento de hacerle saber que su vida es nuestra mayor bendición es ahora, con la torta en la mesa, las risas de fondo y la fortuna de tenerla cerca. >Let’s not wait until the final embrace. Let’s not save our kindest words for when silence is the only answer. The time to let her know that her life is our greatest blessing is now—with the cake on the table, laughter in the background, and the good fortune of having her close by. ![1001230107.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/lorennys/EpQuGor5tScdYuNPd22RNABNus6h94v5tyA9vEJKRZTyQvBavAWTfP1YbDUVkZoE2Re.jpg) La vida es un ratito. Una aventura maravillosa, frágil y hermosa. Hoy los invito a no guardarse nada: llamen a esa persona en la que pensaron mientras leían esto, den ese abrazo pendiente y, si tienen la dicha de tener a mamá celebrando un año más, abrácenla con el alma. Demostremos el amor en vida, que es donde verdaderamente florece. >Life is fleeting. It’s a wonderful, fragile, and beautiful adventure. Today, I invite you to hold nothing back: call that person you were thinking of while reading this, give that long-overdue hug, and, if you’re lucky enough to have your mom with you to celebrate another year, embrace her with all your heart. Let’s show our love while we’re alive, because that’s where it truly blossoms. description.title: Day 2884 | Thai Boxing, Laundry Day, & Playing Pool
description.body:
https://images.hive.blog/DQmbZ4zXEYnL1m3jixHA8vtxF39vdYGxvU3Kt5i7a6KDRjP/Screenshot%202026-06-09%2007.51.34.png
I started a challenge of taking 100 days off to mainly focus on my health and overall personal development and used this account as a personal blog to keep track of all my activity. I enjoyed it and continued afterward trying to build better habits and find a good balance between health, fitness, work, entertainment, and my personal life...

On Monday, I started back with a Muay Thai Boxing Class which went quite well and I'm enjoying getting a workout each morning with a break on Sunday. Afterward, I chilled a bit in my room watching the latest From episode. I also went out to get my Laundry done and around 17:00, I went on my own to a local restaurant where I ate a Panang with Rice and Chicken which was super delicious. I also asked to play some pool and managed to play my first couple of games here with the owner of the restaurant which was an old lady named Nan.

I didn't do all too much in the evening aside from installing Thai Cupid with an eye to meet some more people even though it feels like that mostly is for women who are searching for a much older man to start a relationship with as the age range of most goes well into the 60s. So this is not really for me and I will move on trying out Tinder next. I also had a small craving for sweets and chips so I headed out to one of the Seven Elevens nearby to get something. I also have been texting a lot to friends and family. Next Day Goals: So I plan another Thai Boxing Class to start the day. It's been a couple days since I went out swimming so I will also do that. Aside from this, I will see where the day takes me.

**Basic Procedure:**
• Outline or sketch your painting reference.
• Paint using a lighter background shade by creating a beautiful texture. 
• On the middle ground, paint the first layer of the subject. 
• The same procedure as the foreground. 
• Once the first layer is completely dry, you can proceed to paint with a darker shade of coffee.
• Then add details to bring your painting to life. I used a liner brush for the thin details. 

**Take note:** In putting details, you cannot have sharp lines and shapes unless it is completely dry.

description.title: A strangely colored insect on the canvas of nature.
description.body: <div class=\

> ![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmcWrhHc7VD2rF1ct6gS8mMWYacR681NLVYxAJqttceaus/1780965972432.jpg) Every creation of nature is like a living work of art. We see hundreds of insects around us every day, but rarely do we get the opportunity to observe them in depth. Today I present to you a picture of such a wonderful insect. The insect you see is basically a shield bug, a stink bug, belonging to the Hemiptera order. In Bengali, many people also call it a shield bug. The first thing that catches the eye when looking at the picture is the beautiful reddish or pink hue of its skin. The contrast of this bright color against the background of green leaves highlights a unique beauty of nature. Their body structure looks a lot like a warrior's shield, which is why they are named shield bugs. ![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmQ55DvCkfgwdasdfc2dCw24AdNaBbursVv164w6QwUVSB/1780965972497.jpg) There's a reason they're called stink bugs Whenever they feel threatened or disturbed, they release a foul-smelling liquid from their bodies. This smell helps to keep predators away. Most shield bugs are herbivores. They survive by sucking the sap from young leaves, stems, or fruits of plants. In the picture, one is sitting on a green leaf and sucking the sap. They are seen to be eating or resting. Depending on the species, their color can be green, brown, gray, or even bright red. This bright color is often used to warn enemies. These tiny creatures around us are a very important part of the ecosystem. They can help pollinate some plants and also serve as food for other larger insects or birds. Macro photography, like this one, teaches us how much of an extraordinary world can be hidden on even an ordinary leaf if we look closely.

description.title: Yellow Lady's Slipper in the Black Hills
description.body:
![cb6427ed-e4f6-40b5-b924-849ab7a7d9b6-1_all_103534.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/ultratrain/23vsDsXAyQz7KuBHqBKQLKXX1Gnancv37zkq6RbCUrXHbvM9uapYhgLva1XbX2xQuSQLJ.jpg)
I spotted this dainty little beauty while hiking along the trail in Spearfish Canyon. 
The **Yellow Lady's Slipper** (*Cypripedium parviflorum*) is a rather rare terrestrial orchid here in South Dakota but fortunately the environment in Spearfish Canyon is ideal for them. Plenty of moist, humus-rich soil that has plenty of limestone to maintain a \

pH as well as plenty of overhead forest canopy to provide a protective shaded space.
![cb6427ed-e4f6-40b5-b924-849ab7a7d9b6-1_all_103541.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/ultratrain/23vhsaAc3rwEsWcxHPmr8cAUR2TMN6NzTb9WYhRadHSDkm7VZCZB7TndXYqfvBVfjyD7y.jpg)
This species remains rare and are considered an endangered population and thus are legally protected from collecting. 
These orchids survive by utilizing a symbiotic relationship with particular soil fungi and transplants will mostly die or certainly not germinate if moved.
So I took only photos and hopefully this one little beauty will flourand spread.  
![cb6427ed-e4f6-40b5-b924-849ab7a7d9b6-1_all_103539.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/ultratrain/23vsEFo1FiavsA7bS61hooSGJAKritPzmRpnZUqGfCyJPW8htJrUdJQMc2ymvXFzd6dmr.jpg)

description.body:
Eng 🇬🇧 
GATE: When Modern Technology Faces a Fantasy World

![IMG_20260608_204558.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/valderalazaro/23w2q3odeSQ7C4qq4F2BH7hP5vvvUnkz1JZfg772orSScXRijAdG1LKhrGgffEJXa9QEy.jpg)

What would happen if a portal connected our world to a kingdom of dragons, magic, and medieval armies? Could fantasy withstand the power of modern technology? That is the fascinating premise of Gate, a work that combines military action, epic fantasy, and political conflicts into a story that is as entertaining as it is thought-provoking.

The Day the Gate Opened

The story begins in Tokyo, when a gigantic gate suddenly appears in the Ginza district. From it emerges an army belonging to a Roman-style medieval empire that attacks the civilian population. Knights, archers, and fantastical creatures invade a modern city without understanding the technological gap between the two worlds.

The attack causes numerous casualties, but the Japan Self-Defense Forces quickly respond and manage to repel the invasion. After securing the area, the Japanese government decides to cross the mysterious gate to investigate what lies beyond and prevent future attacks.

Thus begins an expedition that will forever change the relationship between two completely different worlds.

An Unconventional Protagonist

![IMG_20260608_204522.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/valderalazaro/23xp4d1R714YFQXiDMHWzUV8zKyCkNjFWY5m4ZKTkh1pRBzrdSLv4NGW1CrtSvjyB3dPw.jpg)

The main character is Yoji Itami, an officer of the Japan Self-Defense Forces who, far from being the typical military hero, is an avid otaku. His relaxed and pragmatic personality contrasts sharply with the seriousness of the situations he faces.

Unlike many protagonists who seek glory or recognition, Itami acts primarily to protect lives and fulfill his duty. This attitude allows him to earn the trust of both his comrades and the inhabitants of the fantasy world.

A Clash of Civilizations

One of the most interesting aspects of the series is the contrast between two completely different levels of development.

On one side is Japan, with helicopters, armored vehicles, satellite communications, modern medicine, and advanced weaponry.

On the other is the Empire, a society built on agriculture, nobility, cavalry, and traditional warfare.

The differences are so vast that many of the early battles seem impossible to balance. Armies that dominated battlefields for centuries discover that their tactics are useless against automatic weapons, artillery, and air support.

However, the series is not limited to combat. It also explores how people from both worlds react when they discover cultures completely different from their own.

More Than a War Story

Although battles are an important part of the plot, Gate dedicates much of its time to developing political and diplomatic relationships.

The leaders of the Empire must decide whether to continue a war they cannot win or attempt negotiations with an unknown power.

Meanwhile, Japan seeks to maintain stability and prevent other nations on Earth from interfering in the newly discovered territory.

This political dimension adds depth to the story, showing that the real struggle does not always take place on the battlefield. Often, it unfolds through meetings, negotiations, and strategic decisions that affect the fate of thousands.

Characters Who Enrich the Adventure

During his journey, Itami meets several important figures from the fantasy world.

Among them is Rory Mercury, a demigoddess warrior known for her incredible power and enigmatic personality.

Also appearing are Tuka Luna Marceau, an elf scarred by the tragedies of war, and Lelei La Lalena, a young mage with an immense intellectual curiosity.

Each character offers a unique perspective on the encounter between the two worlds and helps build a richer narrative that goes beyond military conflict.

Dragons, Magic, and Helicopters

One of Gate’s greatest strengths is the way it combines elements that normally belong to different genres.

You might see a dragon terrorizing an entire region and then watch modern military units develop strategies to defeat it.

The series constantly explores what happens when myths and fantasy collide with science and technology.

This contrast creates spectacular moments that are difficult to find in other works of the genre.

Themes Explored in the Series

Beyond the action, Gate touches on several interesting themes:

- The impact of technological advancement.
- The consequences of war.
- Cultural clashes between societies.
- International diplomacy.
- Adaptation to change.
- The power and responsibility of nations.

Although the series maintains an entertaining tone, it also invites viewers to reflect on how our civilization would react to the discovery of a completely new world.

Why Did It Become So Popular?

Gate’s popularity stems largely from offering something uncommon: a fantasy world where modern technology does not disappear or become replaced by magic. Instead, both coexist and collide.

The series appeals to fans of military action as well as lovers of epic fantasy. Moreover, its premise sparks immediate curiosity: everyone wants to know what would happen if a medieval army had to face a 21st-century military force.

Conclusion

Gate is much more than an anime about soldiers fighting dragons. It is a story about the meeting of two civilizations separated by centuries of development, the challenges that arise when different worlds collide, and the decisions that determine the future of entire peoples.

Its combination of fantasy, military strategy, politics, and adventure makes it a unique work within modern anime. For those who enjoy stories where imagination blends with realistic scenarios, Gate offers an unforgettable experience.

Summary

Gate tells the story of a portal that appears between Japan and a medieval fantasy world. After an initial invasion, the Japan Self-Defense Forces cross the gate and discover a kingdom filled with magic, dragons, and political conflicts. Through intense battles, unexpected alliances, and a profound cultural clash, the series explores what happens when two radically different civilizations come face to face.

Lesson

True power does not always lie in the most advanced weapons, but in the ability to understand, adapt, and build bridges between different cultures. When two worlds meet, cooperation can achieve more than conquest.

And as always, remember that if you know someone who could use a good story and a helping hand, consider sharing with the BBH community 💪, @thebbhfoundation and @thebbhproject,

GATE: Cuando la tecnología moderna se enfrenta a un mundo de fantasía

![IMG_20260608_204535.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/valderalazaro/23ynatvYdVa91AbpZTLN2RyemX11sBWsoQwYsPGPDTHAYiXcb9CMSwe2h8rn8sR8aaXwe.jpg)

¿Qué ocurriría si un portal 
conectara nuestro mundo con un reino de dragones, magia y ejércitos medievales? ¿Sería la fantasía capaz de resistir el poder de la tecnología moderna? Esa es la fascinante premisa de Gate, una obra que mezcla acción militar, fantasía épica y conflictos políticos en una historia tan entretenida como provocadora.
El día que se abrió la Puerta
La historia comienza en Tokio, cuando una gigantesca puerta aparece de la nada en el distrito de Ginza. De ella emerge un ejército perteneciente a un imperio de estilo romano-medieval que ataca a la población civil. Caballeros, arqueros y criaturas fantásticas irrumpen en una ciudad moderna sin comprender la diferencia tecnológica entre ambos mundos.
El ataque provoca numerosas víctimas, pero las Fuerzas de Autodefensa de Japón reaccionan rápidamente y logran contener la invasión. Tras asegurar la zona, el gobierno japonés decide cruzar la misteriosa puerta para investigar qué existe al otro lado y evitar futuros ataques.
Así comienza una expedición que cambiará para siempre la relación entre dos mundos completamente diferentes.
Un protagonista poco convencional
![IMG_20260608_204522.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/valderalazaro/23xp4d1R714YFQXiDMHWzUV8zKyCkNjFWY5m4ZKTkh1pRBzrdSLv4NGW1CrtSvjyB3dPw.jpg)
El personaje principal es Yoji Itami, un oficial de la Fuerza de Autodefensa que, lejos de ser el típico héroe militar, es un apasionado de la cultura otaku. Su personalidad relajada y pragmática contrasta con la gravedad de las situaciones que enfrenta.
A diferencia de muchos protagonistas que buscan gloria o reconocimiento, Itami actúa principalmente para proteger vidas y cumplir con su deber. Esta actitud le permite ganarse la confianza tanto de sus compañeros como de los habitantes del mundo fantástico.
Un choque de civilizaciones
Uno de los aspectos más interesantes de la serie es el contraste entre dos niveles de desarrollo completamente distintos.
Por un lado está Japón, con helicópteros, vehículos blindados, comunicaciones satelitales, medicina moderna y armamento avanzado.
Por el otro se encuentra el Imperio, una sociedad basada en la agricultura, la nobleza, la caballería y la guerra tradicional.
Las diferencias son tan enormes que muchas de las primeras batallas parecen imposibles de equilibrar. Ejércitos enteros que durante siglos dominaron los campos de batalla descubren que sus tácticas son inútiles frente a armas automáticas, artillería y apoyo aéreo.
Sin embargo, la serie no se limita a mostrar combates. También explora cómo reaccionan las personas de ambos mundos al descubrir culturas completamente diferentes.
Más que una historia de guerra
Aunque las batallas son una parte importante de la trama, Gate dedica gran parte de su tiempo a desarrollar relaciones políticas y diplomáticas.
Los líderes del Imperio deben decidir si continúan una guerra que no pueden ganar o si intentan negociar con una potencia desconocida.
Mientras tanto, Japón busca mantener la estabilidad y evitar que otras naciones de la Tierra interfieran en el nuevo territorio.
Esta dimensión política añade profundidad a la historia, mostrando que la verdadera lucha no siempre ocurre en el campo de batalla. Muchas veces se desarrolla en reuniones, negociaciones y decisiones estratégicas que afectan el destino de miles de personas.
Personajes que enriquecen la aventura
Durante su viaje, Itami conoce a varias figuras importantes del mundo fantástico.
Entre ellas destaca Rory Mercury, una semidiosa guerrera conocida por su impresionante poder y su personalidad enigmática.
También aparece Tuka Luna Marceau, una elfa marcada por las tragedias de la guerra, y Lelei La Lalena, una joven maga con una enorme curiosidad intelectual.
Cada una aporta una perspectiva distinta sobre el encuentro entre ambos mundos y ayuda a construir una narrativa más rica que va más allá de los enfrentamientos militares.
Dragones, magia y helicópteros
Uno de los mayores atractivos de Gate es la manera en que combina elementos que normalmente pertenecen a géneros distintos.
Es posible ver una escena donde un dragón aterroriza una región entera y, poco después, observar cómo unidades modernas desarrollan estrategias para enfrentarlo.
La serie juega constantemente con la pregunta de qué sucede cuando los mitos y la fantasía se encuentran con la ciencia y la tecnología.
Este contraste genera momentos espectaculares que difícilmente pueden encontrarse en otras obras del género.
Temas que aborda la serie
Más allá de la acción, Gate toca temas interesantes:
El impacto del avance tecnológico.
Las consecuencias de la guerra.
El choque cultural entre sociedades.
La diplomacia internacional.
La adaptación al cambio.
El poder y la responsabilidad de las naciones.
Aunque la obra mantiene un tono entretenido, también invita a reflexionar sobre cómo reaccionaría nuestra civilización ante el descubrimiento de un mundo completamente nuevo.
¿Por qué se volvió tan popular?
La popularidad de Gate se debe en gran medida a que ofrece algo poco común: una fantasía donde la tecnología moderna no desaparece ni es reemplazada por la magia. En lugar de eso, ambos elementos conviven y se enfrentan.
La serie logra satisfacer tanto a quienes disfrutan de la acción militar como a los aficionados de la fantasía épica. Además, su premisa despierta una curiosidad inmediata: todos queremos saber qué ocurriría si un ejército medieval tuviera que enfrentarse a una fuerza militar del siglo XXI.
Conclusión
Gate es mucho más que un anime sobre soldados luchando contra dragones. Es una historia sobre el encuentro de dos civilizaciones separadas por siglos de desarrollo, sobre los desafíos que surgen cuando mundos diferentes chocan y sobre las decisiones que determinan el futuro de pueblos enteros.
Su combinación de fantasía, estrategia militar, política y aventura la convierte en una obra única dentro del anime moderno. Para quienes disfrutan de historias donde la imaginación se mezcla con escenarios realistas, Gate ofrece una experiencia difícil de olvidar.
Resumen
Gate narra la aparición de un portal entre Japón y un mundo de fantasía medieval. Tras una invasión inicial, las Fuerzas de Autodefensa japonesas cruzan la puerta y descubren un reino lleno de magia, dragones y conflictos políticos. A través de intensas batallas, alianzas inesperadas y un profundo choque cultural, la serie explora qué sucede cuando dos civilizaciones radicalmente distintas se encuentran cara a cara.
Enseñanza
El verdadero poder no siempre reside en las armas más avanzadas, sino en la capacidad de comprender, adaptarse y construir puentes entre culturas diferentes. Cuando dos mundos se encuentran, la cooperación puede lograr más que la conquista.

description.body:
<liketuimages>

![EBCnHPceRA2TkXR0_mmexport1780928962725.webp](https://cdn.liketu.com/media/angelina6688/images/EBCnHPceRA2TkXR0_mmexport1780928962725/EBCnHPceRA2TkXR0_mmexport1780928962725.webp)
![krDztDNnLmKFnSUP_mmexport1780928957915.webp](https://cdn.liketu.com/media/angelina6688/images/krDztDNnLmKFnSUP_mmexport1780928957915/krDztDNnLmKFnSUP_mmexport1780928957915.webp)
![FjKEtvA0eF5ULFRi_Screenshot_20260608_222954_com_tencent_mm_LauncherUI.webp](https://cdn.liketu.com/media/angelina6688/images/FjKEtvA0eF5ULFRi_Screenshot_20260608_222954_com_tencent_mm_LauncherUI/FjKEtvA0eF5ULFRi_Screenshot_20260608_222954_com_tencent_mm_LauncherUI.webp)
</center>
</liketuimages>

武汉这两天气温真的特别诡异，上周一直都是三十多度的高温。本来天天都是纯短袖、家家户户开空调的盛夏模式，结果从星期天开始，连着周一到今天，气温陡然骤降，最低直接跌到十几度。
 
六月份本该燥热闷热，没想到天气完全反常态，硬生生把收起来的长袖外套又翻了出来。
 
不过突如其来的降温也格外舒服，彻底告别了燥热难耐的酷暑。晚上睡觉不用开空调，开窗通风晚风徐徐，只需要盖一层薄薄的毯子，凉爽又惬意，居然莫名有了秋天的感觉。
 
但昨天晚上发生了一个小小的突发插曲，还挺让人猝不及防。大概晚上九点半，我刚洗完澡从卫生间出来，眼前突然一黑，瞬间吓了一跳，家里人也轻呼了一声，孩子更是大喊了一声停电了。
 
我当场懵了几秒，第一反应就是无比庆幸，还好不是洗澡洗到一半突然停电，不然黑灯瞎火的，真的会尴尬到极致。
 
一开始我以为只是家里跳闸了，前两年盛夏高温，家里三台空调同时开启，曾经烧坏保险丝跳过一次闸，修好后就再也没出过问题。老公出门查看后才发现，不仅我们整层四户全部断电，翻看小区群消息，半个小区都停了电。不止我们小区，周边好几个小区、湖边大半公共路灯也都断电了，听说是片区大型配电房出现故障跳闸。
 
当时群里瞬间热闹起来，大家纷纷吐槽抱怨。当天正是湖北高考第二天，本省高考要持续三天，小区里有不少正在参加高考的孩子，还有初高中孩子的作业还没写完。居民们纷纷咨询抢修时间、联系相关部门。

好在这次抢修速度特别快，从停电到维修人员到场抢修，只用了短短一小时，十一点不到就顺利来电了，也是近几年很少遇到的突发停电情况。

---

description.title: Kercy of OakMoor (a Short Story) - Part 2: The Manifestation of Old World  - Transforming Evil Spirits Into Steam | Mixed Media Project
description.body: <center>![Apophysis-Kercy-Part2.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/justclickindiva/48GhSvYJzeMPaACdvMPCcrmPJXFWm4REx9eRjC3kZN57fzjEdKqgD6JgnyugfsDrzM.jpg)</center>\n\n<div class=\

>

The gavel was Judge Bixby's only weapon against the chaos that had erupted in his makeshift court. Almost shattering the sounding block, he struck until only whimpers were noticeable. His voice rose not to quiet the crowd, but to admonish Axel. 

\

Jonas Krebb sat until his assistant whispered in ear. He rose immediately. 

\

Judge Bixby bristled, but he understood the solicitor perfectly. He'd no choice but to allow the unscheduled witness.

The town hall was suffocating, packed with angry townspeople and the heavy stench of fear and damp wool. Weary, Jonas wiped sweat from his brow as he stood next to Kercy who sat at the wooden defense table, her wrists raw by heavy iron shackles.

At the center of the room, standing before the elevated bench of the town elders, was a small brass-and-iron boiler seized as evidence of dark magic from Kercy's barn.

\
Jonas announced, his voice echoing off the timber beams. Master Machinist Thaddeus Ironwood, of Old World.\
I swear to tell the truth here today against all odds and at great peril to my self and young Kercy over there,\

Look at you all cowering in the dark. Praying to the dirt. Do you think I don't know the names of OakMoor? Your grandfathers sat at my workbenches! Your grandmothers calculated fluid dynamics before they could even weave wool! To put it bluntly, they were masters where you who sit here today are minions and cowards.\

Two generations ago, your people left Old World with a vision of building a peaceful life in this valley. Why they chose to abandon the clarity of reason and return to the ancient ways of ignorance is utterly beyond me!\
They mistook peace for stagnation. They forgot the math. They forgot the science. And now look at you...broken and on the brink of starvation, terrified of a pot of boiling water!\
But that evil magic cauldron screamed, old man!\
It moved without a hand to touch it!\
It moves because of the universe's law, you absolute fools! \

*

At that point, Kercy let escape a weak smile as she glanced at her former Master, recalling her initial confusion. 

\

<center>![rinreMr4T-dividerline-Resized.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/justclickindiva/23tv8hvCs9XJ6jvySDHoq8PqyG4YaAkLbtNT5rMVejff3KMvBDdAtpvqbHwZFE1k5MRdW.png)</center>

I knew Master Ironwood as no other did in OakMoor. He was a brilliant visionary of Old World, whose workshop smelled of iron and ozone. He taught me that \

was just science that we have yet to understand. He taught me the unforgiving laws of thermodynamics, which is the movement of heat, fluid mechanics, and steam power. <sup>1</sup>

Master Ironwood possessed a deep understanding of how hidden forces could be manipulated to do the work of a hundred men. He didn't just teach me how to forge and weld; he taught me the knowledge behind the machines.

He showed me how heat is never truly lost, but transformed, and how the rapid expansion of water into steam builds invisible, tremendous force within enclosed vessels.

He demonstrated how a fire, fed by simple wood or coal, could boil water within a sealed iron boiler. Under intense heat, he explained, water expands into steam at a ratio of over 1,600 - 1,700 to 1, creating a massive, invisible buildup of pressure (psi). <sup>2</sup>

He taught me to calculate the precise psi needed to drive heavy iron pistons and turn massive mill gears, translating raw heat into controlled, rhythmic power. <sup>3</sup>

He taught me to read pressure gauges, tune safety valves, and use the \

of expanding steam and magnetism to coax heavy metal into movement.

He showed me how to direct that high-pressure steam through narrow valves into a heavy cylinder. The expanding vapor forces a metal piston forward. By connecting this moving piston to a crankshaft, the linear thrust of hot air is converted into continuous, tireless rotational energy. <sup>4</sup>

I would stare at the miniature iron boiler on Master Ironwood’s workbench. My hands were blistered. My mind was weary from weeks of advanced mathematics.

But I was knowledgeable. And happy. And in the end, he showed me that moving metal wasn't sorcery; it was simply the masterful harnessing of energy, pressure, and invisible vapors.

When my apprenticeship ended, I realized the pot of boiling water could change the course of OakMoor.

But none of my knowledge could help me now if Master Ironwood couldn't convince the townspeople of OakMoor that the machine he helped me build was not an evil contraption that housed spirits sent by the devil to destroy, but simply a tool emitting steam to assist in milling the sorely needed grain.

*[to be continued]*

<sup>[Source 1: Thermodynamics](https://simple.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thermodynamics)</sup>
<sup>[Source 2: Steam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steam)</sup>
<sup>[Source 3: How to Calculate psi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pound_per_square_inch)</sup>
<sup>[Source 4: How A Steam Engine Works](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steam_engine)</sup>

![262866.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/justclickindiva/23swXV8TTdSfCAMefZgEG2MHmtqq9ibT4QeFL1viVbJRuMz1ESKLDzDm4NkSDENoFbtBM.png)

For Part 2 of my mixed media project and story, I wanted a different design to reflect the iron beast that Kercy returned home with. With the help of the master machinist, Kercy learned the mechanics of steam and how it's used in machinery. The design I created in StarryAI, the stable diffusion program, reflects the two at work in the master's forge shop in Old World. I love how the image portrays an intense conversation and attentiveness on the part of Kercy, as the apprentice. Quite unusual for a female during that era.

I utilized the description in my story of how Ironwood looked to create the project's design. Since the theme of the story is a forging shop, I wanted the background to reflect various tools of the trade. Finally, I included one of my pure fractal veils to cover the entire image. I feel as though it gave the scene an old world look of a forge shop.

**Style**: Cyberpunk Nouveau 

Also, for the story, I wanted to continue with the trial in which Master Ironwood is called as a witness. I utilized Canva, my design program, to blend the different type images. I began with a blank, white canvas, then added layers of elements.

This is a flower and a very beautiful white flower in the natural environment. Flowers always have beauty and people enjoy this beauty. Today I am sharing a flower that I have seen with my own eyes and I found it very beautiful. A beautiful name for this beautiful flower is False daisy flower. It is a weed-like fruit and a wonderful beauty of nature. When I saw this flower, I enjoyed its external beauty and because I liked it, I took a few pictures with my own mobile. Each picture is presented for all friends to see.






I saw this beautiful flower a few days ago in my village house. When I was taking some pictures in the field south of my house during the day, I saw this weed-like flower blooming. I observed the flower in various ways and saw that it was a round-shaped flower and had thin petals all around, which made the flower look very beautiful. This flower has no fragrance but has natural beauty. Flowers always give beauty to people and enjoying the beauty of flowers can brighten the mind of any person. Flowers are worshipers of beauty and I have enjoyed the beauty of this flower myself. I have now shared some of the pictures I took with my Hive community friends because I liked them. Yes, nature sometimes gives us such wonderful gifts that are eye-catching. Just like that, a wonderful and rare sight has emerged in the attached photo. It is a green-colored flower that is bound to capture the heart of any flower lover due to its unique color. We are usually used to seeing red or bright colored flowers. However, this green color is like a secret and peaceful form of nature. The picture shows numerous small flower buds coming together to form a beautiful spherical bouquet. The light green and slightly teal color of the buds gives the whole flower a fresh and vibrant look. The light green color of this flower stands out against the dark green leaves in the background. It created a wonderful contrast that made the flower even more attractive. ![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmTWvSN8wztx6WqSuHrRzn4iW3krFt3Na17DWkLQiKzjMj/1780965150917.jpg) The color green has always been a symbol of freshness and new beginnings. This flower is a manifestation of the endless vitality of nature. The main characteristic of the Rangan flower is its clustered form. Many small flowers bloom together in a beautiful geometric pattern on a single stem. This is beautifully illustrated in the picture. When we think of flowers, bright colors like red, blue, or yellow come to mind. There, this green color gives a kind of mental peace. This strange and beautiful creation of nature reminds us that beauty has no specific boundaries or colors. json_metadata.title: A great night of sleep
json_metadata.body: Good Morning to all my wonderful friends.. How are you? My wife and I spent three nights in Bintulu, and we stayed at three different hotels. One of our quests in Bintulu is to stay at almost all the hotels here to see what they are like. This is the view of Bintulu at night. It is a beautiful city and a lot of the city is quite clean. It is quite quiet at night which is a great destination for a short trip.
/> This is the washroom, and it is reasonably clean. Satisfactory. The water that comes out of the shower flows strongly.
/> Two towels as a standard. The toilet is clean.

/> The room. This is a twin bed room. Quite spacious and the price here is quite affordable, but one thing I did not feel comfortable with is the mirror at the top of the bed. Imagine waking up in the middle of the night and suddenly looking at the mirror.

/> The room is quite brightly lit, and I checked around the room, and it looks quite clean and tidy. They did a good job cleaning this room before I came in. I have been to lots of hotels and this hotel is reasonable.

/> I usually bring my multi-port charger to charge a lot of the devices that I own. After a good night of sleep, it was morning again. Time to get some food. Breakfast is served. One bowl for my wife and one bowl that is mine. Herbal soup noodles. This soup is the highlight of this dish where you get to slowly enjoy the taste of the soup.
/> I ordered a bowl of fried noodles with a fried egg at the top but it is slightly in the saltier side of things. Too much soy sauce.
/> Thank you very much for reading my post. @luueetang YouTube: www.youtube.com/luueejanice Tiktok: www.tiktok.com/@luueejanice

“So, then, if that's how a mosaic works – hey, Velma!”

Six-year-old Grayson Ludlow was rarely loud, and was the least likely Ludlow to go running across the yard for another child, but he was very much attached to eleven-year-old Velma, nine-year-old Milton, and eight-year-old Gracie Trent, each for different reasons.

Velma and he connected around art and architecture.

“Hey, Gray – what's happening?” Velma said as she came off her back porch.

“I need to borrow a favorite painting of yours with lots of red, blue, green, or yellow in it – I think I can make a mosaic out of it.”

“Well, OK, let's go find some paintings,” Velma said. “Are we doing this with Legos?”

“Yes, because stuff clicks right in, and all I gotta do is get the platforms to hold together so we can prop them up on the wall like a mosaic would be on the wall. I'd make a floor, but stepping on Legos is not what people like.”

“Nope,” Velma said.

“Oh, this is going to be some content!” Velma's nine-year-old first cousin Vertran Stepforth said as he went to get his camera.

“Actually, Grayson, I have a better idea – bring me the Legos you want to use, and I'll do a color-matched painting so it will be easier for you,” Velma said.

“OK,” Grayson said, and ran home and filled his little red wagon up with Legos to bring back to Velma.

“Well, we can watch those three and know where they are going to be for a few hours,” Velma's mother Mrs. Melissa Trent said.

“Yep,” Grayson's grandmother Mrs. Thalia Ludlow said. “Grayson entertains himself all the time, and that connects with your more self-contained set, Melissa.”

“And this is good because Milton will be coming out of being grounded in two hours,” Mrs. Trent said.

“Let me go find out where George is so we can contain the upcoming celebration,” Mrs. Ludlow said as Mrs. Trent chuckled.

“My oldest daughter said to my oldest son,” Mrs. Trent said, “'If we gambled, we could run a heck of a betting pool on how long it will take George and Milton will get grounded again.'”

“Easy money,” Mrs. Ludlow said, with a laugh. “Never bet against George or Milton coming through, expeditiously – poor babies!”
