links.title: Theradome LH40 Review: Why I Picked This Laser Helmet for Thinning Hair
links.body:
](https://images.hive.blog/DQmXN8ZqMxtJKa7X2busb2KYjMMnjfZ8Ek2zT9K5xSPsPuK/theradome-lh40-laser-helmet-before-after-thinning-hair-results.jpg.png)

Theradome LH40 Review: Why I Picked This Laser Helmet for Thinning Hair

Disclosure: This post contains affiliate links. If you buy through my link, I may earn a commission at no extra cost to you. As an Amazon Associate I earn from qualifying purchases.

I have been dealing with thinning hair for a long time, and I have tried a lot of things that looked good online but did not really move the needle for me.

The biggest lesson I learned is simple:

Not every red light hair-growth device is the same.

Some products look high-tech, but when you start reading the details, they may not be using the kind of laser light I was actually looking for. That is why I became much more careful about choosing a device. I did not want the cheapest thing I could find. I wanted something that made sense, had real laser technology, and was realistic enough for me to keep using.

That is why I ended up liking the Theradome EVO LH40 Laser Helmet.

Why I Started Looking at Laser Helmets for Hair Loss

For me, thinning hair was not one dramatic moment. It was more like slowly noticing more scalp in photos, especially under bright light.

The crown area is where I noticed it the most. In normal bathroom lighting, I could convince myself it was fine. But in overhead lighting or camera flash, it was much more obvious.

That is what pushed me to take hair loss more seriously.

I already knew consistency mattered. The problem was that a lot of hair-growth routines are annoying. If something is messy, painful, complicated, or takes too much effort, I probably will not stick with it long term.

A laser helmet made sense to me because it is simple. You put it on, let it run, and keep going with your day.

Why I Chose the Theradome LH40 Instead of the More Expensive Model

Theradome has a more expensive model, the LH80, but I personally liked the LH40 because it felt like the better value for me.

The LH40 has fewer lasers than the higher-priced model, so the usage schedule is different. The LH40 is generally used more often, while the higher-priced model is designed for fewer weekly sessions.

That tradeoff actually made sense to me.

I would rather buy the more affordable model and use it consistently than spend around $1,000 on the bigger model just because it sounds stronger.

For me, the LH40 hit the right middle ground:

  • It is not the cheapest random helmet online.
  • It is not the most expensive model either.
  • It still uses real laser technology.
  • And I can actually see myself sticking with the routine.

That last part matters. A hair-growth device only helps if you actually use it.

The Big Thing I Looked For: Real Lasers, Not Just a Cheap Light Device

When I started researching hair-growth helmets, I realized a lot of products get lumped together under “red light therapy.”

That can be confusing.

Some devices use lasers. Some use LEDs. Some use a mix. Some product pages make it hard to know what you are really buying.

I wanted a device that was clear about using lasers, because that was the whole reason I was buying it.

That is one of the main reasons I liked the Theradome LH40. Theradome positions the LH40 as a laser phototherapy helmet, not just a generic red light cap.

For hair loss, I do not want something that only looks impressive in photos. I want the technology inside the helmet to make sense.

My Before and After Thoughts

The photo above is why I feel comfortable talking about this.

My “before” photo showed more visible scalp at the crown. That is the kind of photo most people hate taking, but it is also the kind of photo that tells the truth.

In the “after” photo, the crown looks much better covered. The hair looks fuller, darker, and healthier in that same general area.

Now, I want to be careful here.

Hair photos can change depending on lighting, angle, hair length, styling, and whether the hair is wet or dry. I am not saying every person will get the exact same result. I am also not saying one product is a miracle cure.

What I am saying is this:

For me, the Theradome LH40 became one of the few hair-loss tools I actually felt was worth staying consistent with.

Who I Think the Theradome LH40 Makes Sense For

I think the LH40 makes the most sense for someone who is starting to notice thinning hair and wants to do something proactive before it gets worse.

It may be a good fit if:

  • You are seeing more scalp at the crown.
  • You want something easy to use at home.
  • You do not want a messy treatment.
  • You want a device with real laser technology.
  • You are willing to be consistent for months, not days.
  • You want a lower-cost option than the more expensive Theradome model.

This is not something I would buy if I expected overnight results.

Hair grows slowly. That means any serious hair-growth routine has to be judged over months.

What I Like About the LH40

The biggest thing I like is that it is easy to use.

That sounds basic, but it matters.

You do not have to apply anything. You do not have to wash anything out. You do not have to stand in front of a mirror. You just put the helmet on and let the session run.

I also like that the LH40 is the more affordable Theradome option. I do not mind using it more often if it saves money compared with the higher-priced model.

For me, that is the real value story:

Use the LH40 more often and get access to the same type of Theradome laser helmet technology without paying for the top model.

What I Would Watch Out For Before Buying Any Hair-Growth Helmet

Before buying any red light or laser helmet, I would check a few things.

First, I would look at whether it uses lasers, LEDs, or both.

Second, I would check how often you are supposed to use it. A cheaper device is not a good deal if the routine is confusing or unrealistic.

Third, I would look at the company behind the product. With hair loss, I would rather buy from a company that specializes in the category than from a random brand selling hundreds of unrelated gadgets.

Fourth, I would be honest about my stage of hair loss. If someone has advanced hair loss with very little hair left in an area, a helmet may not be the right expectation. These devices make more sense when you are trying to improve thinning hair and support the hair you still have.

My Bottom Line

The Theradome LH40 is the laser helmet I would pick again because it gives me the balance I wanted.

  • It is not the cheapest option.
  • It is not the most expensive option.
  • It uses real laser technology.
  • It is easy to use at home.
  • And it fits a realistic routine I can actually follow.

For me, the best hair-loss product is not always the strongest or most expensive one. It is the one that has the right technology and that you will actually use consistently.

Again, this is my personal experience, not a guarantee. Hair loss can have different causes, and results can vary. But if you are comparing laser helmets and trying to avoid cheap devices that only look good online, the LH40 is the one I would seriously look at.

links.title: Rote Pyramiden
links.body: Hallo zusammen \n\nHeute möchte ich euch mal etwas über die deutschen Pyramiden erzählen...japp nicht nur in Ägypten gibt es sie, sondern im sogenannten Mansfelder Land prägen sie das Bild der Natur und die hier lebenden \

sind äußerst stolz darauf

Nun um was geht es überhaupt, na um Pyramiden 


![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmdTkxQGVd9TaGPxPp4kAmMaRqLw9snybrAi3aZkGqGuKh/1780950939169.jpg)


Genauer gesagt sind es die Abraumhalden des Mansfelder Kupferbergbaus...diesen gibt es seit über 800 Jahren in der Region, kleine Pingen aus der frühen Zeit,  maximal 50 m im Durchmesser  und so tief, wie die Leitern der Bergleute reichte, und natürlich die mächtigen Halden


![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmXZEsvKsKtM1YEPYHwsH9kz7CU1bBRUPJp8CEQitQc8de/1780950024399.jpg)

Sie zeigen auch die verschiedenen Schächte des Mansfelder Kupfer Kombinats Thomas Müntzer, den Bauernkriegs Anführer...Namen der verschiedenen Schächte waren zb der auf dem Foto, Bernhard Koenen I, Bernhard Koenen II, die hohe Linde in Sangerhausen,  Otto Brosowski in Gerbstedt, oder der Thälmann Schacht in Augsdorf, oder der heute als Museumsschacht geführte Röhrig Schacht in Wettelrode

Alle tragen große Namen teils aus dem Sozialismus der DDR, japp das heute noch so genannte \

hat nicht nur seinen Namen vom roten Gold , dem Kupfer, oder von der teils sehr roten Erde überall, nein die Region war eine Hochburg des Kommunismus  und Sozialismus 

Ein Lied  sangen wir in der Schule ...Pioniere vom Mansfelder Land, daß als rotes und schönes bekannt...
Lang ist es her, und der weitere Text vergessen

Aber die streitbaren Bergleute waren schon in den Kriegen gegen Napoleon zugange und ein sogenanntes Pionierbattalion wurde aufgestellt, Diese Einheit, das Mansfelder Pionierbataillon, wurde berühmt für ihren Patriotismus und ihren Einsatz an vorderster Front (unter anderem beim Einmarsch in Paris 1815). Sie gelten als stolze militärische Pioniere aus der Region.

Dies wurde auf uns junge Pioniere gemünzt und es wurden zahlreiche gesellschaftliche \

der Arbeiter- und Bauernbewegung sowie Pioniere in der Industrialisierung (Kombinat Wilhelm Pieck) geehrt und gefeiert.
Und die Vorbilder waren Martin Luther , der oben erwähnte Thomas Müntzer sowie Otto  Brosowski...über diesen und der Fahne von Kriwoirog gibt es einen Pflichtfilm für Pioniere und FDJ ler.

Auch heute noch wirbt die Region mit diesem jahrhunderte altem Erbe


![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmUmQbjWp51CifhUWTyw4rf3MBr3SXnbaV1r9WNwcsknmh/1780951079064.jpg)

Und die Heimat liebenden Menschen wollen diese Landschaftsprägenden Pyramiden schützen, so haben sie mehrere Kaufversuche aus Südkorea in Bürgerbegehren abgeblockt, auch der jahrelange Slogan \

zeugt von der Liebe zu den Halden

Auch für mich sind sie immer wieder ein Magnet für die Augen, wenn ich da täglich vorbei fahre

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmRGtN7zCPUwcZCjuG3cFtY92dc2KNoDx3yw8v6FtDt8W7/1780951480092.jpg)

In diesem Sinne...abgekupfert und doch Original

links.title: My favourite city of Pakistan
links.body:
![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmRoX7aCHtZ6GBs2qr2hzbrysyxs3g6KLYn26GjxezobSm/1780950013224.jpg)

Hey 🤗 

Today I want to share about  my favorite city of Pakistan (Abboattabad).

Abbottabad is located in KPK province, Hazara division.
Let's explore this city together with lot of beautiful sceneric pictures.


![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmRLridY53zz5pXgfZjaqnW69CMySu3JBzJBhfLbiiDfca/1780950126257.jpg)

This city was founded in 1853, by Major, Sir James Abbott, first deputy commissioner of Hazara region 
that's why this city was named after him
Abbott - Abad. 

City was specifically designed as a Major Military cantonment and administrative center. 


![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmSb6NCfA9xj3NDpTd8YnxxdqqVkZ1iK3uhDy2w3LNyirF/1780951394922.jpg)


After independence of Pakistan in 1947
Pakistan Military Academy (PMA) at Kakul was established. 

Pakistan's best schools are  also located in Abboattabad, dream of every parent to enroll their children there like 

- Abboattabad Public school 
- Burnhall school
-Ayub medical college 

City is approximately (1,256 meter ) (4,121 feet ) above from sea level. 


![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmcfNedNnfxKhHbSTDMds3ttAKFTKmXphnbFMRTXswDWd3/1780950388172.jpg)


Hindko, pashto, and Urdu are commonly spoken languages. 

From Islamabad it's 103 km, a 2 hours drive by motorway, but there are 2 more roads lead to abboattabad one is by Murree Galiyat/ hill road,  another is GT road via taxila haripur. 

Due to road condition it will take long but worth the breathtaking scenic drive. 

Maize 🌽 is the main crop. 


![](https://i.ecency.com/DQman12WDg3mR8EyKCP73FV7oAHmbJrzzQMBrkQvoS8MZsG/1780951452174.jpg)


Abboattabad get global recognization when Al Qaeda leader Osama bin laden was killed in this city.


![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmNoDkN1fywNMNWXr8Bk3kEwabvn3RQiJWHeXMpZUCFwvE/1780950518403.jpg)

I am  in love with this city, whenever someone from Karachi visits me I must take them to visit abboattabad. 

Once a year, I visit and have peaceful few days here. 

The Cantonment area is beautifully situated on hill. 
I mostly go by walk to explore every inch of this beauty and enjoy the amazing weather. 


![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmeZuY8PkQ4x8YxgbeuvKzABWsSnnv96uev31x3rA9RoVp/1780950700179.jpg)


There's Pakistan longest Cable 🚠 car near Kakul, 2.5 km of this aerial journey with lush green mountains and river flowing down is never forgettable moment. 


![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmZcNXnVDvTUvHxCfERBkqKUnKow5hccqvSyzZ9PkZHrdB/1780950785809.jpg)


Even you will find local cable carrier after every km from one mountain to another which villagers use to commute from city to the village. 


![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmTjXZy8ywT6hHswwGxvyFUvc9SfJ7pSYcBkHSyVT1rd9a/1780950829385.jpg)


Once I lived in a cottage far from city that was totally a  different experience.


![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmRKtGvbLsABiyyNrAEHqL2zLFvZyebdCa2gB2z3tnFLRp/1780950861648.jpg)


One of my favourite things is to sitting with the wild flowers by fields. I sometimes bring my crochet with me, walk sometimes and collect interesting stones, twigs & dried leaves for DIY. 


![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmbpSLvyaJEygNKmCMKpiu2v3cd7r1W2BJwHRRcH3rUBDZ/1780951325074.jpg)


Sometimes I am also there with no action at all. The pleasure of breathing the pure, fragrant air, tranquility that nature provides.

links.title: A Time when I played with my instincts..
links.body:
Hello guys, good day all.
‎As a human, they are times when I will want to do somethings on my own without the help of anybody and if I succeed, I boost about it, then I tell people I know how that stuff works without any teachers guild, and it I fail it's a lesson to be leant. Am a victim of that, I engage into some  dangerous things or visit dangerous places and still accomplish my mission before going out. But am always careful when going to places or doing something people think is dangerous. 
‎i love taking risk because they are much lessons I learn when I fail and when I succeed after taking a risk.
‎
![severina-seidl-8bQfUT56f4Y-unsplash (1).jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/favour20045/23tbPY1yxDNNHYxZ29xv68Ww7rxwogrnzk2v7eCZSyFgTk6qCLwwF4F3i4yr3TPxMFmq5.jpg)[img sur](https://unsplash.com/photos/a-hand-touching-a-dark-surface-with-reflection-8bQfUT56f4Y)

‎i have failed many times trying to follow the same voice that make me win many times and it's like I don't really know when the voice is real or trying to place tricks with me.
‎i could remember when I was a mini forex trader, I loved trading, but I don't know how to.
‎i was added in a telegram group (quotex singal bot) by my uncle,  they drop about 100 signals a day.
‎it has a one minute trading  signal and a five minute trading signal, so you Choose where to be. At first I went to the one minute trading group, as a mini trader, I made about  $0.70 or $0.80 per win, I don't stake much tho.
One day after some successful trade, we began to face a great lost and I lost all money, but I didn't stop there. I deposited again and we gain for sometimes and we began to lost, (wish I had a big account, I won't have noticed the lost because I will gain and my lost might just be my profits).
‎After that, I rested, at that time, I began to see win,win, and win without any loss, but I wasn't trading, it made me angry and I wanted to join again, but my brother told me not to, but I refuse to hear.

![maxim-hopman-fiXLQXAhCfk-unsplash (1).jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/favour20045/23t756emzFmepWS1HJMDAbMumq7EP9cn9NnmnLGFSAEyLS7ScJTYwqVVjq144tnT3crto.jpg)[img sur](https://unsplash.com/photos/stock-market-candlestick-chart-on-dark-screen-fiXLQXAhCfk)

 I refunded my account and began to trade, when they are no signals, I use my instincts and I gained, it happened the first time, second and third time. I was happy and I rested for a while before trading again. this time I lost, yeah, my instincts failed me not once but multiple times. I was disappointed in myself. That was when I quite trading, because I used a bit and lost, and I also trusted my instincts and lost again. I just can't imagine my self losing and burning down my little account multiple times.
‎
‎so many event has happened which make me trust my instincts, but in this one, it failed me. I don't know if it was because I was anxious or over confidential.
I trust my instincts but not that much, if am very happy I don't trust my instincts, because bit will definitely fail me. But when am sad or become serious, i work with my instincts. That's when it never fails me. (I noticed this late). But I learned from it too. Learning never ends, and am a kind that love learning from my mistake and that of others.

Thank you for reading..

links.title: Siri is now an AI companion: meeting users where they are at
links.body:
https://img.leopedia.io/DQmfN7LDsV8N9VXLd4aJHxfSbfFDJSh7ZRUQoB4umvUbtNE/Siri-ai_20260608_213212_0000.webp 

>Two years after promising but failing to launch a smarter Siri, Apple unveiled its overhauled AI-powered assistant at its Worldwide Developers Conference, WWDC 2026, on Monday.

>The idea behind the new “Siri AI,” as it’s called, is to turn Siri from a voice-controlled assistant into an AI companion that can do a lot more. The new assistant will launch alongside a dedicated Siri app. 

>The new Siri can draw on current world knowledge to ground its answers to your questions. The updated assistant will also be able to access information on a user’s device and respond based on what’s displayed on their screen. — [TechCrunch report](https://techcrunch.com/2026/06/08/apples-long-awaited-ai-siri-overhaul-is-finally-here/)

One thing has proven true over the years of AI becoming a major topic in the tech industry and at large and that is the evident struggle to monetize AI apps, especially standalone generic apps.

The idea that people will be open to paying a subscription to perform a search or get answers to questions, whether simple or complex ones, hasn't exactly paid off.

Maybe if this was launched in the early days of Facebook or before, just maybe, it would be impressive enough for people to pay in great numbers.

Right now, the world is used to getting information for free. So much knowledge is lying free on the Internet. Almost everything anyone sells as “premium” is free, somewhere on the Internet, one just has to look hard enough.

The funny thing now is that AI makes it easy to find this information within seconds, and the early launch days have given the users the idea that it could be done or accessed for free, attempting to monetize latter models simply because they are termed “smarter and more capable” is delusional.

That is not going to happen.

The other problem with AI apps is that they add to the burden of users.

Having to download, update new applications and find them to use, why should users pay for several more steps and storage costs to do the regular things?

Most of these apps are essentially competing with social apps for users attention span, and that's honestly a battle they cannot win.

### Integration is the way 

Users may not go out of their way to pay for a standalone AI app that can analyze social trends, but they might pay a premium for a social app they already use to be able to conveniently analyze social posts, news reports, correct grammar in comments and messages and even auto-translate information on the platform.

This is what meeting users where they are at looks like.

X is doing this. Facebook is doing this. Google is doing this. Apple will do the same.

In Apple's case, the integration is on the OS-level and we can expect monetization from the developer and consumer front.

The solution, whilst it will have a standalone app, will vastly be an integrated tech that completely changes how users interact with everything and at the same time, how businesses reach users.

As I've always noted, since taking an interest in machine intelligence, AI is an infrastructure solution, it's a tech that needs not be on the front page. What needs to be seen is what has always been familiar, with AI simply improving the capabilities of them.

Advanced search, better recommendation, advanced editing tools, advanced maps, AI is the tech that improves everything already useful, so its monetization should be tied to these things, in their familiar environments.

links.body: I like this idea a lot, for three reasons. It promotes Hive and gives it \

applications. It can tie in with some of the Hive Dapps which run payments etc (it's a shame Distriator seems to have fallen by the wayside). It is a more useful thing to do with DHF funds.

But now I'm going to play Devil's Advocate. How do we assess the potential businesses ? Hive is notorious for it's user's total blindness to normal business practices, and relying on votes by people who have no idea what a business case is or how to read a P&L is a scary idea. How do we identify and weed out those who just want to rip capital from the DHF and then disappear without trace ? What happens if we fund a business which does it's best but still fails though no fault of their own ? How do we stop the whales from just prioritising their own mates at the expense of ordinary Hivers ?

My first thought was to have smart contracts enabling collateral to be placed in escrow accounts. But if someone has an asset like that, why can't they just liquidate it and use that to fund the business ? For smaller investments, I can see the benefits of a smart contract that enables the DHF to lock in someone's HP or HBD savings so they can't be moved out of HIVE while the debt is still outstanding (but can still use the HP for curation etc).

So overall, I really like this idea, but we'd need to find solutions to ensure it is operated fairly, with low risk to Hive funds and with safeguards against bad actors who'd inevitably see it as a source of free money to take.

links.title: Is Donald Trump Pushing Us Towards Green Tech...?
links.body:
This may sound counter-intuitive but Donald Trump might have accelerated the world's switch to Green Energy, while his intent was the complete opposite. 

There's a pretty simple reason for this: renewable energy offers as security buffer against the global supply chain uncertainties which Donald Trumps' policies are causing. 

We saw this first with the Ukraine war as gas prices soared, and now we're seeing it again with the Iran war and the soaring petrol prices. 


### Energy Security Changes Everything

For years, people who didn’t buy into renewables said fossil fuels were cheaper and more reliable. They were supposed to be the backbone of economic growth. But the past few years have flipped that thinking.

If your pipeline can be cut off by a falling out or a conflict, then the fact that it's cheap for 10 years doesn't matter when the supply gets cut off in year 11 - no country has the capacity to store one year's worth of gas. 

Renewable energy simply offers more reliability, and every country, even the US, is pumping huge sums into green tech. 


![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/revisesociology/23z79gKoG8P3Vu39jJ8dhitkF4BaKm2aUDQHZar3gSV7DQvkLM75H9ipaaKVZTuXAYwVS.png)


### The Return of Industrial Policy

There’s a bigger economic shift happening too.

Britain spent decades drifting away from hands-on industrial policy. Government just trusted markets to sort themselves out, while finance and services took center stage.

But recent economic shocks, one might even say being in a state of perpetual shock now Trump is in power, have prompted the government to take industrial policy a bit more seriously - it's giving serious support to AI for example. 

The old belief was simple: global markets would always deliver the goods, cheaply and quickly. But Covid, wars, chip shortages, and misery in supply chains have ended this. 

So, countries want their own capability in critical stuff—energy, chips, batteries, defense tech, AI.

Britain’s got real opportunities here—offshore wind, strong universities, engineering know-how, innovative manufacturing. Those could actually fuel a national strategy.

### Final thoughts...

Who would have thought that climate policy would ever line up with national interest....?!?

Governments don’t need to have some deep environmental conviction to back renewables. If greener tech boosts energy security, cuts out risky foreign suppliers, and creates new jobs, it’s a win-win!

links.title: 1963 Fiat 500 — The Original City Car
links.body:
<center>![](https://images.hive.blog/DQmefY2arvvgiL8mo28C9zc25QbDg1oq4PPNuK5XFLojmZz/1b6b7600795aff97.jpg)</center>
<center>![](https://images.hive.blog/DQmRoXQm8VfnEwbraA5jPFVhEMfoc6VcAcmAynBySjDEF49/36b7740489930076.webp)</center>

---

### 1963 Fiat 500 — The Original City Car

The **Fiat 500**, affectionately known as the “Cinquecento,” is one of the most beloved and recognizable cars ever built. Introduced in 1957 as the “Nuova 500” (New 500), it was designed to replace the pre-war Fiat 500 “Topolino” and bring motoring to the masses in post-war Italy.

Designed by the brilliant **Dante Giacosa**, the Nuova 500 was a revolutionary departure from its predecessor. Instead of a front-engine layout with a water-cooled engine, Giacosa opted for a rear-mounted, air-cooled two-cylinder engine. This allowed for a compact footprint — just 2.97 meters long — while still offering seating for four people (if you were friendly with your fellow passengers).

The 1963 model shown here is from the second series of the 500, featuring the upgraded 499 cc engine producing 18 hp (up from the original 13 hp) and the characteristic fabric sunroof that became a signature feature of the car.

<center>![](https://images.hive.blog/DQmeWHpKVCYQ4RvTUJj1waj8vRL4yrexkR8H5vfJQUWXYJK/5748f512c01a1c8b.jpg)</center>
<center>![](https://images.hive.blog/DQmbFtLSZ4nZbKcRPxroyWeEYv5PKHz41zC3RdjGfxur5mm/baaae17bfd0f225b.jpg)</center>

### A Personal Connection

I have to admit, I have my wife to thank for this post. She absolutely loves the look of the Fiat 500 — she thinks it is the cutest car ever made, and she’s not alone in that opinion. Every time we see one on the road, she points it out with genuine excitement. She has even mentioned that she would love to own the newer version of the 500 one day.

And honestly, I can see why. There’s something incredibly charming about the Fiat 500’s design. It’s cheerful, approachable, and full of personality — the automotive equivalent of a smile. The modern Fiat 500 (launched in 2007) beautifully captures the spirit of the original while adding modern reliability and comfort. It seems like the perfect city car, and I wouldn’t mind having one parked in our driveway either.

<center>![](https://images.hive.blog/DQmRZXcyJYvunNNaM3AN3jhyRXBStNCdN3wV3hUE3uja2Kt/196c4afe52b07ee7.jpg)</center>
<center>![](https://images.hive.blog/DQmTbF2eXYSTek5KpbtpGNwNLQJqetc419QqdHD19r1z68E/1b27530443ea460d.webp)</center>

### Under the Bonnet (Well, Under the Boot)

| Spec | Detail |
|------|--------|
| Engine | 499 cc air-cooled two-cylinder |
| Power | **18 hp** at 4,600 rpm |
| Torque | **24 lb-ft** at 3,000 rpm |
| Top Speed | ~95 km/h (59 mph) |
| 0–100 km/h | Not really — it peaked at about 95 km/h |
| Transmission | 4-speed manual |
| Weight | ~500 kg (1,102 lbs) |
| Designer | Dante Giacosa |
| Production | 1957–1975 (~3.2 million) |

The engine was mounted longitudinally in the rear, with the gearbox placed ahead of it (between the rear seat and the engine). The valves were pushrod-operated, and the fan was driven by a belt from the crankshaft. It was simple, robust, and easy to maintain — exactly what a car of this nature needed to be.

<center>![](https://images.hive.blog/DQmabrYGWqNWmDpFs4faovn6KFgTQRAajAuGHQFbzWkBnwE/976b5060aab85355.jpg)</center>
<center>![](https://images.hive.blog/DQmdVBHzExZzoke6mKEBp813wfSVHJXmRN2z4TjBGMe1NBk/32b70425a32a5bd2.jpg)</center>

### Design That Defined a Generation

The Fiat 500’s styling was pure function that somehow became timeless. The rounded shape maximized interior space within the tiny footprint, while the large windows gave the cabin an airy feel. The fabric sunroof (or “tetto apribile”) was not just a style feature — it provided essential ventilation in cars that lacked proper air conditioning.

Inside, the dashboard was minimal — a speedometer, a few warning lights, and basic controls. The seats were simple tubular frames with thin padding. But the driving experience was surprisingly engaging. The 500 was nimble, easy to park, and cheap to run. It was exactly what post-war Europe needed.

The 500 spawned countless variants: the **500 Giardiniera** (estate version with a longer wheelbase), the **500 Sport**, the **500 D**, **F**, and **L** (Lusso). Each iteration refined the formula without losing the essential character of the original.

### Fiat in South Africa

Fiat has a long history in South Africa, stretching back to the early 20th century. The first Fiats arrived in SA in the 1910s, and the brand quickly established a reputation for affordable, practical motoring. By the 1960s, Fiat was a well-known name on South African roads, with models like the Fiat 500, 600, and 1100 proving particularly popular.

The **Fiat 500** was sold through official importers in South Africa and became a beloved city car for its economy, simplicity, and charm. While it wasn’t locally assembled (that came later with models like the Fiat 128 at the Rosslyn plant), the 500 was a regular sight in South African cities.

In the 1970s, Fiat South Africa established local assembly operations, producing models like the Fiat 128 and 132 at the **Rosslyn** plant near Pretoria. The Fiat 500’s legacy continued, and the modern Fiat 500 has found a new audience in South Africa, sold through dealers nationwide.

Today, the Fiat 500 enjoys a dedicated following among classic car enthusiasts in South Africa, with active clubs and regular gatherings celebrating this iconic little car.

### Legacy

The Fiat 500 remained in production until 1975, but its influence extends far beyond those years. In 2007, Fiat launched a modern interpretation of the 500, designed by Roberto Giolito at Centro Stile Fiat. The new 500 was an instant hit, capturing the spirit of the original while offering modern safety, performance, and technology.

The original 500 has become a design icon — exhibited at the Museum of Modern Art (MoMA) in New York and celebrated as one of the most important automotive designs of the 20th century. Values of well-preserved originals have risen steadily, and the 500 remains one of the most accessible and enjoyable classic cars to own.

For a car that started life as basic transportation for a rebuilding nation, the 500 has transcended its humble origins to become a true automotive icon. It’s proof that great design doesn’t need to be big, powerful, or expensive — it just needs to be honest.

---

links.title: Instincts in the Face of Limited or No Information
links.body: > As humans, we tend to be meticulous and calculative about a lot of things. I think we've become more like that in today's world, where you have to be sure to some extent about some important things you do. Leaving it to chance or probability isn't always a welcome or encouraged idea. People want to be certain about the things they're going into or expending their efforts on, hence the need for some sort of information before going on. ![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmb1r8FWwjMb9kADjUb5Q4sKwZsxPSN5TF5kegAyFFLMMB/file_00000000884871f4a50da1e603b4746e.png) However, can we say that's always the case? No. There's a thing known as instincts which we all as humans have. It's in a way the opposite of being certain about a thing before moving on. Instincts tell you to move on, with little information or no certainty about an intended outcome. It's that within which says to go ahead, and you just do so with some hope that it will bring the intended results. Do humans act based on instincts? Of course. I believe that humans act based on instincts, as much as we would have loved to always do so out of certainty. I dare to say even that some of the research and analysis we do before embarking on some things tends to boil down to our instincts in the end. In some cases though, especially when a person is still sceptical about the data or information. And as a person who values certainty, I can't help but say that instincts have made the call sometimes. There are times I don't have the liberty, privilege and maybe resources to make a decision based upon necessary and helpful information. With limited and possible absence of that information, I turn to instincts, to my guts, to go ahead or not. At times, it's a yes. Other times, it's a no. Either way, the ‘yes’ and ‘no’ from trusting my instincts have both been beautifully and regretfully rewarding. Well, that's the thing with trusting your guts. ![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmawiggeKmdqSrrxUGmJwfHnHTLEecrT4s58Mjg2LvJ5eg/file_0000000045107243b23dda26d437a4ce_2_.png) Perhaps, we can say that instincts are there to help in cases when one has little or no information, and maybe limited time, yet they have to make a decision. Instincts have helped me at some points and in some situations. It has also made regret why I trusted it at other times or situations. It has caused me some financial losses, or losses in time, opportunities, resources and in other human endeavours. We tend to employ instincts also when dealing with people. That's why we could barely know some people enough but we decide to give them the benefit of doubts on opportunities and even our friendliness. I think it's okay to say that we employ instincts in many things more than we could imagine, especially when they have to do with people. We don't go around sizing people, but we relate to them from instincts, and of course from the impressions they give. In cases where we have some information, we walk by that. But instincts do go wrong, in different ways. We could perceive people as negative or positive, only to have them prove us otherwise. As much as we tend to do some things through instincts, we should choose to be certain, in critical cases, especially life-defining choices. Instincts alone don't suffice for such cases or situations. That's where a level of information or certainty is necessary for me. --- *Images are AI generated.* --- ###### Thank you for reading!

##  Why I Picked This Laser Helmet for Thinning Hair

**Disclosure:** This post contains affiliate links. If you buy through my link, I may earn a commission at no extra cost to you. As an Amazon Associate I earn from qualifying purchases.

I have been dealing with thinning hair for a long time, and I have tried a lot of things that looked good online but did not really move the needle for me.

The biggest lesson I learned is simple:

**Not every red light hair-growth device is the same.**

Some products look high-tech, but when you start reading the details, they may not be using the kind of laser light I was actually looking for. That is why I became much more careful about choosing a device. I did not want the cheapest thing I could find. I wanted something that made sense, had real laser technology, and was realistic enough for me to keep using.

That is why I ended up liking the **Theradome EVO LH40 Laser Helmet**.

### ## Why I Started Looking at Laser Helmets for Hair Loss

For me, thinning hair was not one dramatic moment. It was more like slowly noticing more scalp in photos, especially under bright light.

The crown area is where I noticed it the most. In normal bathroom lighting, I could convince myself it was fine. But in overhead lighting or camera flash, it was much more obvious.

That is what pushed me to take hair loss more seriously.

I already knew consistency mattered. The problem was that a lot of hair-growth routines are annoying. If something is messy, painful, complicated, or takes too much effort, I probably will not stick with it long term.

A laser helmet made sense to me because it is simple. You put it on, let it run, and keep going with your day.

## Why I Chose the Theradome LH40 Instead of the More Expensive Model

Theradome has a more expensive model, but I personally liked the LH40 because it felt like the better value for me.

The more expensive model may require fewer weekly sessions, but I was okay using the LH40 more often if it meant I could get into the Theradome laser helmet line at a lower price point.

That tradeoff made sense to me.

I would rather buy the more affordable model and use it consistently than spend around $1,000 on the bigger model just because it sounds stronger.

For me, the LH40 hit the right middle ground:

It is not the cheapest random helmet online.

It is not the most expensive model either.

It still uses real laser technology.

And I can actually see myself sticking with the routine.

That last part matters. A hair-growth device only helps if you actually use it.

## The Big Thing I Looked For: Real Lasers, Not Just a Cheap Light Device

When I started researching hair-growth helmets, I realized a lot of products get lumped together under “red light therapy.”

That can be confusing.

Some devices use lasers. Some use LEDs. Some use a mix. Some product pages make it hard to know what you are really buying.

I wanted a device that was clear about using lasers, because that was the whole reason I was buying it.

That is one of the main reasons I liked the Theradome LH40. I did not want something that only looked impressive in photos. I wanted the technology inside the helmet to make sense.

With hair loss, I do not want to buy based only on the outside of the device. I want to know what kind of light is actually reaching my scalp.

## My Before and After Thoughts

The photo above is why I feel comfortable talking about this.

My “before” photo showed more visible scalp at the crown. That is the kind of photo most people hate taking, but it is also the kind of photo that tells the truth.

In the “after” photo, the crown looks much better covered. The hair looks fuller, darker, and healthier in that same general area.

Now, I want to be careful here.

Hair photos can change depending on lighting, angle, hair length, styling, and whether the hair is wet or dry. I am not saying every person will get the exact same result. I am also not saying one product is a miracle cure.

What I am saying is this:

**For me, the Theradome LH40 became one of the few hair-loss tools I actually felt was worth staying consistent with.**

## Who I Think the Theradome LH40 Makes Sense For

I think the LH40 makes the most sense for someone who is starting to notice thinning hair and wants to do something proactive before it gets worse.

It may be a good fit if:

You are seeing more scalp at the crown.

You want something easy to use at home.

You do not want a messy treatment.

You want a device with real laser technology.

You are willing to be consistent for months, not days.

You want a lower-cost option than the more expensive Theradome model.

This is not something I would buy if I expected overnight results.

Hair grows slowly. That means any serious hair-growth routine has to be judged over months.

## What I Like About the LH40

The biggest thing I like is that it is easy to use.

That sounds basic, but it matters.

You do not have to apply anything. You do not have to wash anything out. You do not have to stand in front of a mirror. You just put the helmet on and let the session run.

I also like that the LH40 is the more affordable Theradome option. I do not mind using it more often if it saves money compared with the higher-priced model.

For me, that is the real value story:

**Use the LH40 more often and get access to the same type of Theradome laser helmet technology without paying for the top model.**

## What I Would Watch Out For Before Buying Any Hair-Growth Helmet

Before buying any red light or laser helmet, I would check a few things.

First, I would look at whether it uses lasers, LEDs, or both.

Second, I would check how often you are supposed to use it. A cheaper device is not a good deal if the routine is confusing or unrealistic.

Third, I would look at the company behind the product. With hair loss, I would rather buy from a company that specializes in the category than from a random brand selling hundreds of unrelated gadgets.

Fourth, I would be honest about my stage of hair loss. If someone has advanced hair loss with very little hair left in an area, a helmet may not be the right expectation. These devices make more sense when you are trying to improve thinning hair and support the hair you still have.

## My Bottom Line

The Theradome LH40 is the laser helmet I would pick again because it gives me the balance I wanted.

It is not the cheapest option.

It is not the most expensive option.

It uses real laser technology.

It is easy to use at home.

And it fits a realistic routine I can actually follow.

For me, the best hair-loss product is not always the strongest or most expensive one. It is the one that has the right technology and that you will actually use consistently.

That is why I like the **Theradome EVO LH40**.

[**Check the Theradome LH40 on Amazon here:**](https://www.amazon.com/dp/B08SNSSTPZ?th=1&linkCode=ll2&tag=hairtips05-20&linkId=7d9334b0c2daef83d42aa8183a941a77&language=en_US&ref_=as_li_ss_tl)



Again, this is my personal experience, not a guarantee. Hair loss can have different causes, and results can vary. But if you are comparing laser helmets and trying to avoid cheap devices that only look good online, the LH40 is the one I would seriously look at.

links.title: Rainy afternoons in June/ Las tardes lluviosas de junio ⛈️🍃💔
links.body:
></center>

I always remember June, not only because the rains begin in the city where I live, where the sun seems like an unmoving statue of the days, but also because it's the month of the birthday of someone I loved very much, who sadly passed away more than 15 years ago.

That person died of pancreatic cancer. It was the first time someone close to me had suffered from this disease, and I didn't know then how devastating and painful it could be. I remember that around that time, the famous actor Patrick Swayze and Steve Jobs suffered from the same cancer, and in one way or another, they brought to the world's attention how invasive and devastating this type of disease could be.

I remember that when this person found out about the diagnosis, they called me and, unable to string a sentence together, began to cry. No matter how much I asked them what was wrong, they couldn't tell me; I just heard them crying until they finally hung up. Later he sent me a message just telling me not to worry, that he would tell me later when we saw each other. That meeting happened a few days later, and although I was the one who started crying after he told me what was going on, he was the one who cheered me up because now I would need \
as he put it, to get through it. \n\n

> Through him, I learned not only to have faith, hope, and pray for a miracle, but also to hide my tears, to encourage him, and to overlook his emaciation, his sallow complexion, his hair loss, and his body ravaged by the disease and chemotherapy. Despite his condition, we met every so often, and as if we’d agreed on it, we didn’t talk about his illness, but about pleasant things: movies, books, new places we might visit someday. Only once, as he was nearing death, did the imminent end come up: “Don’t you dare start crying, or I’ll come back and take you with me.” He said it as a joke, trying to lighten the mood. I didn’t cry at that moment. What I did was respond with another joke, and we both laughed—half-heartedly, fearfully—as if neither of us wanted to be brave. Every time June comes around and I see the rain, I remember that friend who said he’d come back if he saw me cry, and even the June clouds cry for him, yet he never comes back....💔
>The first image was made in Canva and the others are from my personal gallery. The text was translated with Deepl\n\n
>Thank you for your support, reading, and comment. Until next time, friend. Regards\n\n

>Las tardes lluviosas de junio Siempre recuerdo junio, no solo porque empiezan las lluvias en la ciudad donde vivo, donde el sol parece una estatua inmóvil, sino también porque es el mes del cumpleaños de alguien a quien quise mucho y que, lamentablemente, falleció hace más de 15 años. Esa persona murió de cáncer de páncreas. Fue la primera vez que alguien cercano a mí padecía esta enfermedad, y entonces no sabía lo devastadora y dolorosa que podía ser. Recuerdo que, por esa época, el famoso actor Patrick Swayze y Steve Jobs padecieron el mismo cáncer, y de una u otra forma, llamaron la atención del mundo sobre lo invasiva y devastadora que puede ser esta enfermedad. Recuerdo que cuando esta persona se enteró del diagnóstico, me llamó y, sin poder articular palabra, rompió a llorar. Por más que le pregunté qué le pasaba, no supo decírmelo; solo lo oí llorar hasta que finalmente colgó. Después me envió un mensaje diciéndome que no me preocupara, que me lo contaría más tarde cuando nos viéramos. Esa reunión tuvo lugar unos días después, y aunque fui yo quien rompió a llorar cuando me contó lo que estaba pasando, fue él quien me animó porque ahora necesitaría \
, como él decía, para superarlo.\n\n

>o0o

Gracias a él, aprendí no solo a tener fe, esperanza y a rezar por un milagro, sino también a contener las lágrimas, a animarle y a pasar por alto su delgadez extrema, su tez amarilla, la caída del cabello y su cuerpo devastado por la enfermedad y la quimioterapia. A pesar de su estado, nos veíamos de vez en cuando y, como si lo hubiéramos acordado, no hablábamos de su enfermedad, sino de cosas agradables: películas, libros, nuevos lugares que quizá pudiéramos visitar algún día. Solo una vez, cuando se acercaba a la muerte, salió a relucir el inminente final: \

. Lo dijo en broma, tratando de aligerar el ambiente. No lloré en ese momento. Lo que hice fue responder con otra broma, y ambos nos reímos —sin ganas, con miedo— como si ninguno de los dos quisiera ser valiente.\n\nCada vez que llega junio y veo la lluvia, recuerdo a ese amigo que dijo que volvería si me veía llorar, y hasta las nubes de junio lloran por él, pero él nunca vuelve...💔

links.title: The twenty seconds of a tremor
links.body: 😁 Nah, there was a 6.1 quake on the Richter scale in western Cuba: Pinar del Río, Isla de la Juventud and Havana. I didn’t feel a thing, 😐 but honestly I had no idea what title to give this photo post.

> The only thing I want to do right now is live intensely… No importa, así sean 20 segundos... 😁 for example, not leave for tomorrow what I can do today. I don’t want my days to blend together to the point of not remembering exactly what I did yesterday, or the day before.

>
</center>

A wise man said: It is not that we have little time, but that we lose much <sub>(<a href=\
>*). And it’s about savouring what we have here, now. And dream big, so that greatness may come.

> The butterfly may not be aware of its wings, yet it uses them with perfect efficiency… and that makes me wonder how many gifts we still have to discover, if only we observe life, our surroundings, and ourselves more closely. This could be the beginning of something truly beautiful, the great discovery that will lead us to our deepest desires.

>
</center>

I took these photos just three days ago at <a href=\

>La Finquita del Arte, over in Playa Baracoa. Right after the beach clean-up we did at Playa Habana for World Environment Day, we enjoyed some very pleasant moments with Mendiola, his son, Elio, and two members of the Nativa Project.

>
</center>

😃

Elio, besides having a lovely smile… 👇



<div class=\

> Elio brought down a few coconuts for us to enjoy. The flesh and the water of those coconuts are simply unmatched in history. He even made me a straw to drink the water using the stem of a pumpkin plant. Wow, how brilliant 😁. That’s what I said. I had never seen a pumpkin plant used that way before.

> The other two lads joined the beach clean-up a little later than I did. I have proof that I took part. Yes, because now as you’ll see the photos I took of them, you might be wondering, and what about her? I arrived very early on my bicycle and immediately collected a few sacks of rubbish, which in no way fills me with satisfaction. There shouldn’t be any rubbish on the beach! Every time I’ve seen meetups of Hivers from other latitudes doing this activity and barely finding anything thrown around, I can’t help but think about the lack of awareness of people here, who I believe don’t live intensely, but rather live just to live and to destroy… though I really shouldn’t be judging anyone, to be honest.
> Right? 😄 He... or she? agrees that I should only worry about what is under my control! A sequence ;)
> Now that I’m listening to a very boisterous thrush in my backyard and looking at this photo I’ll share right now…
> I remembered the thrush’s nest Elio showed me.

> They even use bits of nylon in them, anything they can find. We went to explore a trail behind La Finquita, and you can tell the rains make everything look more colourful. The grass in this area must be delicious for the cattle ;) … it kept tripping me up all the time hahaha…

>
</center>

She’s got a little white goat, can you see it? 😅

<div class=\
> Wonderful moments that make you want to repeat them.
> But that’s all for today. I need to hop on my bike to run an errand… this story will (surely) continue…

> ---

links.title: Day of 2026-06-08: Market Distortions From the Bridge Issue
links.body: The bridge issue on Hive-Engine has effectively taken tools out of the respective $HIVE markets still. When infrastructure becomes impaired, inefficiencies tend to appear quickly, and liquidity can behave differently than expected. From a trading perspective, situations like this deserve attention but not overreaction. Temporary disruptions can create unusual conditions, but they also increase operational risk. The priority remains understanding whether market behavior is being driven by fundamentals or by infrastructure constraints before making allocation decisions. Plants Approaching the Next Cycle --------------------------------- The plants are getting closer to the transition from the growth phase into bloom. This stage change is important because the objective shifts. During growth, the focus is building structure; during bloom, the focus moves toward output. The timing of that transition matters, and moving too early or too late can reduce efficiency. There is a parallel here with portfolio management. Different phases require different priorities, and success often depends on recognizing when the underlying objective has changed rather than continuing to optimize for a previous stage. Efficiency increase for the parents ----------------------------------- One of the bigger projects this year has been upgrading the utilities at my parents' house. What started as a few small improvements quickly turned into a broader modernization effort, replacing aging infrastructure and improving reliability for the years ahead. From networking and communications to power distribution and general household systems, the goal has been to make everything more efficient, easier to maintain, and better prepared for future needs, with the next generation to take over the house in mind. While utility upgrades are rarely the most exciting projects on the surface, seeing decades-old equipment give way to modern solutions has been both satisfying and rewarding, especially knowing it will help keep the house running smoothly for years to come. This week they gonna get a new dish washer and deep freezer, but it will be hard to track the current consumption of these devices. I have to track total household consumption for some time and then run appliances, and subtract all snaps shots. Portfolio Movement (25 May → 8 Jun) ----------------------------------- Changes over this period, expressed in percentage terms: * $ACE: ➖ 0% (no change) * $BBH: 📉 approximately -2.01% * $BBHO: 📉 approximately -0.86% * $BTC: 📉 increase in short exposure (~2.86% increase in magnitude) * $DAB: 📉 approximately -0.30% * $LTC: 📉 approximately -2.08% (increase in short exposure) * $MATIC: ➖ 0% (no change) * $SURGE: 📈 reduction in short exposure (~0.004% decrease in magnitude) * $TGLD: ➖ 0% (no change) * $TNVDA: ➖ 0% (no change) * $TTSLA: ➖ 0% (no change) The overall theme continues to be incremental adjustment rather than major portfolio restructuring. Volume Context --------------

/>

Volume is overwhelmingly concentrated in $LTC, accounting for more than 70% of observed activity. $BBHO and $SOL form a secondary tier, while the rest of the market sees relatively limited participation. Such concentration can improve liquidity in a few specific areas while leaving the broader market thin. In those conditions, execution quality becomes increasingly asset-specific, making disciplined sizing and patience even more important.

links.title: The gifting paradox
links.body:
>

  What is the perfect gift? The intention is important, but the meaning of it and why you are gifting it? Is gifting to prove something to the other? Birthday gifts are a challenge to understand; sometimes we see them as an obligation, just as the etiquette of society. And how we should deal with gifting is always a challenge as a gifter or receiver. Maybe it is easier to start the problem as a receiver.

![couple-opening-christmas-presents-by-tree.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/gwajnberg/23xAXq3fM9gdFLRWz6vY1AXbKwhmjBFJL8wYeevGqS6Nn3DsaKZSiwkeEjYkyjWaTN2BA.jpg)

>

  I have just remembered one birthday party that i received probably 10 of the same stationery kits with scissors, staples, pencils and pens. After the party, we just started to think what to do with the same kit, multiple times. On that time parents didn't communicate between themselves to understand what the birthday kid would enjoy. Nowadays, at least before a party, we parents ask the parents of the birthday kid what the kid likes to do, and ask for tips. That helps, but still the kid is dumped with toys and presents that end up forgotten in a corner within a week. Then, some parents started with the idea of instead of receiving gifts, just 5 -10 dollars in an envelope. That way with that money the kid will be able to buy maybe one or two presents that will last longer. I think that type of mechanism also works even with grown-ups. Who is better to understand what we want? Only ourselves.

  Personal tastes are difficult to understand and accept. If we can listen to the other and what we need, we will basically ruin a gift. My parents' gifts improved a lot when, instead they buying directly, they started to send the money and I just told them what I was going to buy. Even if I tell them if I need or like a certain type of thing, they will add an opinion on top that probably will make the gift unusable. I love wine, and once they bought me a bottle vacuum sealer kit that for sure was very expensive. I used it a couple of times, but it isn't practical, and I don't care about using, just closing the wine with a cork is sufficient for me. When we add to a gift some taste about yourself, maybe the gift loses context because we are thinking about if the other one will use that gift, not ourselves.

  As a gift sender, I need to think about the purpose of this gift. Just giving something that we think the other person should have loses the purpose totally. But something important that someone important told me: sometimes we just want to prove to the other person that we like them. Why keep proving that? I think the problem is society. How many times have I heard people complaining about the quality of a present? Because it isn't from a specific brand or material? So, it is such a pressure on us that a present will please someone.

![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/gwajnberg/23xKvhtRZtaw6VoXDWM4LSQD2EpiLLiB6cqdq4vrHmMWRK87QUSMK3WVhMVeWAFE6aXjK.jpg)

where even the misspelling has a significance for me .

  I think the best presents that I received are drawings or cards when those were made with the heart. This drawing made by my daughter is something that really put me close to her heart, and that is much better than any other gift bought with money. This drawing shows her feelings about herself a land of imagination where she is happy. The misspelling gives the charm of her stage of learning how to write. I think she drew that 1 year ago and she even don't remember about it, but this is the type of gold that we miss sometimes. What is the real purpose of a gift?

[![](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/gwajnberg/23wMS5Mk5RaoA6EdKv35TPtYzT2oppCtUWD6qwC5GUBMb877AgJ5rGzJeoTew2bGQJQWZ.png)](https://vote.hive.uno/@gwajnberg)
Banner created in canva

![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/gwajnberg/23u5tR8RSXuZFgpjQ6Eiqz8JMMjig1nLZFvxM1sFhvNmiGYA2snkPD7Z4TnmFxxRyih87.png)

 Qual é o presente perfeito? A intenção é importante, mas o significado e o motivo pelo qual você está presenteando também são importantes? Será que presentear serve para provar algo para a outra pessoa? Presentes de aniversário são um desafio para entender; às vezes os vemos como uma obrigação, como uma etiqueta social. E como devemos lidar com a questão dos presentes é sempre um desafio, tanto para quem presenteia quanto para quem recebe. Talvez seja mais fácil começar a reflexão sobre o assunto como quem recebe.

![couple-opening-christmas-presents-by-tree.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/gwajnberg/23xAXq3fM9gdFLRWz6vY1AXbKwhmjBFJL8wYeevGqS6Nn3DsaKZSiwkeEjYkyjWaTN2BA.jpg)

>

 Acabei de me lembrar de uma festa de aniversário em que recebi uns 10 kits de material escolar iguais, com tesoura, grampos, lápis e canetas. Depois da festa, ficamos pensando no que fazer com o mesmo kit várias vezes. Naquela época, os pais não se comunicavam para entender o que a criança gostaria de ganhar. Hoje em dia, pelo menos antes de uma festa, nós, pais, perguntamos aos pais da criança o que ela gosta de fazer e pedimos dicas. Isso ajuda, mas mesmo assim a criança acaba com brinquedos e presentes que ficam esquecidos em algum canto em menos de uma semana. Então, alguns pais começaram a ter a ideia de, em vez de presentes, dar 5 a 10 dólares em um envelope. Assim, com esse dinheiro, a criança consegue comprar um ou dois presentes que durem mais. Acho que esse tipo de mecanismo também funciona com adultos. Quem melhor para entender o que queremos? Só nós mesmos.

 Gostos pessoais são difíceis de entender e aceitar. Se dermos ouvidos ao outro e ao que precisamos, basicamente arruinaremos um presente. Os presentes dos meus pais melhoraram muito quando, em vez de comprarem diretamente, começaram a enviar o dinheiro e eu apenas lhes dizia o que ia comprar. Mesmo que eu diga se preciso ou gosto de algo específico, eles acrescentam uma opinião que provavelmente tornará o presente inútil. Eu adoro vinho, e uma vez eles me deram um kit de seladora a vácuo para garrafas que, com certeza, era muito caro. Usei algumas vezes, mas não é prático, e não me importo de usar; fechar o vinho com uma rolha já é suficiente para mim. Quando adicionamos um toque pessoal a um presente, talvez ele perca o seu propósito, porque estamos pensando se a outra pessoa vai usar o presente, e não em nós mesmos.

 Como quem envia um presente, preciso pensar no propósito dele. Dar algo que achamos que a outra pessoa deveria ter tira completamente o sentido do presente. Mas algo importante que alguém importante me disse: às vezes, só queremos provar para a outra pessoa que gostamos dela. Por que continuar provando isso? Acho que o problema é a sociedade. Quantas vezes já ouvi pessoas reclamando da qualidade de um presente? Porque não é de uma marca ou material específico? Então, existe uma pressão enorme sobre nós para que um presente agrade a alguém.

![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/gwajnberg/23xKvhtRZtaw6VoXDWM4LSQD2EpiLLiB6cqdq4vrHmMWRK87QUSMK3WVhMVeWAFE6aXjK.jpg)

, onde até o erro de ortografia tem um significado para mim.

  Acho que os melhores presentes que já recebi foram desenhos ou cartões feitos com carinho. Este desenho feito pela minha filha me tocou profundamente, e isso é muito mais valioso do que qualquer presente comprado com dinheiro. O desenho mostra os sentimentos dela, um mundo de imaginação onde ela é feliz. Os erros de ortografia dão um charme especial à fase em que ela ainda está aprendendo a escrever. Acho que ela fez esse desenho há um ano e nem se lembra mais, mas é esse tipo de preciosidade que às vezes nos escapa. Qual é o verdadeiro propósito de um presente?

[![](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/gwajnberg/23wMS5Mk5RaoA6EdKv35TPtYzT2oppCtUWD6qwC5GUBMb877AgJ5rGzJeoTew2bGQJQWZ.png)](https://vote.hive.uno/@gwajnberg)

links.title: Im Schatten der Fußball-Weltmeisterschaft macht die Sparkasse Bitcoin Handel möglich?/In the shadow of the FIFA World Cup, is the savings bank making Bitcoin trading possible?
links.body:
![61344.png](https://images.hive.blog/DQmTAwmuA7ZVuB8ygu6Nufny2XmZ1c6dtNWB5RJQkRqzHip/61344.png)

Bei Krypto denken Sie direkt an Bitcoin? Das ist verständlich, denn Bitcoin ist die bekannteste und erste Kryptowährung. Doch die Welt der digitalen Währungen ist weitaus vielfältiger: Von Ethereum über Cardano bis hin zu Solana gibt es zahlreiche spannende Kryptos, die mit innovativen Technologien und Anwendungsbereichen überzeugen. 

Egal, ob Sie langfristig investieren, Ihr Portfolio diversifizieren oder einfach nur neugierig auf die Möglichkeiten der Blockchain-Technologie sind – mit unseren Angeboten ist der Einstieg in Krypto günstiger, als Sie vielleicht denken! 

---
Der Euro-Stablecoin, an dem die Sparkassen-Finanzgruppe über das europäische Bankenkonsortium „Qivalis“ (unter Beteiligung der DekaBank und der Landesbank Hessen-Thüringen) arbeitet, wird voraussichtlich in der zweiten Jahreshälfte 2026 gelauncht.

Wichtige Details zum LaunchGemeinschaftsprojekt: Die Sparkassen entwickeln diesen Stablecoin nicht alleine. Sie tun dies in einem Konsortium aus mittlerweile 37 führenden europäischen Banken (darunter auch die DZ Bank, ING und UniCredit).Das Ziel: Der digitalisierte Euro soll schnelle, kostengünstige und programmierbare Zahlungen rund um die Uhr ermöglichen. 

Damit wollen Europas Banken eine regulierte Alternative zu den US-Dollar-beherrschten Stablecoins wie USDT oder USDC schaffen.


![61109.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmZfpj12jqQeysZRbZCZoamLxhX35MYnTtuZXtNg25G7vd/61109.jpg)


Rechtliche Absicherung: Das Projekt wird über ein eigens gegründetes Unternehmen in den Niederlanden realisiert. Es wird vollständig den strengen EU-Krypto-Vorgaben (⁠MiCAR) entsprechen.Parallel dazu plant die Sparkasse, ihren Kunden den regulierten Kauf von klassischen Kryptowährungen (wie Bitcoin und Ethereum) über die reguläre Sparkassen-App ebenfalls im Laufe des Jahres 2026 zu ermöglichen.

Die deutsche Sparkassen-Finanzgruppe wird den Handel mit Bitcoin und anderen Kryptowährungen voraussichtlich ab Sommer 2026 direkt über die Sparkassen-App freischalten. Für die Einführung eines bankeigenen Euro-Stablecoins haben sich die Sparkassen (über die DekaBank) zudem einem großen Bankenkonsortium (Qivalis) angeschlossen, dessen Launch für die zweite Jahreshälfte 2026 geplant ist.

Bitcoin-Direkthandel über die AppStarttermin: Geplant für Sommer 2026.

Umsetzung: Der Krypto-Handel und die Verwahrung erfolgen über das Wertpapierhaus der Sparkassen, die DekaBank.

Angebot: Kunden sollen direkt über ihr Girokonto beziehungsweise die Banking-App auf Kryptowährungen wie Bitcoin und Ethereum zugreifen können. 

**Es ist ein direkter Kauf ohne Beratung und mit Warnungen vor Kursschwankungen vorgesehen.**

Quelle 
Sparkasse 

Mein persönliches Fazit:
Eigentlich brauche ich die Sparkasse gar nicht, um in Bitcoin und Co. zu investieren. Ich spekuliere jedoch auf ein besseres Ranking, wenn dort zukünftig mehr Eigenkapital von mir herum liegt. Meine Bewertung liegt derzeit bei Stufe 9, d. h., ich bekomme ungünstige Immobilienkredite. Ab Stufe 1–3 sieht das für mich günstiger aus.  Günstigere Kreditzinsen würden es mir erleichtern, eine neue Immobilie zu finanzieren.

Mein neuer Plan ist es deshalb, in den nächsten drei Jahren bei der Sparkasse in Kryptowährungen zu investieren und dann vor dem nächsten Kryptowinter in den Sparkassen-eigenen Stablecoin umzuschichten.

---

English 

![61344.png](https://images.hive.blog/DQmTAwmuA7ZVuB8ygu6Nufny2XmZ1c6dtNWB5RJQkRqzHip/61344.png)

When you think of crypto, do you immediately think of Bitcoin? That's understandable, as Bitcoin is the most well-known and first cryptocurrency. But the world of digital currencies is far more diverse: From Ethereum and Cardano to Solana, there are numerous exciting cryptocurrencies that impress with innovative technologies and applications.

Whether you're investing for the long term, diversifying your portfolio, or simply curious about the possibilities of blockchain technology – with our offers, getting started with crypto is more affordable than you might think!

The euro stablecoin being developed by the German Savings Banks Finance Group through the European banking consortium \

(with the participation of DekaBank and Landesbank Hessen-Thüringen) is expected to launch in the second half of 2026.

Key details about the joint project: The savings banks are not developing this stablecoin alone. They are doing so in a consortium of 37 leading European banks (including DZ Bank, ING, and UniCredit). The goal: The digitized euro is intended to enable fast, cost-effective, and programmable payments around the clock.

With this, European banks aim to create a regulated alternative to US dollar-dominated stablecoins such as USDT or USDC.

 ![61109.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmZfpj12jqQeysZRbZCZoamLxhX35MYnTtuZXtNg25G7vd/61109.jpg)

Legal safeguards: The project will be implemented through a specially established company in the Netherlands. It will fully comply with the strict EU crypto regulations (MiCAR). In parallel, the savings bank plans to enable its customers to purchase traditional cryptocurrencies (such as Bitcoin and Ethereum) via the regular savings bank app, also during 2026.

The German Savings Banks Finance Group expects to activate trading in Bitcoin and other cryptocurrencies directly via the savings bank app starting in summer 2026.  For the introduction of their own euro stablecoin, the savings banks (via DekaBank) have joined a large banking consortium (Qivalis), whose launch is planned for the second half of 2026.

Direct Bitcoin trading via the app: Launch date planned for summer 2026.

Implementation: Crypto trading and custody will be handled by the savings banks' securities house, DekaBank.

Service: Customers will be able to access cryptocurrencies like Bitcoin and Ethereum directly through their checking account or banking app.

**Direct purchase without consultation and with warnings about price fluctuations is planned.**

Source: Savings Bank

My personal conclusion:

Actually, I don't need the savings bank to invest in Bitcoin and other cryptocurrencies. However, I'm hoping for a better rating if I have more of my own capital invested there in the future. My rating is currently at level 9, meaning I get unfavorable mortgage rates.  From level 1 to 3 onwards, it looks more favorable to me. Lower interest rates would make it easier for me to finance a new property.

Therefore, my new plan is to invest in cryptocurrencies with the savings bank over the next three years and then switch to the savings bank's own stablecoin before the next crypto winter.

links.title: Photographing strangers and their dogs in the park- Monomad Challenge.
links.body:
![cover.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/malos10/23tH1deRc1VQy1yD6KaUPyMK88WmgXGGHqhQyNofvDADu7jXWUYxosR53njWMQ62bC5GB.jpg)
Greetings to all my friends in this beautiful community, today I am back with a new set of photographs that I took as part of my content dynamic where I approach strangers and ask them if I can take their pictures, on this occasion I saw a guy who was walking with a puppy that clearly looked like a puppy and was adorable so I decided to approach them and we took these photos. First I took a couple of photos of the puppy alone, that is the easiest way to break the ice between strangers and me, usually when they see the photos of their pets they get very excited and happy:
Un saludo a todos mis amigos en esta hermosa comunidad, hoy estoy de vuelta con un nuevo set de fotografia que hice como comparte de mi dinamica de contenido en donde me acerco a desconocidos y les pregunto si les puedo hacer fotos, en esta ocasion vi a un chico que estaba caminando con un perrito que se veia que era cachorro y era adorable asi que decidí acercarme a ellos y hicimos estas fotos. Primero le tomé un par de fotos al perrito solo, esa es la manera mas facil de romper los nervios entre los desconocidos y yo, usualmente cuando ven las fotos de sus mascotan se emocionan y se alegran mucho:
![IMG_0001.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/malos10/Eo4B3kzLctsModBWMfzsCtLjsxu7Jp9eyL9qbKQjfRaemyV6Q1qy7zxidmye2eKeSTA.jpg)
The puppy is still a baby and looked too adorable, it was a cocker spaniel breed mixed with some other breed.
El perrito aun es cachorro y se veia demasiado adorable, era de raza cocker spaniel mezclado con alguna otra raza.
![IMG_0003.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/malos10/Eo23dhrZVxpDbDUqsKFbRiRHj9RqxKhX6r9HazVsUkX2PCKR4ZbqqD6V9R88i2sjoji.jpg) ![IMG_0010.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/malos10/Eo4B7VR9qbXZr4zqNovXgZgofhiZyWuDygpRetUwPtvacddkBjHYuJG3dybgKbYGmS2.jpg)
Then I asked the owner if he wanted a photo with his pet, he immediately crouched down and we took this photo:
Luego le pregunté al dueño si quería una foto con su mascota, el inmediatamente se agachó y hicimos esta foto:
![IMG_0017.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/malos10/EoGw3TCvHG3tMXxc1tfVq64ur5RcVyXnw9NVPgKkgKRvHz5U4JdzguoKVoasML3AvGY.jpg)
I suggested that he could hold his pet up to his face level and we made my favorite photo:
Yo le sugerí que podia alzar a su mascota a la altura de su cara y hicimos mi foto favorita:
![IMG_0021.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/malos10/EoGwSvPEtHw9G29SsTuYiy1i1mJ7SiD5Xt1tzrfB8d5qM6YT6HVVim2HSnUWLYynzgs.jpg)
All the photos were taken with my Canon R8 camera, a 50mm lens at 1.8/f and only natural light. At the end of this spontaneous photo session both the guy and I were super happy with the results and I hope you like them as much as we do!
Todas las fotos las tomé con mi camara Canon R8, un lente 50mm a 1.8/f y solo luz natural. Al final de esta sesion de fotos espontanea tanto el chico como yo quedamos super contentos con los resultados y espero que a ustedes les gusten tanto como a nosotros!

links.title: Why Was Jesus Christ Baptized Despite Being Sinless?(Part 1)//The Old Path.
links.body: https://youtu.be/PTc3HPscd14?si=4V-e4GLYqREonR3M\n\nOne question that many people ask is : \

.  According to the bible, the baptism of Jesus was not because he needed cleansing from sin, but because he came to fulfill God's righteousness and set an example for mankind. In **Matthew 3:13-15** when Jesus came to John the Baptist to be baptized, John hesitated knowing that Jesus was greater than him, but Jesus said to him \

. This statement shows that Christ's baptism was an act of obedience to God's will.

Jesus never committed sin. He was holy, blameless, and separate from sinners. His baptism was not for forgiveness of sins as it is for ordinary people; it shows complete submission to God and obedience to divine plan.
His baptism teaches christians the importance of humility, obedience, and faithfulness to God's commandments. Through this act, Christ showed that righteousness is demonstrated not only by what we believe but also by how faithfully we obey God.

**Thanks for your support**

links.title: Maggico Casino y la evolucion del entretenimiento digital en Chile
links.body:
# Un viernes en Maggico Casino: asi disfrutan hoy su tiempo libre muchos jugadores chilenos

![](https://vipon.s3.amazonaws.com/img/44364222502b0fda89aa85b09206bd189ad2e93171c0bd.png)

La tarde cae sobre Santiago, las calles siguen con movimiento y, mientras algunos se reunen con amigos o buscan una serie para terminar el dia, otros prefieren una forma distinta de entretenimiento. En medio de esa rutina moderna aparece [Maggico Casino](https://maggicocasinocl.com/), una plataforma que se ha convertido en parte de las opciones digitales que muchos usuarios en Chile incluyen en sus momentos de descanso. Lo interesante no es solo el juego en si, sino la manera en que encaja dentro de una noche cualquiera: desde el sofa de casa, durante una pausa despues del trabajo o incluso mientras se comenta el resultado de un partido con amigos por mensajeria.

Lo que antes exigia desplazarse hasta un lugar fisico ahora cabe perfectamente en una pantalla. La experiencia es rapida, directa y adaptada a un publico que valora la comodidad tanto como la variedad.

## La nueva rutina de entretenimiento digital en Chile

Durante los ultimos anos, los habitos de ocio han cambiado de forma evidente. Las plataformas digitales han ganado terreno porque permiten elegir el ritmo de la experiencia. No hay horarios fijos ni necesidad de organizar grandes planes. Cada persona decide cuando conectarse y cuanto tiempo dedicar a su entretenimiento.

En una noche comun, un jugador puede comenzar explorando algunas novedades, probar diferentes categorias y alternar la experiencia con musica, conversaciones o incluso eventos deportivos en directo. Todo sucede de forma natural, sin prisas y sin complicaciones.

### Que suele buscar el usuario chileno durante una sesion nocturna

*   Acceso rapido desde cualquier dispositivo.
*   Interfaz sencilla y facil de entender.
*   Gran variedad de opciones disponibles.
*   Ritmo dinamico y tiempos de carga reducidos.
*   Posibilidad de elegir entre experiencias cortas o sesiones mas largas.
*   Ambiente visual moderno y atractivo.

## Una noche real: entre la curiosidad y la diversion

Al observar como se desarrolla una sesion tipica, llama la atencion la variedad de comportamientos. Algunos usuarios llegan con una idea clara de lo que quieren probar. Otros simplemente exploran. Cambian de categoria, revisan nuevas opciones y buscan experiencias diferentes para romper la rutina del dia.

No existe una formula unica. Precisamente ahi esta parte del atractivo. Mientras unos prefieren partidas rapidas para relajarse despues del trabajo, otros convierten la experiencia en una actividad mas extensa durante el fin de semana. La libertad de elegir el ritmo marca una diferencia importante.

## Por que las plataformas digitales forman parte del ocio moderno

![](https://vipon.s3.amazonaws.com/img/849737f4a50f139236e6e5b0e884bef628c8fc3d30123d.png)

La tecnologia ha transformado la manera en que las personas consumen entretenimiento. Hoy todo compite por la atencion del usuario: series, redes sociales, videojuegos, videos cortos y plataformas interactivas. En ese escenario, las opciones que ofrecen variedad y accesibilidad tienen una ventaja evidente.

Para muchos jugadores chilenos, la clave no esta solo en participar, sino en encontrar una experiencia que resulte entretenida, intuitiva y capaz de adaptarse a distintos momentos del dia. Esa flexibilidad es precisamente una de las razones por las que este tipo de plataformas mantienen una presencia cada vez mas visible dentro del panorama digital chileno.

## Cuando termina la noche, la experiencia continua

Al final de la jornada, la sensacion se parece mucho a la de cualquier otra forma de entretenimiento moderno: desconectar durante un rato, disfrutar de una experiencia dinamica y volver a la rutina con la impresion de haber aprovechado bien el tiempo libre. No se trata solamente de una tendencia tecnologica, sino de una nueva manera de entender el ocio en un pais donde cada vez mas personas eligen experiencias digitales adaptadas a su propio estilo de vida.

links.title: Golden hour and quiet thoughts 🌅💖
links.body:
https://img.leopedia.io/DQmeZunp2E3fSsmHoWEozgDeCSrjGXDQZQG9ME1YXDdLvNK/IMG_4152.jpg 

There is something special about the last sunlight of the day. It slows everything down and makes even ordinary moments feel a little more magical.

Today I took a few minutes to enjoy the golden hour and reflect on everything I’m working toward. Sometimes it’s easy to focus only on the destination, but I’m learning to appreciate the journey too. Every photo I share, every new idea, and every small achievement is helping me get closer to the life I dream about.

One day, I hope to combine my passion for travel, photography, and helping others discover amazing places around the world. Until then, I’ll keep learning, creating, and enjoying these beautiful moments along the way ✈️🌍

The future may still be unwritten, but I’m excited for every chapter that’s ahead.
