body.title: Film Review: The Revenge of Frankenstein (1958)
body.body:
![(source:tmdb.org)](https://image.tmdb.org/t/p/original/uYkRhx99msTSz5MTReoF5siEkJ1.jpg)



In the horror cinema, the problem of resurrecting a seemingly deceased franchise icon is a familiar one. In 1931, Universal’s classic [*Frankenstein*](https://peakd.com/hive-166847/@drax/film-review-frankenstein-1931) concluded with the Monster apparently perishing in a burning windmill, only for the studio to devise an ingenious—if contrived—escape for his return in 1935’s [*The Bride of Frankenstein*](https://peakd.com/hive-166847/@drax/film-review-the-bride-of). Two and a half decades later, Britain’s Hammer Film Productions faced a remarkably similar narrative quandary. Their 1957 smash hit, [*The Curse of Frankenstein*](https://peakd.com/hive-166847/@drax/film-review-the-curse-of-frankenstein-1957-41p) had concluded with its ruthlessly ambitious protagonist, Baron Victor Frankenstein (Peter Cushing), awaiting execution for murder, his fantastical tale of creation dismissed as the ravings of a madman. For Hammer, the commercial imperative for a sequel was clear, but the creative challenge was how to plausibly spring the Baron from the guillotine. The resulting film, 1958’s *The Revenge of Frankenstein*, reuniting Cushing with screenwriter Jimmy Sangster and director Terence Fisher, provides a convenient if not entirely convincing solution, launching a second chapter that is both a testament to Hammer’s burgeoning house style and a film hampered by the rushed circumstances of its production.

*The Revenge of Frankenstein* opens with titles placing the action in 1860, immediately establishing a curious retcon. Where the first film’s epilogue suggested Frankenstein’s story was disbelieved, here we are told his exploits and the existence of his Monster have become a source of Europe-wide infamy. The Baron’s execution is a public event met with a sigh of relief. Yet, as the blade falls, it is not Frankenstein who is decapitated but a complicit priest (Alex Gallier), in a plan orchestrated by the Baron’s hunchbacked servant, Karl (Oscar Quitak). The escape is executed with a swift, almost perfunctory efficiency that prioritises getting the plot moving over narrative elegance. It is a functional, rather than inspired, piece of screenwriting—a necessary evil to return Cushing’s magnetic villain to the centre of the action.

Having cheated death, Frankenstein resurfaces in the city of Karlsbrück under the alias “Dr. Victor Stein”. He establishes a hugely successful medical practice, cynically catering to the wealthy while operating a free clinic for the poor to cultivate a benevolent reputation. His methods baffle and irritate the local medical council, whose delegation to his hospital includes the young, ambitious Dr. Hans Kleve (Francis Matthews). Kleve alone recognises Stein as the infamous Frankenstein and, in a pivotal scene, reveals himself as a fanatical admirer, begging to become the Baron’s pupil. This dynamic injects a fresh energy into the formula; where Frankenstein previously worked in isolated obsession, he now has a devotee. Together, they embark on a new project: creating a perfect body for Karl, who willingly donates his brain in hopes of a new life. The experiment initially seems a triumph, though an ominous precursor—a chimpanzee subject that, upon revival, cannibalised its mate—hints at latent savagery. The new creature (Michael Gwynn) is a tragic, articulate figure, a far cry from Christopher Lee’s mute, shambling Monster in the first film. However, when a well-meaning but foolish patient, Margaret Conrad (Eunice Gayson), releases him from his restraints, Karl’s idyllic new existence shatters. Confused, rejected, and increasingly violent, he escapes, unleashing a series of incidents that inevitably expose “Dr. Stein’s” true identity.

This plot hinges on a notable, and rather cavalier, disregard for continuity between the two films. As noted, Frankenstein’s tale shifts from being dismissed as lunacy to being accepted as widespread fact. This inconsistency can be directly attributed to the film’s rushed genesis. Producer Michael Carreras allowed Sangster a mere six weeks to deliver the script, a pressure that inevitably forced corners to be cut and logical through-lines to be simplified in favour of expedient set-up.

Despite this foundational wobble, *The Revenge of Frankenstein* mostly works, thanks largely to the assured hands of its core creative team. Terence Fisher, operating again on a limited budget, directs with a lean, confident efficiency that distinguishes the sequel from its predecessor. He moves the action from a gothic castle to a more urban, clinical environment, reflecting the Baron’s new, more socially integrated guise. The film’s greatest success is Michael Gwynn’s performance as the creature. An experienced stage actor, Gwynn brings a profound pathos and intelligence to the role, making Karl’s tragic fate—his consciousness trapped in a body that becomes a prison of its own—arguably more nuanced and memorable than Lee’s more iconic but less psychologically explored Monster. Fisher also maintains the series’ brief flashes of levity, notably through Lionel Jeffries’ scene-stealing turn as a garrulous, morally flexible gravedigger.

However, not all elements land effectively. The film dabbles in proto-slasher tropes when the disturbed Karl stumbles upon a young couple on a secluded street, resulting in the death of the girl (Avril Leslie). The scene feels tonally jarring, a crude intrusion of sudden violence that clashes with the film’s more measured gothic and tragic tones. Furthermore, the female lead is conspicuously wasted. Eunice Gayson, who would later find fame as James Bond’s first girlfriend, Sylvia Trench, is given the inconsequential role of Margaret Conrad. She serves neither as a romantic interest nor a meaningful damsel in distress; her function is purely plot-catalytic, a device to unleash the monster before receding into the background—a disappointing treatment for a capable actress.

In terms of content, the film’s reputation for causing contemporary critics to call for stricter censorship seems hyperbolic by modern standards. Even for the 1950s, *The Revenge of Frankenstein* is relatively tame. True to Hammer’s early approach, much of the violence occurs off-screen, and there is very little of the explicit gore that would later define the genre. The horror is more suggested through implication and the chilling amorality of Cushing’s Frankenstein.

Sangster and Fisher salvage a potentially routine monster-on-the-loose narrative with a clever double-twist near the climax. After his patients, enraged by his deception, nearly beat him to death, Frankenstein appears to meet his end. Yet, in a final act of arrogant triumph, it is revealed that Dr. Kleve has saved the Baron’s brain, transplanting it into a new body. The epilogue, set in a London surgery where Kleve assists a “Dr. Frank”, is brilliant. It not only provides a deliciously cynical punchline but also seamlessly bridges the film to future sequels, ensuring the Baron’s—and Hammer’s—line of unholy research could continue indefinitely.

*The Revenge of Frankenstein* is a sequel of pragmatic ingenuity rather than groundbreaking inspiration. Hamstrung by a rushed script that papers over continuity gaps, it nonetheless succeeds through Fisher’s solid direction, Cushing’s eternally compelling central performance, and a genuinely tragic turn from Michael Gwynn. It consolidates the Hammer formula established in *The Curse of Frankenstein*: colour, cynicism, and a focus on human evil over supernatural monstrosity. While it stumbles in its handling of female characters and occasional tonal missteps, its effective final twist ensures it remains a compelling and important link in the chain of one of British cinema’s most enduring horror series.


RATING: 5/10 (++)

body.title: A rainy day ⛈️, which ended with a small gathering to celebrate 🎉 a friend's 30th birthday
body.body:
![1000936389.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/yessi08/EpNnzbjJANTaKGKxFSVByLgMSHpwyGMAehfTgSLc23UAptFjZyka3rEpoAD4A4VCAPE.jpg)

<hr>

<div class=text-justify> 
<div class=\

> **
ESPAÑOL
** El día de ayer amaneció con mucha lluvia, me levanté a eso de las 7 de la mañana, ya hacía rato que estaba lloviendo pude notarlo por lo bastante mojado que estaba el patio de mi casa; cada domingo acostumbro ir a la iglesia a reunirme con mis hermanos y celebrar el servicio de escuela dominical, pero este día me tocó salir un poco más tarde de lo acostumbrado ya que la lluvia sesó por un poco de tiempo a eso de las 9:50 de la mañana, ya en casa estábamos vestidos, estábamos listos en cuanto escampó un poco nos dispusimos a ir a la iglesia. Al salir del servicio me quedo siempre en casa de mi mamá haciendo almuerzo con ella, allí comemos y comparti compartimos en familia, a eso de las 3 de la tarde cuando regresábamos a casa en el camino volvió a iniciar la lluvia, cayó bastante fuerte, tuvimos que hacer una parada en el camino para no mojarnos ya que sabemos que para esta fecha hay muchos virus en el aire sobre todo el que llamamos gripa o comúnmente resfriado, allí estuvimos aproximadamente 40 minutos, cuando escampo un poco aprovechamos que no faltaba mucho, llegamos a casa de justo al llegar nuevamente comenzó la lluvia, ya teníamos una invitación desde hace unos días para las 7 de la noche que una amiga había organizado un pequeño compartir para celebrar su cumpleaños número 30; al principio habíamos pensado en no asistir e incluso pensamos que el compartir no se iba a realizar por motivos de la lluvia; así que, nos contactamos con nuestra amiga para confirmar si se iba a realizar o no el cumpleaños, ella nos dijo que ya había organizado la pequeña decoración que todo estaba dispuesto que solamente estaban esperando que cesara la lluvia para que pudiéramos trasladarnos al lugar; gracias a Dios a eso de las 6:30 escampó definitivamente, así que, nos dispusimos a arreglarnos un poco porque era algo bastante informal, nos trasladamos hasta el lugar, fue un compartir bastante sencillo, fueron pocas las personas, solo los familiares y los amigos más allegados; estuvimos un rato, reímos charlamos, disfrutamos un delicioso arroz chino que ella había preparado el cual sirvió acompañado de una gaseosa, luego de esto se dio una ronda de pasapalos, tequeños, galletas con diversas crema y finalmente a eso de las 9:30 de la noche cantamos el cumpleaños feliz cortamos y disfrutamos el delicioso pastel deseándole a nuestra amiga un feliz cumpleaños número 30 y que este año que inicia para ella venga cargada cargado de dicha y prosperidad !🎉🎉 Espero la lectura haya sido de tu agrado . Gracias por visitar mi blog ! Dios te bendiga🙌

>

**<center>ENGLISH</center>**

Yesterday dawned with heavy rain. I woke up around 7:00 a.m. It had been raining for a while, as I could tell by how wet my patio was. Every Sunday I usually go to church to meet with my brothers and sisters and celebrate Sunday school, but this time I had to leave a little later than usual since the rain stopped for a while around 9:50 a.m. Once home, we were dressed and ready, and as soon as it eased up a bit, we headed to church.

 After my shift ends, I always stay at my mom's house and have lunch with her. We eat there and spend time together as a family. Around 3 pm, as we were walking home, it started raining again. It came down quite hard, and we had to stop along the way to avoid getting wet, since we know that at this time of year there are a lot of viruses in the air, especially what we call the flu or the common cold. We were there for about 40 minutes. When it let up a bit, we took advantage of the fact that we didn't have much time left. We arrived home, and just as we got there, it started raining again. We had received an invitation a few days earlier for 7 pm, which a friend had organized to celebrate her 30th birthday. At first, we had thought about not going and even thought that the party wouldn't happen because of the rain. So, we contacted our friend to confirm whether or not the birthday celebration was going to take place. She told us that she had already organized the decorations, that everything was ready, and that they were just waiting for the rain to stop so we could go there.  Thank God, around 6:30 the rain finally stopped, so we got ready since it was a pretty informal gathering. We went to the venue, and it was a simple get-together with just a few people, only family and close friends. We spent some time laughing and chatting, enjoying a delicious Chinese rice dish that she had prepared, which she served with soda. After that, there was a round of appetizers: tequeños (cheese sticks), cookies with various creams, and finally, around 9:30 at night, we sang \

cut and enjoyed the delicious cake, wishing our friend a happy 30th birthday and that this coming year is filled with joy and prosperity! 🎉🎉 I hope you enjoyed reading this. Thanks for visiting my blog! God bless you! 🙌 ![IMG_20251118_202019_667 (1).jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/yessi08/23wMYT8Q7ed7h8LjCA8beMXs2LvpNgftdDmtbW6LbsDKqTaWbCVobSNYa65gVx1robm9P.jpg) ![IMG_20251118_201427_200 (1).jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/yessi08/23xAZyuNKRPVkHSeJ8HRRD2PwMRaRjHNbStbQj6TYqEtpGK6dFsFLnFUtN8J1oXow9U3L.jpg) ![IMG_20251118_201701_395 (1).jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/yessi08/EpQvDxgeNkUZcBPfgLu4PyZeiv7kMSq8iWCcnSjxeB6QdLPzG5mM4BUbcP2eMBtcpYj.jpg) ![IMG_20251118_201902_579 (1).jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/yessi08/23x19F1US1wujum7r34S2iiknR9tZUtZckZ1deHreYEuD2vgkmkpv9nTU1p4LmW3RQviE.jpg) ![IMG_20251118_201040_214 (1).jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/yessi08/23xAZyqfVyjxTiRxhHGTDjnSfZWTuf7pDoY5j3unuSWGL6TsYCtCbMzSH91LVwY1Z7Sd7.jpg)

body.title: Solemnidad Tallada en Silencio - Solemnity Carved in Silence. [Esp - Eng]
body.body: alt=\
/>\n\n
data-align=\

>Recuerdo como se sentaba a mi lado mientras conversábamos en los largos pasillos de las escuelas al campo en Caimito del Guayabal cuando los dos éramos profesores, porque mientras yo fui alumno, nunca se había tomado el tiempo para conversar, claro que tampoco había mucho para tomarse tiempo libre. Fue solo años después cuando estábamos en medio de la investigación del monumento de la rotonda cuando escribíamos el artículo para Girón de Luz que expresó su profundo deseo de visitar Santa Ifigenia y mezclarse con toda la historia que allí se respira, honrar con su visita todo el homenaje que se rinde a todos los patriotas y los héroes que allí descansan. Pero yo sabía que de todos, al que quería visitar era a Martí, y es que el amor que le profesaba era titánico. Aún el sueño no se ha cumplido, y en más de una ocasión he intentado ayudarlo a alcanzarlo pero la actualidad de Cuba no ayuda mucho.

\n\n>
data-align=\

>I remember how he used to sit beside me as we talked in the long hallways of the escuelas al campo in Caimito del Guayabal, back when we were both teachers. Because when I was a student, he never took the time to talk—of course, there wasn’t much free time to take anyway. It was only years later, when we were in the middle of researching the monument at the roundabout while writing the article for Girón de Luz, that he confessed his deep desire to visit Santa Ifigenia and immerse himself in all the history that breathes there, to honor with his presence the tribute paid to all the patriots and heroes who rest in that place. But I knew that, above all, the one he longed to visit was Martí, because the love he professed for him was titanic. The dream still hasn’t come true, and more than once I’ve tried to help him reach it, but Cuba’s current reality doesn’t make it easy.

\n\n
alt=\
/>\n\n
data-align=\

>Pensaba en él y en cada cubano que añoraba de cierta forma conocer su patria, en cada cubano que después de muchos años no había podido explorar su tierra como hubiera querido. En cada paso en el cementerio, en cada vista que ofrecía trataba de retratar, de documentar cada espacio para después regalar una imagen, una evidencia del lugar y su armonía. También, supongo que como Martí en Caracas, frente a la estatua del Libertador, mi querido amigo hubiera querido rendirle honores. Cada paso sobre el mármol encendido por la cálido e intenso sol de Santiago valía la pena, cada imagen que le robé al lugar era un tesoro que después compartiría con el en la distancia. Recuerdo que era domingo, pero no cualquier domingo, era el segundo domingo de mayo y la ciudad de Santiago acompañada de flores daban muestra de amor a las madres.

\n\n>
data-align=\

>I thought of him, and of every Cuban who longed, in one way or another, to truly know their homeland—of every Cuban who, after so many years, had not been able to explore their own land the way they wished. With every step I took through the cemetery, with every view it offered, I tried to capture, to document each space so I could later gift him an image, a trace of the place and its harmony. And I suppose that, like Martí in Caracas before the statue of the Liberator, my dear friend would have wanted to pay his respects. Every step on the marble, lit by the warm and intense Santiago sun, was worth it; every image I stole from that place was a treasure I would later share with him from afar. I remember it was a Sunday—but not just any Sunday. It was the second Sunday of May, and the city of Santiago, adorned with flowers, was offering its love to the mothers.

\n\n
alt=\
/>\n\n
data-align=\

>Fue un tiempo para contemplar, para escuchar las explicaciones que nos daban de cada detalle, de cada escudo, de cada escultura que acompañaba el lugar, de asombro ante el cambio de guardia de honor después de las campanadas que retumbaron en todo el cementerio en aquel silencio profundo que caracteriza a cada uno de estos lugares, en especial a este. Como la luz y la sombra se dividían para dibujar en las paredes patrones, dejar a oscuras parte del monumento mientras que simultáneamente alumbraba otras que posteriormente también caerían en la penumbra mientras otras salían de ellas en el ciclo casi infinito de los días.

\n\n>
data-align=\

>It was a time for contemplation, for listening to the explanations they gave us about every detail, every coat of arms, every sculpture that shaped the place. A time for wonder as the honor guard changed after the bell tolls echoed through the entire cemetery, resonating in that profound silence that defines places like this—especially this one. I watched how light and shadow split themselves to draw patterns on the walls, leaving parts of the monument in darkness while illuminating others that would later also fall into shadow, as new ones emerged from it in the almost endless cycle of the days.

\n\n
alt=\
/>
alt=\
/>\n\n
data-align=\

>El recorrido tenía que seguir, la observación y la visita se complementaba con otros grandes de la patria: Carlos Manuel de Céspedes y Mariana Grajales (Padre y Madre de la Patria, respectivamente). Cada uno con sus historia y anécdotas que trascendieron a sus tiempos todo por la lucha de liberación de la España colonial. Uno, se cuenta, que abandonó todas sus riquezas y privilegios por la libertad de Cuba despertando el espíritu de lucha en el oriente cubano, la otra entregó a la lucha los guerreros más bravos que conocieran los enemigos, de una braveza tan grande que sus hazañas parecen sacada de cuentos fantásticos o de ficción.

\n\n>
data-align=\

>The path had to continue; the observation and the visit were completed by other great figures of the homeland: Carlos Manuel de Céspedes and Mariana Grajales (Father and Mother of the Nation, respectively). Each carried stories and anecdotes that transcended their time, all born from the struggle for liberation from colonial Spain. One, it is said, abandoned all his wealth and privileges for Cuba’s freedom, awakening the spirit of rebellion in the eastern part of the island. The other gave to the cause the bravest warriors the enemy would ever face, a courage so immense that her feats seem taken from fantastic tales or works of fiction.

\n\n
alt=\
>\n\n
alt=\
/>\n\n
data-align=\

>En su mármol blanco reposaba Céspedes, en una pulcritud inmaculada, una blancura que realzaba su brillo bajo el intenso sol y a su lado, Mariana con su busto como saliendo del tronco de una ceiba, árbol que tiene una representación religiosa y poética entre los cubanos, en una estructura tosca y aparentemente interminada que me hicieron pensar en la entereza de aquella mujer, de sus raíces y su firmeza. Allí frente a la estatua me estremecí, no fue cuando me paré ante Martí ni cuando lo hice ante Céspedes, fue cuando la presencia de esa madre la tuve enfrente cuando todas las historia que te contaban por años se agolparon en mi cabeza y me llenaron de emoción. La palma, esa hermosa palma real, custodiaba en cada caso firme a sus lados como centinelas eternas de aquellas grandes personalidades.

\n\n>
data-align=\

>On its white marble rested Céspedes, in immaculate purity, a brightness intensified by the fierce sun. And beside him, Mariana—her bust emerging as if from the trunk of a ceiba, a tree with deep religious and poetic meaning for Cubans. The rough, seemingly unfinished structure made me think of her steadfastness, her roots, her unbreakable strength. Standing before her statue, I trembled. It wasn’t when I stood before Martí, nor when I did so before Céspedes. It was when I found myself in the presence of that mother that all the stories told to me over the years rushed into my mind and filled me with emotion. The royal palm, that beautiful palm, stood firm at their sides like an eternal sentinel guarding those great figures.

\n\n

/>\n\n
data-align=\

>No podía faltar Emilio Bacardí, que tanto amor le entregó la ciudad, fue su primer Alcalde después de la dominación española y hoy no se puede entender la grandeza de la ciudad sin vincularla de alguna forma su figura y su acción cultural y patriótica. Hoy quizás solo vinculemos su apellido al afamado ron cubano, pero la verdad es que hizo grandes cosas en la ciudad de Santiago de Cuba, la cual amó con gran pasión. Un ejemplo de esa gran dedicación fueron los diez tomos heredados a las nuevas generaciones donde se narran las Crónicas Santiagueras de la época, reconstruyó la ciudad tras la guerra de 1898, instruyó la Fiesta de la Bandera y electrificó y urbanizó gran parte de la ciudad. Todo un ejemplo de hijo ilustre.

\n\n>
data-align=\

>Emilio Bacardí could not be absent—the man who gave so much love to the city. He was its first Mayor after the end of Spanish rule, and today it is impossible to understand the greatness of Santiago without linking it in some way to his figure and to his cultural and patriotic work. Perhaps now we associate his surname only with the famous Cuban rum, but the truth is that he accomplished extraordinary things for the city he loved with such passion. One example of that dedication are the ten volumes he left to future generations, where the Crónicas Santiagueras of the era are recorded. He rebuilt the city after the war of 1898, established the Fiesta de la Bandera, and electrified and urbanized large parts of Santiago. A true example of an illustrious son.

\n\n
alt=\
>
data-align=\

>Mucho quedaba por explorar, muchas otras cosas por ver pero por retratar quedaba poco, justo cuando me paré frente a la tumba de Estarda Palma, allí se acabó la capacidad de almacenamiento de la cámara (que gracias a amigos de la ciudad se solucionó, pero ya había quedado atrás Santa Ifigenia). Allí acabaría nuestro recorrido fotográfico por este inmenso monumento a la cubanía y a nuestras personalidades. Allí nunca regresé para seguir documentando la historia que encierra el lugar, quizás en algún momento lo haga, quizás lo haga acompañado de ese amigo que con cada imagen suspiraba, con cada historia se emocionaba y con cada episodio de mi viaje sentía que estaba allí. Eso quedará para una posible futura historia, crucemos dedos y esperemos que se concrete. Hasta aquí este hermoso paseo por parte ese Cementerio Patrimonial que en el silencio guarda el homenaje a cada uno de esas grandes personalidades.

\n\n>
data-align=\

>There was still much left to explore, many other things to see, but little left to photograph. It happened just as I stopped in front of Estrada Palma’s tomb—there the camera’s storage finally ran out. Thanks to friends in the city it was later resolved, but by then Santa Ifigenia was already behind us. That moment marked the end of our photographic journey through this immense monument to Cuban identity and to the figures who shaped it. I never returned to continue documenting the history held within those grounds; perhaps one day I will, perhaps I’ll do it accompanied by that friend who sighed at every image, who was moved by every story, who felt present in every episode of my trip. That will remain for a possible future story—let’s cross our fingers and hope it becomes real. And so ends this beautiful walk through a part of that Heritage Cemetery, which in its silence guards the tribute to each of those great figures.

body.title: KISS BLOG IDEAS: WEEK #215 ~ Without Voice, dressing speaks
body.body: <div class=\

>

<center>![4318c3cd9fcc42c593d4e51ccb50d0e8.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/nwaadiaha/23xVPmHiqPMeKez9pAFHrKDXvAGUKzWAGQdUH7w3ti99gwEFx9ABTPLq94qPdMTDes1Jy.jpg)</center>

***Option 1: How can dressing simply reflect inner steadiness?***
___
___
___

This prompt topic reminded me of a short story that happened last year; it's the reason why I picked it to talk about. The story is an embarrassing one but to pass my message across,  I would have to spill it.

So, last year, in November precisely, my mom died, and during that period, I and a few of my colleagues we're scouting for a favourable place to do our IT but in my discipline it is called practicum. Luckily, we found a place and we submitted our letter given to us by our school. 

Unfortunately, we were called to come meet the person in charge of this establishment, the period I was still grieving my mom, but because I didn't want to slow down the others, I had to come in that same day from my hometown to go with the others to the establishment, and after we meet with the person in charge, due to a little error or misconception,  we were sent back with our letter to go meet our head of department for some changes before we could be allowed to start our exercise.

I got to school and went into my head of department's office to talk to her and explain the issue since I was the leader of the group and immediately she saw me, she said and I quote \

___ ___ ___ ![FB_IMG_17760313100544193.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/nwaadiaha/23xVPbELUp5Cw63DUghxWfFBehJP71A15etMmvwYfmTrqukM6u2PxNZc599XCeB3RGax5.jpg) I wasn't crying, and I wasn't obviously looking sad, neither were my eyes puffy at least I tried to be strong even though I had lost someone but somehow, my dressing revealed that even though I was smiling and my face showed no trace of pain, sadness, or tears, I wasn't okay inside. My outer self reflected a different emotion from my inner self and anyone who is meticulous can catch it just by paying attention. A lot of times, even though we are not conscious of it, what we decide to wear or pick to wear at the point reflects how we are feeling, it reflects our emotions, if we are stable emotionally or not, our emotions work hand in hand with our brain as our heart does the job of sending signal to the brain about how we are feeling, the state of our emotions and what to dress to fit or match the emotions we are going through at the moment. How emotions simply reflect on our dressing mode, it shows if we have inner steadiness or not, it shows exactly what we are or maybe going through at the moment. I felt bad and embarrassed that she said I looked mentally unstable but she wasn't lying, my dressing that particular day wasn't something I would naturally want to do now, but after that day, I tried as much as possible to put effort into my dressing even though I was grieving. Anyone who can stop outsourcing their mood to clothes, will be able to get over this aspect, because most times letting our mood reflect on dressing is a big flaw. Regardless of what is happening inside of us, if we can still put ourselves together when picking clothes, it will be of immense help and advantage. ___ ___ ___
![f39d4d2318fe48fa848c2f189c68fbc3.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/nwaadiaha/23vsQkWTaqE5S8MzC67qeESMrV53JVdTenwgABAn4aops5q3S6L1SnPxdUp3Y5ReVeJYY.jpg)
Also, it's easy to know someone with inner steadiness from someone without one, because the first doesn't just jump on any clothing trends, they see, just for the sake of feeling among, they pick what fits them, they concentrate on what fits not what is trending. People with inner steadiness, do not dress to be noticed because they know they do not need their dress to do the talking for them, they are confident, simplicity and comfort take the top chart when choosing their clothes, they do not go for something loud, busy, extravagant, or heavy, they believe in simplicity, comfort, and classiness. Their confidence reflects in their wearing clean clothes with well-ironed lines, a good fit not trying to dress to gain external validation, and to feel put-together. Their inner steadiness is visible in their put-together dress which also reflects on their attitude. With all said and done, dressing without a mouth or voice says more about you, speaks more about what is happening inside of you, what you are thinking, or the emotions you are currently going through. Inner steadiness is fits, classy, choice, fine lines, neat, simple, comfort, and not constant validation, not trends. ___ ___ ___ *Images are mine* ___ ___ ___

body.title: Borkovačko Lake and Forest Park
body.body:
For our gardeners, May and June can be quite busy and overcrowded with work. But my wife and I decided to take a break and go on a little trip with our son. We chose Borkovačko Lake, which is right next to the town of Ruma.This lake was created in the 1970s as an accumulation lake on the Borkovac stream.Our path first led us to Borkovački Park, where we left our car and started walking.
![20260607_132646.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/markone85/23uQpekCx1m6RaADaSstrLBQ1fjB6MFMG2PZw5Q3pTVaGXpBhMu8yS8KRaXVrdFv6o3yR.jpg)

![20260607_132726.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/markone85/23uQmvWxmX2LMtrb2qaxbdUAZNGsjSRL21ZAs4gh2bqDVh2LpmpM6JJdmrY9JaZoaT2fH.jpg)
The park is quite well laid out, with plenty of paths and signs. And there are several fountains, which is extremely important for refreshment in the summer.
![20260607_132941.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/markone85/23xyQmN5T6H2zDjFA6rfMfDK6XKvoRJEFjsQ5GBU3YjPFDFrxidRfVLzzvVVHcTejiR8M.jpg)

![20260607_133012.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/markone85/EpzwoEUwc3KdDPEStJH4ExRXsW35SHjX5UBrTUAqitaw2gEncmUb2DhVHxfifoussGe.jpg)
This inconspicuous canal is actually part of the Borkovac stream.My son immediately set out to explore the surroundings.
![20260607_133948.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/markone85/23z7HnMwT9GXuwPoTgfodtRR1ufRggQyXgus8m9cmS8KnZ8MhS3ghvCkY2KTT5oqsFthf.jpg)

![20260607_133951.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/markone85/23zGeS1nW7yvUqcfMVsYSXsAQE3ZgMBdGoXY3rqj5TE1wPjT9WLLNDi5e2LUPzfjvszpi.jpg)
The grass along the path has been mowed, so the walk is truly pleasant in the beautifully landscaped park.
![20260607_133956.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/markone85/23xAVYRrxY9ASZ9cP7y6CMpaLZaiaiwUuwjB7s3Pu3BxApasmsZ5xJrVDzGrnfKsrAxLZ.jpg)

![20260607_134032.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/markone85/23wMRrpV7wX5bRJ5YGnDnQusNf94mqa8LHLN8J8NfZkQdnLXcgwm6swUFrAFpWD7pBsGv.jpg)
The name originally belonged to a stream that springs from the southern slopes of Fruška Gora and flows down towards Ruma. This stream is so historically important for the city that, together with the streams Kudoš and Jelenci, it has been on the official coat of arms of Ruma since 1749. Later, when the lake and park were built, it was forested and inherited the name from the stream, and the place itself is full of pine trees.
![20260607_134036.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/markone85/23zbKEtaJVSKqhXdXVqSjShnQ98Ybpx376oTgA7EjiVnMugakPhYTDC7SPCpYyxZTBQTc.jpg)

![20260607_134439.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/markone85/23xeZ5VuW7QdAW74YKXMyuY6U3wsEKFCtUCqoJrF5i9HC55ZPcd4UEsRs4EZtn6AqaHG9.jpg)
We climbed a small hill with a beautiful view of the lake.
![20260607_135908.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/markone85/EqDj72Crkb3k13k8Eh1nBS4KpLPMMCbYesSm9CRrUFMWXQHw7spaXbd7e8tb4ExFfs5.jpg)

There are also a lot of trees here.In addition to its original purpose for land irrigation, today it is an important tourist destination for all lovers of nature and fishing.
![20260607_135121.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/markone85/Eonk53BwzYKjjhzhfo8ySh8izkp6hziiWwpQshA5tdAbFfzSQfFtwgzJxGxh6BbUKzS.jpg)

It is extremely rich in various types of fish, so every year at the beginning of May a fishing competition is organized.There are catfish, perch, carp, babushka, white fish, grass carp and largemouth bass.
![20260607_144429.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/markone85/Ep7ubXnhmGt1fZzv4Vg5KE7xJ2iujCtPoeScMQkpWGe9ox5QyU8f3QBdE9uQ6oxMLMb.jpg)

The access to the part where the beach \

is inconvenient for a car. Luckily we were on foot, part of the road, the descent to the beach itself, was destroyed, so if your car is not high or an SUV, I do not recommend going down.
![20260607_144433.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/markone85/EpEGLMQ72HDEv4XTiDZt32LoGhvSDU1xfCdk2M5L1LcxaTXeR9xbmmZSAeJ3YBtQuwK.jpg)

It's ok for fishing and hiking, but not for swimming, so I don't really know.
The water is transparent up to half a meter deep.

A water bloom was observed in the lake, in which blue-green bacteria from the genera Phormidium, Microcystis and Aphanisomenon, as well as the dinoflagellate Ceratium hirundinella participate. ,,Simeunović, J., Svirčev, Z., Krstić, S., Lazić, L. 2005. Occurrence of Cyanobacterial Blooms in Vojvodina Water Ecosystems. Geographica Pannonica 9: 13–19. [Link](https://sr.wikipedia.org/sr-el/%D0%91%D0%BE%D1%80%D0%BA%D0%BE%D0%B2%D0%B0%D1%86_(%D1%98%D0%B5%D0%B7%D0%B5%D1%80%D0%BE)),,


![20260607_144851.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/markone85/EqhNNpx6LazJ1uvsxTFyA6Di8Q39LePZstURcy6cJNGuH9JaVk6GAmKAqxKkQZr25ng.jpg)

---

Thanks for reading.
Until next time.
Stay healthy.
Markone85.

body.title: The Pragnell Tiara
body.body:
Pragnell are a family-owned English jewellers that have been in business for 170 years.

The Pragnell Tiara is owned by the family (and thus not for sale), and was made by them in the late Edwardian period. It's made of diamonds and pearls and features a greek key motif combined with laurel wreaths in the Edwardian style.


![Untitled.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmXv8nFUig5t5wDF3j4szaSLeB9iHvvBdmprXGi9na7ACv/Untitled.jpg)

[source](https://pbs.twimg.com/media/HKIfqNcWQAAlR8Z?format=jpg&name=small)

It made an unexpected appearance yesterday at the second wedding of Peter Phillips (Princess Anne's son) to Harriet Stirling. The couple had bought their engagement ring at Pragnells, and borrowed the Pragnell Tiara just for the day.


![Untitled1.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmd5EHHik2FWBcgrVzN6qsFcnPyyoFqcaTPW5jBx8iX1eP/Untitled1.jpg)

body.body: <div class=\

> Happy and blessed start to the week to all my Hive friends! I'm grateful to share a new post here in the #hivegarden community, where I'm sharing great photos and updates on the growth of my tomato seedlings, as well as the sweet pepper plants we have at home. And last but not least, there are the lemon plants, which I really hope will grow so I can have them here at home. ![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmaqKsSfDrSq75qSYssbHPhbozaCx2u2AMmP3xcz9ArtC3/1780941016109.jpg) To begin my post, here are the tomato plants, which still need to be transplanted into individual plastic cups. This will make it easier to move them to the containers where I want to plant them, since I don't want to plant them directly in the ground yet. I need to try out different techniques that I've been told about and see if I can have any success. ![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmefE4wnDsUmuuxqtudmN2gaJfueevFfMXckh8BSAJ7Cmx/1780940923062.jpg) ![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmP4CMBoTdzVef8jdDuBJGNJJJaRe1y3fW7agGnpiyvtai/1780940923457.jpg) ![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmdnVBvxX7uGMNy6Vhj7As8G4oj5h7iNC3kCRTDgWNugCD/1780940923736.jpg) There's also this sweet pepper plant, which I have here at home and showed in a previous post. It has grown quite a bit, but it hasn't produced any fruit yet. However, it does have a large number of flowers, which, if all goes well, will soon become peppers that we can use in our cooking. ![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmZRKNVERqHJKXec6H3a11XswKRbizzdvasiaVrqfDLSij/1780940952666.jpg) ![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmPTL5pqyKqsP5bBzKEBQyjPUQx541gv4JiD8tXoB9bG9G/1780940952954.jpg) ![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmXUCvz29N6aPPLoW2pXgjUKPHhYx36JoWpsVkMHNYDv5r/1780940953193.jpg) ![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmdcHupdfob9Vumhzvvty7ZCDry6ygincc7X47tCmSufHo/1780940953457.jpg) Finally, and perhaps most importantly, these are the ones I consider most important because having a lemon at home is always a big help. However, lately I've noticed that the ones I have growing individually haven't grown enough; on the contrary, they're drying out. Perhaps it's because of too much water, although I'm not entirely sure, but something could be harming them. ![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmTVepmkaa4jyFg2CEHqs5fsV5eJWziiNjcUfgJd8S93fw/1780940985734.jpg) ![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmUeTPYx32eHEUfJqBS79sfYz2qaez3dHFL4TmPJWbscSD/1780940986014.jpg) ![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmULHjRxcjNKVN87ByAEWs6TRbzjb9jQdTAneBTcDwS7vE/1780940986248.jpg) I'll say goodbye now, but not before thanking you for the support you've given my posts here in the #hivegarden community, which is one of my favorites because I'm passionate about gardening.

body.title: The sixth sense? [EN/PT]
body.body: ![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmV2EUwmqu6xeK7XXyCtWusoFXai1hTr4FNdEe2L2AKqwn/image.png)\n\n<div class=\
>\n\nPeople say that a person's sixth sense is, in fact, instinct: the ability to sense that something is about to happen, relying only on that \

lingering in the air or perhaps on something more closely related to faith. Simply following your instinct and believing that things will work out. Instinct seems to be something beyond our understanding, a feeling, a sixth sense, or perhaps something even more intuitive.

My mother has always been good at this. She seems able to predict things, to sense when something is wrong. I remember one time when my friends and I were planning a party. Everyone was really excited about it, we had arranged everything perfectly, and when the day finally arrived, my mother told me not to go because she had a bad feeling about it. Her instinct was telling her that I shouldn't go and, like any good disobedient young man, I went anyway and, well, things did not end well.

Someone who had not been invited to the party was heading home after being turned away when a few police officers stopped him and found drugs in his possession. The officers asked where he was coming from and, well, he said he had come from our party, which technically wasn't a lie. He just forgot to mention that he had never been invited and had never actually entered the party. Things got out of control that day, and everyone who was present ended up at the police station. Even months later, I still had to go back there a few times to give statements. But all of that trouble could have been avoided if I had listened to my mother (or if that uninvited guest had never shown up in the first place). How did she know it could end badly? Pure instinct.

Maybe I inherited this trait from my mother, not exactly the ability to predict events that may end badly, but a certain intuition when it comes to people. Can I call it intuition or instinct? In some ways yes, and in some ways no, but I believe I'm good at reading people and, when that ability fails, intuition takes over. Describing it sounds a bit like a \

in the positive sense of the word, of course, but most of the time this way of seeing people turns out to be right. I can't really explain how it works, but it certainly seems to be one of those characteristics associated with intuition, instinct, and things of that nature.

I trust my instincts completely in many situations, but especially when it comes to people. I rarely get it wrong. I may sometimes misjudge something, pay too little attention to one detail or too much attention to another, but most of the time I'm right and even I am impressed by that ability. Perhaps it is a combination of factors that created this efficiency: something inherited from my mother, personal experiences, or pure survival instinct. Who knows... All I know is that it works, and I'm glad it does, because when reason fails or I find myself in a moment of doubt, that instinct gives me direction, the answer, or something very close to it. Maybe everyone has a little bit of this, they just don't pay attention to it. And for those who know they have it, well, use it wisely and don't waste it!

Dizem que o sexto sentido das pessoas é, de fato, o instinto: presumir que algo está para acontecer, basear-se apenas nessa \

que fica no ar ou em algo mais relacionado com a fé. Simplesmente seguir seu instinto e acreditar que as coisas vão dar certo. O instinto parece ser, de fato, algo que está além da nossa compreensão, um sentimento, um sexto sentido ou algo mais sensitivo?

Minha mãe sempre foi boa nisso, parece que consegue prever algo, sente que algo está errado. Me lembro de uma vez que meus amigos e eu estávamos planejando uma festa. Todos estavam bem ansiosos por isso, tínhamos combinado tudo perfeitamente e, quando o dia finalmente chegou, minha mãe disse para eu não ir, pois estava com uma espécie de mau pressentimento. Seu instinto estava dizendo que eu não deveria ir e então, como um bom jovem desobediente, eu fui e, bem, as coisas não terminaram nada bem.

Uma pessoa que não foi convidada para a festa estava voltando para casa depois de ser barrada, quando alguns policiais o abordaram e encontraram drogas com ele. Os policiais perguntaram de onde ele estava vindo e, bem, ele disse que estava vindo da nossa festa, o que de fato não era mentira. Ele só esqueceu de dizer que não foi convidado nem entrou na festa. As coisas saíram do controle naquele dia e todas as pessoas que estavam presentes foram parar na delegacia e, mesmo depois de alguns meses, ainda tive que comparecer por lá algumas vezes para prestar depoimento. Mas todo esse problema teria sido evitado se eu tivesse escutado minha mãe ( ou se esse penetra não estivesse dado as caras por lá). Como ela sabia que isso poderia acabar mal? Puro instinto.

Talvez eu tenha herdado essa qualidade da minha mãe, não exatamente para prever eventos que podem acabar mal, mas uma certa intuição referente a pessoas. Posso chamar de intuição ou instinto? Em partes sim e em partes não, mas acredito que sou bom em ler pessoas e, quando essa leitura falha, entra a intuição. Descrever isso soa como um \

, no bom sentido, óbvio, mas, em grande parte, essa forma de ver as pessoas quase sempre está certa. Não sei descrever exatamente como isso acontece, mas de fato deve ser uma característica quando vamos descrever coisas relacionadas à intuição, instinto e essas coisas. Eu confio totalmente no meu instinto para muitas coisas e ocasiões, mas principalmente quando é referente a pessoas. Raramente eu erro. Posso até medir algo de forma errada, ser menos atento a algo ou atento sem necessidade a outra coisa, mas normalmente eu acerto e até eu fico impressionado com essa destreza. Talvez seja um conjunto de fatores que determinaram essa eficiência: uma herança da mamãe, experiências próprias ou puro instinto de sobrevivência? Vai saber... Mas só sei que funciona e que bom que funciona, pois quando o racional falha ou tenho aquele momento de dúvida, esse instinto me dá a direção, a resposta ou algo bem próximo disso. Talvez todos tenham um pouco disso, apenas não sejam atentos. Puedo oler su aroma mientras estoy aquí sentada pensando en el tema del reto ZAPFIC Monday de esta semana. El «café» es un placer universal que muchos disfrutan. Quería centrar mi historia en aquellas personas que quizá no puedan disfrutar de esta bebida por diversas razones, entre ellas el precio. Espero que os guste mi historia.

El reto ZAPFICMonday fue creado por @felt.buzz y consiste en una historia contada en 240 caracteres o menos. Si te interesa, visita el post del reto actual: [It's Monday 8th June 2026! Time for #ZapFicMonday: ZapFic240! The \

**El cliente atento**

Aquella fresca mañana, los clientes no se fijaron en Otis, sentado en el rincón más alejado del Bela's Cafe.

Frotándose las manos desnudas, se quedó mirando al interior y luego apoyó la cabeza sobre los brazos cruzados.

Unos instantes después, se levantó, atraído por el aroma del café y un bagel.

La empatía en acción.

body.body:
Right now AI is too expensive or too risky to be used by businesses at a high scale. But costs will be driven down like anything in technology, and then the really powerful integrated systems will come out and many people won't be needed for supervision either. In fact, even now early adopters build tiered architectures where they (humans) are like the CEOs communicating directly only with a supervising agent (depending on how complex their architecture gets, it can be a sort of a CTO on top of team leaders who are in charge of worker agents or it can be directly a team leader for a less complex architecture).

Very soon we'll have OS's with fully integrated AIs, as in, workflows can be controlled by the OS's agent(s). That keeps people in the loop, unless the device is programmed to run fully automated, and we will see that as well.

Specialized AIs will likely be much more powerful than the current generalized (and even specialized) LLMs. We see that with Tesla and its automated driving system. I'm hearing quite impressive things about specialized AIs in the medical field.

So yeah, generally, people haven't been replaced yet as workers or supervisors, but it's likely we will see major shifts the following years.

body.body: yes, exactly that.\nThat is the whole idea: stop running HiveFest as its own separate thing and fold it into ChainCulture. One free, open, one-day conference with two tracks, and one of those tracks is HiveFest, the dedicated Hive space. Same Hivers, same talks and workshops, but now sitting inside a room full of people who turned up for something broader. You nailed the framing: \

That is precisely it.\nAnd that is exactly where the effort and the money go. Organising the ChainCulture day is the thing that pulls people in, from EBC, from Barcelona, from other chains and the maker and art scene. They come for ChainCulture and then bump straight into the Hive track. The reach is the product, and producing that day is the real work. HiveFest on its own does not draw new faces, you saw the difference yourself last year.\nA few small Hive-focused bits would hang off it: maybe a tiny hackathon, and a breakfast roundtable the morning after where HiveFest folks dig into actually improving Hive together. But the core is that one ChainCulture day, with Hive unmissable inside it. Networking with new people, like you said, is the whole point.

body.title: My Variegated Alocasia Macrorrhiza EN-SP
body.body:
**Lessons learned**


![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmeY5vTJCmv4HVMHLoCXTQprbe46PCTbe54TpuePrN11Nh/img_3727.png)


I have been working with my Variegated Alocasia Macrorrhiza for a while now, and I really wanted to share how it is doing in My Petit Edén Jardín. It is a plant that demands attention, and I have had to learn a lot about what it needs to stay happy.

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmPxsTcqLrBE77XMQWBjPe6EkCbQZ2jx9557LVDmt8YDUt/img_3648.jpg)


At first, I struggled a bit. These plants are very sensitive to their environment. I noticed that if the spot is too dark, it loses its variegation, but if the sun is too strong, the white parts of the leaves just burn. Finding that \

took some time and a few brown edges on my leaves.
Regarding the care, here is what I have learned through experience:

 **The Watering Routine:** This is the most important part. I found that a chunky, well-draining mix is essential. I prefer to keep the soil slightly moist, like a wrung-out sponge. If I let it dry out too much, the older leaves turn yellow, but if I overdo it, the roots suffer. It is all about finding that balance. This time a year it's raining regularly, so nature does the job for me.

 **Cleaning the leaves:** Since the leaves are huge, they collect a lot of dust. I clean them gently with a damp cloth every week. This helps the plant \

and look much better.

 **Humidity and Air:** I try to keep her in a place where the air circulates, but without direct drafts from fans or A/C units, which dry out the foliage very quickly.

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmfAXV5eTsTJydVrJapWqLJNZMLVDmxZgDFgHysfRBrzNt/img_3642.jpg) *A whole variegated leaf*

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmQ8yVV74TAk184AW1cgU6gYJV9rziycpPvWjdtpb9LcnW/img_3643.jpg)

Even though it can be a headache sometimes, seeing a new leaf unfurl with those beautiful patterns is the best reward. It’s part of the day-to-day life here in the garden.

Every new leaf is happiness unfolding to my eyes which I enjoy with a cup of infusion.

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmavLVtiqrrxKWqV2h5mXVmasXYn92uXaXqM8uq41sSMnX/img_3644.jpg)

**How's everything with your alocasias?**

🌱🌱🌱🌱🌱🌱🌱🌱🌱🌱🌱🌱🌱🌱🌱

Pictures are taken by me in My Petit Eden Jardín 
This Alocasia was a gift from @iscandel 

☀️☀️☀️☀️☀️☀️☀️☀️☀️☀️☀️☀️☀️☀️☀️☀️

**SP**

**Lo que he aprendido**

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmeY5vTJCmv4HVMHLoCXTQprbe46PCTbe54TpuePrN11Nh/img_3727.png)

Llevo un tiempo trabajando con mi Alocasia Macrorrhiza Variegata y por fin quería compartir cómo va todo aquí en My Petit Edén Jardín. Es una planta que pide mucha atención, y me ha tocado aprender bastante sobre lo que necesita para mantenerse bien.

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmPxsTcqLrBE77XMQWBjPe6EkCbQZ2jx9557LVDmt8YDUt/img_3648.jpg)

Al principio me costó un poco. Son plantas muy sensibles al entorno. Me di cuenta de que si el lugar es muy oscuro, pierde el variegado, pero si el sol es muy fuerte, las partes blancas de las hojas se queman enseguida. Encontrar ese \

me tomó tiempo y algunos bordes marrones en mis hojas.

Sobre los cuidados, esto es lo que he aprendido a base de experiencia:

 **El riego:** Es la parte más importante. Me he dado cuenta de que un sustrato grueso y con muy buen drenaje es fundamental. Prefiero mantener la tierra ligeramente húmeda, como una esponja bien escurrida. Si la dejo secar demasiado, las hojas viejas se ponen amarillas, pero si me paso con el agua, las raíces sufren de una vez. Todo es cuestión de encontrar ese equilibrio. En esta época del año llueve regularmente, así que la naturaleza hace mi trabajo. 

 **Limpieza de hojas:** Como las hojas son enormes, acumulan mucho polvo. Las limpio suavemente con un paño húmedo cada semana. Esto ayuda a que la planta \

y se vea mucho mejor.

 **Humedad y aire:** Intento tenerla en un lugar donde el aire circule, pero sin corrientes directas de abanicos o aires acondicionados, que secan el follaje muy rápido.

Aunque a veces da un poco de dolor de cabeza, ver cómo sale una hoja nueva con esos patrones tan bonitos es la mejor recompensa. Es parte de la vida diaria aquí en el jardín.

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmfAXV5eTsTJydVrJapWqLJNZMLVDmxZgDFgHysfRBrzNt/img_3642.jpg) *Una hoja totalmente variegada*

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmQ8yVV74TAk184AW1cgU6gYJV9rziycpPvWjdtpb9LcnW/img_3643.jpg)

Cada hoja nueva es felicidad que se despliega ante mis ojos que disfruto con una taza de infusión.

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmavLVtiqrrxKWqV2h5mXVmasXYn92uXaXqM8uq41sSMnX/img_3644.jpg)

**Que tal te va con tus alocacias?**

🌱🌱🌱🌱🌱🌱🌱🌱🌱🌱🌱🌱🌱🌱🌱

Las fotos son tiradas por mi en My Petit Eden Jardín.

body.title: Why I'm Choosing to Stay Single Today (Without Giving Up on Love)
body.body: data-align=\
>If you had the power to choose your path right now—free from social pressures, without the ticking biological clock looming over you, and without fear of what others might say—<span class=\
style=\
>would you choose to stay single, or would you prefer to be in a relationship?
data-align=\

>This question kept running through my head as I read the community’s weekly initiative; check it out here. We live in a contradictory society: on the one hand, we romanticize singlehood as the only path to success and independence; on the other, we’re bombarded with the idea that absolute happiness is achieved by finding your soulmate.

\n\n
alt=\
/>\n\n
data-align=\

>If you ask me, my honest answer today is rooted in reality. After being in a relationship where I experienced the two most painful aspects of modern relationships—the manipulation of “love bombing” at the beginning and the complete emotional abandonment through “ghosting” at the end—I learned to redefine my boundaries. After surviving the confusion of going from being on cloud nine to absolute silence overnight, I realized that my peace of mind is non-negotiable. That’s why I prefer being single—because I value my time alone without feeling empty.
data-align=\

>This doesn’t mean I reject love, but rather that I’m fascinated by the life I’ve built for myself. I value my time alone without feeling empty; I enjoy the freedom to spend a weekend reading, sitting in a park sipping a milkshake, and just relaxing—to go for a walk without having to explain where I’m going, to write in silence without seeking approval, and to treat myself without having to negotiate a single moment.

\n\n
alt=\
/>\n\n
data-align=\

>Our generation was raised to believe that being single was a temporary state—a waiting room before our real life began—and that is a huge mistake. Today I know that being single isn’t a refuge to escape commitment, but a fertile, complete, and very intimate space to get to know ourselves and figure out exactly what we’re not willing to compromise on. In my case, this stage has allowed me to build a solid foundation and embrace who I am, preparing me for what I truly want to be in the future.

\n\n
alt=\
/>\n\n
data-align=\

>If I decided to be in a relationship tomorrow, the big difference is that I wouldn’t do it out of desperation anymore. I’m not looking for my soulmate, because I feel like I’m a whole person. If someone comes into my life, it’s not to fill emotional voids or heal childhood wounds, but to expand and enrich who I am. For me, romantic love is mainly about three things:

\n\n1.
data-align=\
><span class=\
style=\

>Mutual growth: Inspiration and a genuine desire to evolve together.

\n2.
data-align=\
><span class=\
style=\

>Reciprocity and tenderness: A connection that ignites the mind.

\n3.
data-align=\
><span class=\
style=\

>Space to be: Someone with whom to share life without feeling like I have to shrink or justify my needs to keep the peace. Love is not a cage.

\n\n
alt=\
/>\n\n
data-align=\

>I don’t want a relationship just to fill the silence, ease the fear of loneliness, or meet the typical social expectation of getting married, having children, and following a monotonous script. I choose a conscious, secure, and reciprocal relationship over using loneliness as a shield. I don’t want just any relationship, nor just anyone by my side, and I’m not afraid of being seen as “too picky.”
data-align=\
>The most mature decision isn’t to rush into a relationship or swear we’ll never have one. The real victory is being able to look in the mirror and say, “<span class=\
style=\

>I’m okay with myself, and precisely because of that, I allow myself to wait for a relationship that’s truly worth it.”

\n\n
alt=\
/>\n\n
alt=\
/>\n\n
>
data-align=\
>Si tuvieras el poder de elegir tu camino en este momento, sin presiones sociales, sin el reloj biológico asechando y sin el miedo al qué dirán <span class=\
style=\
>¿Elegirías quedarte soltera o preferirías estar en una relación?
data-align=\
>Esta pregunta me dio vueltas en la cabeza al leer la iniciativa semanal de la comunidad, consúltala <a target=\
rel=\
class=\
href=\

>aquí. Vivimos en una sociedad contradictoria: por un lado, nos romantizan la soltería como el único espacio de éxito e independencia; por el otro, nos bombardean con la idea de que la felicidad absoluta se alcanza encontrando una media naranja.

\n\n
alt=\
/>\n\n
data-align=\

>Si me lo preguntan a mí, mi respuesta honesta hoy, tiene un trasfondo real. Después de haber tenido una relación en la que experimenté las dos caras más dolorosas de los vínculos modernos -la manipulación del love bombing al inicio y la total responsabilidad afectiva ausente con el ghosting al final- aprendí a redefinir mis límites. Tras sobrevivir a la confusión de pasar de los altares al silencio absoluto de un día para otro, entendí que mi paz no es negociable. Por eso prefiero mi soltería, porque valoro mi tiempo a solas sin sentirme vacía.
data-align=\

>Esto no significa que rechace el amor, sino porque me fascina la vida que he construido por mi cuenta. Valoro mi tiempo a solas sin sentirme vacía; me gusta la libertad de disfrutar un fin de semana leyendo, en un parque y tomándome una malta, y estar relajada, caminar sin tener que explicar mi ruta, escribir en silencio sin buscar aprobación y consentirme sin tener que negociar un instante.

\n\n
alt=\
/>\n\n
data-align=\

>Generacionalmente nos educaron que estar soltera era un estado provisional una sala de espera antes de que empezara nuestra verdadera vida, y es un gran error. Hoy sé que la soltería no es un refugio para huir del compromiso, sino un lugar fértil, completo y muy íntimo para reconocernos y saber exactamente qué cosas no estamos dispuestas a negociar. En mi caso, esta etapa me ha permitido construir bases sólidas y fluir con quién soy, preparándome para lo que realmente quiero ser en el futuro.

\n\n
alt=\
/>\n\n
data-align=\

>Si mañana decidiera estar en una relación, la gran diferencia es que ya no lo haría desde la urgencia. No busco a mi media naranja, porque siento que soy una persona entera. Si alguien llega a mi vida, no es para cubrir vacíos emocionales, para tapar heridas de la infancia, sino para expandirme y multiplicar quién soy. Para mí, el amor en pareja se trata de 3 cosas principalmente:

\n\n1.
data-align=\
><span class=\
style=\

>Crecimiento mutuo: Inspiración y ganas reales de evolucionar juntos.

\n2.
data-align=\
><span class=\
style=\

>Reciprocidad y ternura: Una conexión que encienda la mente.

\n3.
data-align=\
><span class=\
style=\

>Espacio para ser: Alguien con quien compartir la vida sin sentir que debo encogerme o justificar mis necesidades para mantener la paz. El amor no es una jaula.

\n\n
alt=\
/>\n\n
data-align=\

>No quiero un vínculo para llenar silencios, aliviar el miedo a la soledad o cumplir con la típica expectativa social de casarse, tener hijos y seguir un guion monótono. Elijo una relación consciente, segura y recíproca antes que usar la soledad como una armadura. No quiero cualquier vínculo, ni cualquier persona a mi lado, y no me da miedo que me vean como \
.
data-align=\
>La decisión más madura no es correr hacia una relación ni jurar que nunca la tendremos. La verdadera victoria es poder mirar al espejo y decir: <span class=\
style=\

.

\n\n
alt=\
/>\n\n
alt=\
/>\n\n
>
></center>

body.title: I Ran 10Km then I had a Swim Before my Shift ( also powered up 5 HP)
body.body:
Yesterday there was a semi marathon in La Marsa, which is a costal neighborhood in the northern outskirts of Tunis. I woke up early (around 5:30 AM), had my breakfast and went to La marsa. We had some warm up and some animation then we started running. I haven't ran any long distances for the last months but I didn't feel any pain. Maybe the occasional biking I do helped with that. I started getting tired by the time we reached the hill of Gammarth after about 3 Km. I was about to give up and walk uphill then I saw these guys. ![](https://usermedia.actifit.io/e551d679-edd8-4ad4-b00c-4ad85724b4fb.jpg) These are the pacekeepers for 10Km per hour. One guy was running with them halding a big speaker with loud songs. If he could keep up with the pace holding that heavy thing, so can I. I thought to myself. My heavy thing being the overweight I only notice when it's unconvinieny. Meaning when I'm doing sports. I failed to keep up with them but I succeeded in running till the end. I made a resolution that no matter the pace, I have to keep running till the end. No stopping and no walking. Except for the three stop where they provide us with drinks and other stuff to recharge. The view of course helped motivate me. I was looking at the sea all the way, eager to reach the finish line and have a swim. I tried to record the activity via actifit but the app glitched and paused after less than a Km. But luckily Actifit came through and recorded 23917. I should have used actifit's new tracking feature. ![](https://usermedia.actifit.io/e927a8f1-6b94-43ca-933d-804982f676d3.jpg) La Marsa beach isn't the best in Tunisia but it was convinient to have it right at the finish line. It was actually nice this time of the year. Very clean and calm. But the water was still cold unlike late in the summer. After a quick swim I went back to the finish line where there was a fun animation anf some giveaways. Free snacks and drinks and all. People from all over the world participated as usual. ![](https://usermedia.actifit.io/252cad73-e78f-4ea4-b4da-bec29404bfd0.jpg) The event is a yearly marathon called Run of Heroes, organised to raise money to help treat children from cancer. Last year, according to their official website, they helped 140 families with their struggle against cancer. ![](https://usermedia.actifit.io/9c313405-7a7e-4de3-8a67-2cac97dfc115.jpg)
_This report was published via Actifit app ([Android](https://bit.ly/actifit-app) | [iOS](https://bit.ly/actifit-ios)). Check out the original version [here on actifit.io](https://actifit.io/@hazem91/actifit-hazem91-20260608t174039078z)_

body.title: HIVE THRIVE— Show #59 —Guest: @worldmappin
body.body:
Hive Thrive #59: Our Hour for Hive Community

![2fdaf271-b47e-4c99-8845-d16ec9a9f519.jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/buttcoins/23wqknBgrfSAyzhxsCxhiss2ocYL2xyPg5ooEv6BkBo9v92yujPpEFYjvEm6xbuii9jXE.jpeg)


Tuesday, June 9
6 PM UTC
Live in the Hive Thrive Discord

Hosts: @alessandrawhite and @buttcoins
Guests: @detlev and @lizanomadsoul from @worldmappin

This week on Hive Thrive, we are joined by the Worldmappin team to talk about one of Hive’s most visible community projects: a global, interactive map where Hive travel posts, local discoveries, food posts, HBD locations, and community stories can be explored by place.

Worldmappin recently released its 2026 Transparency and Strategy Report, following the launch of Worldmappin V2. We will talk about the map, the travel community, the daily curation work, the new version, the role of @asgarth and the wider development team, and the future roadmap.

What We’ll Dig Into

* What Worldmappin actually is, beyond “that map thing”
* Why travel content still matters on Hive
* What changed with Worldmappin V2
* How the team handles curation, quality, spam, and daily operations
* The role of @detlev, @lizanomadsoul, and @asgarth in keeping the project moving
* What happened with the DHF proposal and the recent defunding
* How much the project costs to run now
* What “transparency” should actually mean, not just as a nice word in a title
* Whether Hive projects should be expected to survive without DHF support
* The uncomfortable but necessary questions around HiveFest, event spending, and community value
* What Worldmappin needs next from Hive users, voters, and witnesses

This will not be a courtroom. Nobody is getting dragged into the village square and pelted with stale downvotes.

But we also are not going to pretend the questions are not in the air.

Hive is having broader conversations right now about funding, sustainability, accountability, events, and what kind of projects deserve long-term support. Worldmappin sits right inside that conversation, so we want to give the team space to explain what they are building, what has worked, what has been difficult, and where they think the project goes from here.

As always, Hive Thrive is a weekly town hall for the Hive community. It is casual, open, and built around direct conversation with the people building, curating, experimenting, and sometimes taking a few arrows while trying to move Hive forward.

Bring questions. Bring curiosity. Bring your slightly suspicious but still hopeful Hive brain.

body.title: 8 June 2026, Freewriters Community Daily Writing Prompt Day 3128: mosaic of life
body.body:
Human existence can be thought of as a mosaic: a set of diverse pieces that, when put together, reveal a unique and meaningful image. Each fragment—small or large, luminous or opaque—contributes its shape and color to the whole.

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmaFR7AkRxg1WWT7jV5hAwjQKzS6CphvvwYTx8C8LUXyKf/img_20251017_wa0024.jpg)



In that mosaic are the moments of joy, which shine like golden tiles; the moments of pain, which resemble dark stones but necessary to provide contrast; the relationships we cultivate, which are intertwined pieces forming patterns of companionship and affection. There are also learnings, which add texture and depth, and dreams, which brighten the edges with vibrant hues.

Life is not a uniform picture, but a composition made of diversity. Every day he adds a new piece, sometimes unexpected, that modifies the design and forces us to look at the whole again. What seemed like a mistake can become an essential nuance; What seemed insignificant can be the detail that gives harmony to the whole.

The mosaic reminds us that beauty is not in the perfection of each fragment, but in the way they are integrated. Thus, our contradictions, our lights and shadows, become part of a greater work. Patience and acceptance are the hands that place each piece in its place, and time is the artisan who reveals the final drawing.

Credits: The image is mine and I used Google translator.

body.body:
Hello, guys!

So yesterday, I went to church as usual, and it was the first Sunday in June, and the time for preaching or message came, the theme was introduced, and it was compelling and suited at the right time for me. My pastor mentioned a prayer push. And he went further to mention that every prophetic word equips a man with a responsibility to pray out that prophecy.





![1000807273.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/peckypeace/AL7QcxQW7EbFAooBJohj69gtepeNjHC7bCWHA5f3eCKVJVyLWWQH28LjcEnu6y3.png)


[Source](https://pixabay.com/vectors/muslim-prayer-pray-mosque-islam-7059888/)


Many believers, celebrate prophecy a lot without enforcing it through prayers, celebrating it will not bring it to actualization but dormant. What will activate or bring it to manifestation is prayers. 

What are the things that will help us to warfare in other for the prophecies to come into reality. 

* You need the right word. 

Just like what happened to Mary in the scripture and the angel of the lord appeared into her and said that she will carry a son in her womb and she replied that she doesn't know any man. How shall that be?

She held unto this word and have faith in God that it will surely come to pass.

>Romans 10:17 So then faith cometh by hearing, and hearing by the word of God.

So hearing the word is very powerful and using it to pray about your prophecy is very important and to stay on it. 

* The second thing to help you war is crying for the mercy of the Lord. 

>Hebrews 4:16 Let us therefore come boldly unto the throne of grace, that we may obtain mercy, and find grace to help in time of need.

Obtain the mercy of the Lord. Let God's mercy speak for your situation and go ahead of you.


* The third thing is to enforce it
>James 5:16 Confess your faults one to another, and pray one for another, that ye may be healed. The effectual fervent prayer of a righteous man availeth much.

The fervent prayer of the righteous man avail much. Fervency is the compelling power from the inside or inward  energized power of a man. Fervency doesn't start from the outside. People pray with a loud voice or shouting the prayer doesn't mean it's fervent. It's needs to come from inside.

These are the ways to bring God's prophecy over your life your reality.

Thank you very much.

body.body:

*My England World Cup Run 😂*

Bro I picked England for International Cup mode and the game didn’t play at all. Immediately I clicked it, it removed every player that wasn’t English from my squad. All my Mbappe, Vinicius, De Bruyne... gone. Then it loaned me England players so I could even fill my team. So my starting 11 became Palmer, Foden, Bellingham, Saka... full Three Lions only. No Chelsea, no Arsenal mix. It felt weird at first but also kind of cool, like I was actually Gareth Southgate.

I’m in Group L and my group is Ghana, Croatia, and one other team. First match was vs Croatia and I just wanted to test things. I set difficulty to Beginner because I didn’t want stress. Big mistake 😂 I ended up winning 13-0. Palmer scored like 4 goals, Saka was dancing on their defenders, Bellingham was everywhere. It didn’t even feel like football again. Their defense was just standing. I kept thinking “this can’t be World Cup sha”. But it was fun to see all those England passes connect since the game forced me to use only them.

But I know Beginner level is just vibes. Once I move to Legendary or World Class, Croatia with Modric and Ghana with Kudus will punish me if I play like that. Still, 13-0 to start the group means my Palmer experiment is working. Now I just have to manage with only England players till the final. No buying, no transfers. If my LB is trash, I’ll suffer with him. That’s the real World Cup feeling.

You copying my Palmer tactic for your next game vs Ghana?

body.title: Some moments of joy of my son with kittens at my sister's house.
body.body: <div class=\

> ![IMG_20250807_171931~2.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmWdbC4K3Zq1ofxELUt7uw48PPmgQdAa53G8x1Q8zSWePc/IMG_20250807_171931~2.jpg) I hope you are all doing well. Today I am going to share with you the story of a very simple but very joyful experience in our life. A few days ago, we went to my sister's house with our family. After going there, a great surprise was waiting for us. There are some wonderful and very cute kittens at my sister's house. As soon as I saw these fluffy, soft and playful little kittens, my son was completely overwhelmed with joy. ![IMG_20250808_214939~2.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmX1FXaggwXBuGTwVwz2n4RkdMsq1EuowtAh7Q2SgCGrXm/IMG_20250808_214939~2.jpg) Those of you who love pets or cats at home must know how much positive energy their presence spreads in the mind. My son fell in love with them at first sight. The whole time, he was busy with them all the time. Sometimes he was holding them in his arms and lovingly caressing them, and sometimes he was running around the house after them. The playful nature of the kittens and the innocent joy of my son created a joyful atmosphere in the whole house. He really kept the whole house busy with them all the time. ![IMG_20250807_172004~2.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmYPFrkry4o8GeVYgShS8y9GNNghJw9EUZwovapDLG8U1J/IMG_20250807_172004~2.jpg) This innocent love between children and helpless animals is really worth seeing. In this busy mechanical life, some such beautiful moments refresh our minds for a moment. This day spent at my sister's house will be etched in my son's memory for a long time. I have shared some pictures of those beautiful moments with this post. Thank you very much for your valuable support. ___ |

body.title: The Chicken Get Bigger
body.body:
Hello Friends

Once a while I want to share something different, and this time please allow me to share one of my happy moments that I have recently. 

Last week I visited my workshop and I saw my chickens were getting bigger. Some of them even had reached adult size. So here were my chicken on the cage.

https://play.3speak.tv/embed?v=dewabrata/rbd9di82

Actually they were roosters lol. I was happy because usually they got killed when they were at 2-3 weeks old. People here usually only cared for the hens, because they laid eggs and that gave more economic value.

Male or roosters usually had no cage or coop. People let them lived freely and ended up as civet, monitor or snake food. I tried to convinced some of them to let small cockerels to grow up in coop, but always failed badly. They always shoved them out when I was not there, then I got back and found them gone.

So yeah, I was very happy to see some adult roosters or cockerels that time. I knew that finally I could have my own grown chicken soup lol. Roosters were better for soup, they gave better taste for the broth. 

Maybe young generation feels something wrong with me or older generation, we are happy in growing our livestocks, nurture them from offspring to adult size, then butcher them happily... I try to respect Vegan people, but sorry I could not do that here lol... Those roosters soon would be my chicken soup!!!

Anyway I wonder what @deraaa does nowadays. I recall the last time I talked to her it was about rising her chickens. I know she has retired from HIVE, so I hope she could be happy out there with her chicken. It's a rare sight to see young people happily rise chicken then eat them like me lol.

---

Thank you for coming and reading my post. I live in Jakarta, Capital City of Indonesia.  I used to live by making money online, that's why I like being here, on HIVE, and in #PIMP - (Paper In My Pocket) community. Feel Free to leave any comment below

body.title: A story of some murder with Guava and the girl.
body.body: <div class=\

> ![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmYFeirWvDSw5QN7bBUjjuVcSXrmyho7GeZMQsXW2Qm3Ef/1780939431341.jpg) Amidst the thousands of troubles of our busy lives, many of us forget that true happiness lies in the smallest moments. Today I had such a simple yet extraordinary moment with my daughter. Whether it's pouring rain outside or the scorching sun inside, any weather is sweeter if you have a loved one and a plate of fresh fruit. Today, our afternoon was sweetened with a plate of raw, ripe guava. On a lazy afternoon at home, I quickly cut up some guavas and arranged them on a plate. The raw green peel and the soft, white inside, along with a little bit of turmeric and a pinch of salt, are perfect. But the joy of eating with my daughter is different. Her excitement is palpable right from the moment she cuts the guava. When she picks up a piece of guava with her tiny hands and takes a bite, the smile of satisfaction on her face is incomparable. ![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmYd1WuEL5bcrigeDSKqcAZM4BHjGL5iSbie7hmFpNmxzZ/1780939431485.jpg) We not only sat at the table eating guava, but also had various stories and jokes. He was telling stories about his school, and I was fascinated by listening to all the grand happenings of his little world. Sometimes he would put down his piece and take a bigger piece from my plate. It's these sweet whims of children that make life beautiful. The wheel of time turns so fast that you can tell when children grow up No. So I try to keep these little memories in the depths of my mind. The main reason for sharing this simple moment with friends at Hive is so that we don't lose these precious moments in the rat race of mechanical life. Rather than taking our children to expensive toys or luxurious places. It's so important to sit with them and talk like this and spend quality time. This sweet afternoon of eating guava today will be fresh in my memory for a long time. 📸 Photography| Details 📸 |-|-| |Model|Realme-C53| |Location| Bangladesh|

body.title: TRUSTING YOUR INSTINCTS
body.body:
<div class=text-justify>

Do I trust my instincts? I am not sure I can answer a yes or a No because there have been times when I have been completely right, and there have been times when I have been completely wrong. Instead what I do is check my instincts. If there is something that I am sure of is that my instincts is revealing a depth in me that I have not noticed and instead of just doing what it is telling me, the best thing is to check it to see just what it is telling me to do and why it is telling me to do whatever it is. For example, if I suspect my partner is cheating and I go tell them they are cheating because my gut tells me so or my instincts preserves it then I will be setting myself up for emotional torture. A lot of the time I have seen these things happen and whether it’s true or not, the way to respond to it will either expose the truth, or destroy a relationship for life. Most of the time, the latter is what happens.

https://img.leopedia.io/DQmQ2GXAsTspUEbFubDn336WV823RytH58YEz55zuq5xoMt/10602788_42415.jpg 

<a href=\

>Image by macrovector on Magnific There are two ways it destroys things, one is you speaking negativity to live by continually suspecting my partner, the other way is showing them I do not trust them and thus making them feel unsafe. Although, if it turns out that my instinct is correct, I would have saved myself a lot of stress, but if I am wrong, then I am wrong. This is why I always verify what my instinct is actually telling me. Perhaps it’s telling me that I am insecure and need to work on my self esteem, perhaps it’s showing my fears and making me act on them. I can say for a fact that one of the many people who follow their guts a lot are gamblers, and guess what, they usually lose until they win. Some might never even win. This is because their instincts were only feeding their greed, and they mistook it for it, showing them the way. ![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmRDUCxsFHMDkYoRaNXkMUUuv9AgBHWz6BTZcGNSYN6ApX/rnfetchblobtmp_fgtcef2qubuke3qlh9re6s.jpg) Our instinct is like a 7th sense, it pushes us to make decisions promptly. But then again, just like how you can’t see clearly if something is in your eyes, or you can’t hear clearly is something is in your ear, or you can’t breathe well if something is in your nose, that’s how it is when something is blocking your instincts or making you think something is what it is not. Desires can block our instincts, our fears can trigger it, people's narrative could affect it, our upbringing could also affect it. This is why I try to always check what my instincts are really saying, instead of going in blindly and failing woefully. But then again this does not mean we should ignore that 7th sense when it speaks, in fact we should check it immediately else we will fall apart when it tells us something and we do not listen. >THIS IS MY RESPONSE TO HIVE LEARNER'S [PROMPT](https://discord.com/channels/928986840747372636/929001473231183873/1513478273395327027) FOR WEEK 221 EPISODE 1 ![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmYqbQGFerHXinrqqmfCGrRHtwdZRhqAtCVWMna3geK2vc/20230716_224852_0000.png) Posted Using [INLEO](https://inleo.io/@kilvnrex/trusting-your-instincts-fsb)
