body.title: Lo que aprendí demasiado tarde #4: Sobre dejarme siempre para el final | What I Learned Too Late #4: About always putting myself last
body.body: 🇪🇸 En Español * * * Lo que aprendí demasiado tarde #4 ================================= _Sobre dejarme siempre para el final_ ------------------------------------- * * *
alt=\

/> Fuente [Pixabay](https://pixabay.com/photos/adult-woman-portrait-window-black-3304306/) * * * > Hay costumbres que parecen virtudes durante muchos años, hasta que un día descubrimos cuánto nos han costado. * * * Hola querida comunidad de Holos & Lotus Desde muy joven me acostumbré a pensar primero en los demás. No recuerdo haber tomado esa decisión conscientemente. Simplemente fue ocurriendo poco a poco, hasta convertirse en una forma de vivir. Mis hermanas mayores ya trabajaban mientras yo todavía estudiaba. Tal vez por eso sentía la necesidad de aportar algo a la casa, aunque fuera poco. Estaba en una escuela becada y recuerdo que durante las jornadas de recogida de naranjas, aunque estaba prohibido sacarlas, escondía algunas en mi maletín para llevárselas a mis hermanas. No era gran cosa. Pero para mí significaba ayudar. Y de alguna manera, aquella necesidad de contribuir me acompañó durante toda la vida. Con el tiempo ayudé a mi hermana mayor en la crianza de mi sobrino. Después llegaron otras responsabilidades, otras etapas y otras personas importantes. Formé mi propia familia. Llegó mi esposo. Llegó mi hija. Y sin darme cuenta, seguí haciendo lo mismo que había aprendido desde joven: poner las necesidades de los demás antes que las mías. * * * Una costumbre que parecía normal -------------------------------- Durante muchos años ni siquiera me cuestioné esa manera de actuar. Me parecía lo correcto. Si había dinero para una sola cosa, normalmente era para alguien más. Si había que hacer un sacrificio, lo hacía yo. Si había que esperar para comprar algo personal, también esperaba yo. No porque mi familia me obligara. Al contrario. He tenido la suerte de compartir mi vida con personas que me quieren y me apoyan. Pero muchas veces fui yo misma quien se colocó al final de la lista. Y cuando una repite algo durante años, termina creyendo que es completamente normal. * * * > Me acostumbré tanto a ocupar el último lugar que dejé de darme cuenta de que también tenía necesidades. * * * Con el paso del tiempo entendí que no siempre se trata de grandes cosas. A veces son detalles muy sencillos. Posponer una compra necesaria. Ignorar un cansancio que lleva semanas acompañándonos. Dejar para después algo que nos gustaría hacer. Pensar que siempre habrá otro momento para nosotras. Y así pasan los años. Siempre ocupadas. Siempre pendientes de alguien más. Siempre resolviendo. Hasta que un día una se pregunta cuándo fue la última vez que se tuvo verdaderamente en cuenta. * * * Lo que entendí con los años --------------------------- Creo que muchas mujeres de mi generación crecimos con la idea de que ser buenas significaba sacrificarse constantemente. Y aunque el amor implica generosidad, también he aprendido que olvidarse completamente de una misma no es una virtud. Es un desequilibrio. Porque una también necesita cuidados. También necesita descanso. También necesita sentirse importante. Durante mucho tiempo pensé que dedicarme tiempo era una forma de egoísmo. Hoy lo veo de manera diferente. Entendí que cuidar de una misma no significa querer menos a la familia. No significa dejar de ayudar. No significa abandonar responsabilidades. Significa reconocer que una también forma parte de las personas que merecen atención. * * * > Con los años entendí que pensar en una misma no es egoísmo. También es una forma de respeto. * * * Quizás aprendí esta lección más tarde de lo que debía. Pero me alegra haberla aprendido. Porque ahora sigo disfrutando hacer cosas por las personas que amo, pero intento recordar algo que durante mucho tiempo olvidé: Yo también soy una de esas personas que necesitan cuidado. * * * Aprendí demasiado tarde que no debía esperar a estar completamente agotada para recordar que yo también era importante. Gracias por leer. * * * Las imágenes son de Pixabay. La versión en inglés fue hecha con DeepL Translate. * * * 🇬🇧 In English * * * What I Learned Too Late #4 ========================== _About always putting myself last_ ---------------------------------- * * *
alt=\

/>
Source [Pixabay](https://pixabay.com/photos/adult-woman-portrait-window-black-3304306/)

---

> Some habits seem like virtues for many years, until one day we realize how much they have cost us.

* * *

Hello dear Holos & Lotus community,

From a very young age, I got used to thinking about others first.

I do not remember consciously deciding to do that. It simply happened little by little until it became a way of life.

My older sisters were already working while I was still studying. Perhaps that is why I always felt the need to contribute something to the household, even if it was small. I attended a boarding school and I remember that during orange harvesting days, although it was forbidden to take any fruit out, I would hide a few oranges in my school bag to bring home to my sisters.

It was not much.

But to me, it meant helping.

And somehow, that need to contribute stayed with me throughout my life.

As time passed, I helped my older sister raise her son, my nephew. Later came other responsibilities, other stages of life, and other important people.

I built my own family.

My husband became part of my life.

Then my daughter arrived.

And without realizing it, I continued doing what I had learned when I was young: placing the needs of others before my own.

* * *

A habit that felt normal
------------------------

For many years, I never questioned that way of living.

It seemed like the right thing to do.

If there was money for only one thing, it usually went to someone else.

If a sacrifice had to be made, I made it.

If something personal had to wait, I was the one who waited.

Not because my family demanded it.

Quite the opposite.

I have been fortunate to share my life with people who love and support me.

But many times, I was the one placing myself at the bottom of the list.

And when you repeat something for years, it starts to feel completely normal.

* * *

> I became so used to being last that I stopped noticing I had needs too.

* * *

Over time, I realized that it is not always about big things.

Sometimes it is about simple details.

Postponing something you need.

Ignoring a tiredness that has been with you for weeks.

Putting off something you would enjoy.

Assuming there will always be another moment for yourself.

And that is how the years pass.

Always busy.

Always thinking about someone else.

Always solving problems.

Until one day you wonder when was the last time you truly considered yourself.

* * *

What I learned over the years
-----------------------------

I believe many women of my generation grew up believing that being good meant sacrificing themselves constantly.

And while love certainly involves generosity, I have also learned that completely forgetting about yourself is not a virtue.

It is an imbalance.

Because we also need care.

We also need rest.

We also need to feel important.

For a long time, I believed that dedicating time to myself was selfish.

Today I see it differently.

I understand that taking care of myself does not mean loving my family any less.

It does not mean helping less.

It does not mean abandoning responsibilities.

It simply means recognizing that I am also one of the people who deserves attention.

* * *

> Over the years, I learned that thinking about yourself is not selfish. It is also a form of self-respect.

* * *

Maybe I learned this lesson later than I should have.

But I am glad I learned it.

Because I still enjoy caring for the people I love, yet now I try to remember something I forgot for many years:

I am one of those people who deserves care too.

* * *

I learned too late that I should not have waited until complete exhaustion to remember that I mattered too.

Thank you for reading.

body.body:
![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmVAfMu99Hme6Cb9vBmnDxAjMMUJs2bx7XS1KmiqVsPURo/beige_scrapbook_vision_board_instagram_post.png)


Hay lecturas que te encuentran en el momento exacto, justo cuando la vida te acaba de dar una lección de frente. Eso me pasó hace unos días al leer una reflexión de nuestro apreciado compañero @emiliorios sobre el arrepentimiento. Su texto me dejó pensando profundamente en esa frase tajante que muchas veces escuchamos o incluso repetimos con orgullo: \

. Suena maduro, suena a una autoestima bien plantada, pero cuando rascas un poco la superficie, la aseveración se vuelve dudosa. Somos humanos, erramos, y cerrarse a la posibilidad del arrepentimiento puede ser, a veces, solo un mecanismo de defensa para no mirar de frente nuestras propias sombras.

Hace muy poco viví una experiencia que me obligó a desmontar ese orgullo. Al calor de un café en la cocina, en un espacio de supuesta complicidad, le comenté a mi hermana que mi hijo adolescente había tenido un mal día en el liceo y estaba molesto. Lo hice sin mala intención, asumiendo que hablaba con alguien de mi propia sangre, una persona en la que se supone que debería confiar plenamente. Sin embargo, la confianza es un cristal delicado. Días después, ante la presencia de mi hijo, mi hermana soltó el comentario como un balde de agua fría, exponiendo su intimidad sin ningún tipo de filtro.

En ese instante me quedé fría. Sentí una vergüenza moral enorme porque, por una ligereza mía, había roto el pacto implícito de silencio que tengo con mi hijo. En el carro, de regreso a casa, él me puso un límite con una madurez que me sobrepasó: me pidió que no ventilara sus cosas con nadie, ni siquiera con su círculo cercano.

¿Cómo no arrepentirme de haber hablado de más? Si me hubiera refugiado en el cliché de \

, habría sido una postura soberbia e hipócrita. Me arrepentí en el acto. Pero no desde el espacio oscuro, estéril y destructivo de la culpa, ese juez interno cruel que nos machaca la cabeza sin darnos tregua, sino desde la necesidad urgente de la corrección. Le pedí perdón a mi hijo, asumí mi error y entendí que el arrepentimiento sano es, en realidad, una herramienta de pensamiento crítico. Es el dolor necesario que nos avisa que hemos cruzado una línea sagrada y que debemos recalibrar la brújula inmediatamente.\n\nA veces confundimos el arrepentimiento con la debilidad o con un castigo moral. Pero mirar al pasado con ojo crítico es el único camino real hacia la evolución personal. Si no somos capaces de aceptar que hubiésemos querido hacer las cosas de otra manera, nos condenamos a repetir los mismos patrones, disfrazando la testarudez de \

.

Equivocarse con la familia duele el doble porque las expectativas son más altas. Esperamos discreción de quienes comparten nuestra sangre y esperamos ser el puerto seguro de nuestros hijos. Cuando fallamos en lo segundo por culpa de lo primero, la evaluación interna debe ser implacable pero constructiva. Hoy entiendo que el arrepentimiento no es una mancha en el expediente; es la honestidad de reconocer que la confianza de un hijo no se negocia por un momento de conversación casual. Al final del día, la corrección no duele si el objetivo es proteger lo que más amamos; lo que realmente desgasta es cargar con el peso de una culpa que no se transforma en cambio.

---

# _English_

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmVAfMu99Hme6Cb9vBmnDxAjMMUJs2bx7XS1KmiqVsPURo/beige_scrapbook_vision_board_instagram_post.png)

#

# Repenting is Not Weakness

#

There are readings that find you at the exact right moment, just when life has handed you a lesson right face-to-face. That happened to me a few days ago while reading a reflection on regret by fellow our partner @emiliorios  His text left me thinking deeply about that sharp phrase we often hear or even repeat with pride: \

It sounds mature, it sounds like well-grounded self-esteem, but when you scratch the surface a bit, the statement becomes doubtful. We are human, we err, and closing oneself off to the possibility of regret can sometimes be just a defense mechanism to avoid looking at our own shadows head-on.

Very recently, I lived through an experience that forced me to dismantle that pride. Over a warm cup of coffee in the kitchen, in a space of supposed complicity, I mentioned to my sister that my teenage son had had a bad day at school and was upset. I did it with no ill intent, assuming I was speaking with someone of my own blood, a person I am supposed to trust completely. However, trust is a delicate glass. Days later, right in front of my son, my sister let the comment slip like a bucket of cold water, exposing his privacy without any kind of filter.

In that instant, I froze. I felt an enormous moral shame because, through a carelessness of my own, I had broken the implicit pact of silence I share with my son. In the car, on the way back home, he set a boundary with a maturity that surpassed me: he asked me not to vent his business to anyone, not even to his close circle.

How could I not regret talking too much? If I had taken refuge in the cliché of \

it would have been a arrogant and hypocritical stance. I regretted it on the spot. But not from the dark, sterile, and destructive space of guilt—that cruel inner judge that pounds our heads without giving us a truce—but rather from the urgent need for correction. I asked my son for forgiveness, owned my mistake, and understood that healthy regret is, in reality, a tool for critical thinking. It is the necessary pain that warns us that we have crossed a sacred line and that we must recalibrate the compass immediately.\n\nSometimes we mistake regret for weakness or a moral punishment. But looking at the past with a critical eye is the only real path toward personal evolution. If we are not capable of accepting that we would have wanted to do things differently, we condemn ourselves to repeating the same patterns, disguising stubbornness as \

Making a mistake with family hurts twice as much because expectations are higher. We expect discretion from those who share our blood, and we expect to be the safe harbor for our children. When we fail at the second because of the first, the internal evaluation must be relentless yet constructive. Today, I understand that regret is not a stain on one's record; it is the honesty of recognizing that a child's trust is not to be negotiated for a moment of casual conversation. At the end of the day, correction does not hurt if the goal is to protect what we love most; what truly wears us down is carrying the weight of a guilt that does not transform into change.

Hello, Ram Ram, Namaste, Satriyakaal to all Hive users. Today, I'll tell you why we should move away from the artificial environment. We all live in an artificial environment, as we are surrounded by artificial environments like offices, schools, tuition, colleges, and this is not the only artificial enviornment but, but the artificial environment and the virtual environment, the things like laptop, phone and other devices are the real cause for the destruction of our life so, we should be away from these attractions and I can say this by experience because I have faced this problem in my summer holidays and I can give you an example of my day that how I spend a day in summer holdidays, there is my tution class at morning 5:30 am and it runs from 5:30 to 7:30 and I go tution after a bath because I feel sleepy after waking up so, to avoid sleepyness and to avoid distraction while study, I bath. 

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmUfujw7m9SfkZ68TaJHagjXmthsgpkkzXVKhcio1BRN8v/chatgpt_image_jun_8_2026_08_50_26_pm.png)

 the fields of my village and the calming wind that helps me to take my mind away from hustle and bustle of cities and I would like to avoid electronic gadgets and devices there because I want some peace between nature, and I am sure that my village can definately give me peace so, I am eagerly waiting to go to my village and I'll surely make a blog on my village tour.

links.title: Actitudes al descubierto # 19. La ayuda que nadie estaba obligado a ofrecer. [ES/EN]
links.body: * * * **Serie:** Actitudes al descubierto **Capítulo 19** **Título:** La ayuda que nadie estaba obligado a ofrecer * * *

/> Fuente [Pixabay](https://pixabay.com/photos/teenager-student-studying-writing-6981855/) * * * Hola, comunidad. Hoy continúo con la serie llamada _“Actitudes al descubierto”_, donde me propongo observar y compartir pequeños fragmentos del comportamiento humano en situaciones cotidianas. La idea no es juzgar, sino explorar cómo nuestros gestos, decisiones y reacciones reflejan actitudes y emociones que a veces pasan desapercibidas. Hay actitudes que llaman la atención precisamente porque parecen ir en dirección contraria a lo que solemos esperar. Vivimos en un mundo donde casi todo tiene un costo. Muchas veces las relaciones se construyen alrededor de intereses, intercambios o beneficios mutuos. Por eso, cuando alguien ayuda sin estar obligado a hacerlo, el gesto adquiere un valor especial. Hace algunos años conocí una situación que me hizo reflexionar sobre eso. Una vecina alquilaba una habitación a estudiantes extranjeros que cursaban sus estudios en Cuba. Entre ellos había un joven de Nicaragua que estudiaba Medicina gracias a una beca. Aunque muchas personas imaginan que una beca cubre todas las necesidades de un estudiante, la realidad suele ser bastante más compleja. Los recursos son limitados y, en muchos casos, los estudiantes necesitan alquilar habitaciones particulares, cubrir parte de su alimentación y asumir otros gastos cotidianos que no están incluidos. En el caso de aquel muchacho, la ayuda económica provenía fundamentalmente de su familia. Durante años hicieron el esfuerzo para sostenerlo mientras avanzaba en la carrera. Sin embargo, llegó un momento en que ya no pudieron seguir enviándole dinero. La situación se volvió insostenible. Después de muchas conversaciones, la familia tomó una decisión dolorosa: regresar a Nicaragua sin terminar los estudios. Imagino lo difícil que debió ser aceptar aquello después de tantos años invertidos en una carrera tan exigente. No se trataba solamente de abandonar una universidad. También significaba dejar atrás un proyecto de vida que parecía estar al alcance de la mano. Fue entonces cuando ocurrió algo que nadie estaba obligado a hacer. Mi vecina, al enterarse de la situación, le dijo algo que sorprendió a todos los que conocimos la historia. Le explicó que no tenía que seguir pagando el alquiler. Que podía quedarse allí. Que ella se ocuparía de ayudarlo para que terminara la carrera. No era un familiar. No era su hijo. No tenía ninguna responsabilidad sobre él. Tampoco existía una garantía de recibir algo a cambio en el futuro. Simplemente decidió intervenir cuando vio que una persona estaba a punto de perder años de sacrificio por una situación económica. Y así fue. El joven permaneció allí y pudo continuar estudiando hasta graduarse de médico. Lo que más me llama la atención cuando recuerdo esta historia no es el resultado final, sino la actitud que la hizo posible. Porque muchas veces pensamos que ayudar significa resolver problemas enormes o realizar sacrificios extraordinarios. Sin embargo, en ocasiones la diferencia entre el fracaso y la oportunidad depende de una decisión aparentemente sencilla tomada por alguien que podría haber permanecido al margen. Mi vecina tenía derecho a decir que aquello no era asunto suyo. Probablemente nadie la habría juzgado por hacerlo. Pero eligió otro camino. Y creo que ahí se encuentra una de las formas más valiosas de la empatía: la capacidad de asumir, aunque sea por un tiempo, una carga que no nos corresponde. No para obtener reconocimiento. No para recibir aplausos. Simplemente porque comprendemos que nuestra ayuda puede cambiar el rumbo de la vida de otra persona. En tiempos donde tantas noticias parecen recordarnos lo peor del comportamiento humano, historias como esta me hacen pensar que todavía existen personas capaces de actuar con una generosidad silenciosa. De esa que rara vez aparece en los titulares. Pero que transforma vidas. * * * En los próximos capítulos de _Actitudes al descubierto_ continuaré compartiendo pequeñas escenas y actitudes que revelan diferentes maneras de relacionarnos con quienes nos rodean. * * * English Version --------------- * * * **Series:** Attitudes Uncovered **Chapter 19** **Title:** The Help No One Was Obligated to Offer * * *

/>
Source [Pixabay](https://pixabay.com/photos/teenager-student-studying-writing-6981855/)

* * *

Hello community. Today I continue with the series _“Attitudes Uncovered”_, where I observe and share small fragments of human behavior in everyday situations. The idea is not to judge, but to explore how our gestures, decisions, and reactions reflect attitudes and emotions that often go unnoticed.

Some attitudes stand out precisely because they go against what we usually expect.

We live in a world where almost everything has a cost. Many relationships are built around interests, exchanges, or mutual benefits. That is why, when someone helps without being obligated to do so, the gesture becomes especially meaningful.

Several years ago, I learned about a situation that made me reflect on this.

A neighbor of mine rented a room to foreign students studying in Cuba. Among them was a young man from Nicaragua who was studying Medicine through a scholarship program.

Many people assume that a scholarship covers all of a student's needs, but reality is often much more complicated. Resources are limited and, in many cases, students must rent rooms, pay for part of their meals, and cover many everyday expenses that are not included.

In this young man's case, financial support came mainly from his family.

For years they made great efforts to support him while he advanced through medical school. Eventually, however, they reached a point where they could no longer continue sending money.

The situation became unsustainable.

After many discussions, the family made a painful decision: he would return to Nicaragua without finishing his studies.

I can only imagine how difficult it must have been to accept that after investing so many years in such a demanding career. It was not only about leaving a university. It also meant leaving behind a life project that seemed within reach.

That was when something happened that nobody was obligated to do.

When my neighbor learned about the situation, she told him something that surprised everyone who later heard the story.

She explained that he no longer had to pay rent.

That he could stay.

That she would help him remain there until he completed his degree.

He was not a relative.

He was not her son.

She had no responsibility toward him.

Nor was there any guarantee that she would receive anything in return someday.

She simply decided to step in when she saw that someone was about to lose years of effort because of financial difficulties.

And that is exactly what happened.

The young man stayed and was able to continue studying until he graduated as a doctor.

What impresses me most when I remember this story is not the final outcome, but the attitude that made it possible.

We often think that helping means solving huge problems or making extraordinary sacrifices. Yet sometimes the difference between failure and opportunity depends on a simple decision made by someone who could easily have remained uninvolved.

My neighbor had every right to say that it was not her problem.

Most people would not have judged her for doing so.

But she chose a different path.

And I believe that is one of the most valuable forms of empathy: the ability to carry, even temporarily, a burden that does not belong to us.

Not to gain recognition.

Not to receive applause.

But simply because we understand that our help can change the course of another person's life.

At a time when so many stories seem to highlight the worst aspects of human behavior, experiences like this remind me that there are still people capable of acting with quiet generosity.

The kind that rarely makes headlines.

But changes lives.

* * *

In the next chapters of _Attitudes Uncovered_, I will continue sharing small scenes and attitudes that reveal different ways people relate to one another.

* * *

Thank you for reading.  
Special thanks to @bradleyarrow for supporting the community.

好久没有到公司吃饭，今天晚上到公司吃的肠粉，没想到这么好吃，弄得我都想天天想来食堂吃饭了,今天搞笑的事情吧!今天一天都处于兴奋的状态,主要是上次那个同事，我上次有说有个同事住ICU，主要是他坐椅子摔倒了，没有想到进ICU。

links.title: Instinct
links.body:
/>

Sometimes life forces us to make decisions when we are short of time, lacking in information and cannot be sure whether the chosen course of action is correct. In these moments, instinct is our guiding light. Instinct is an inner feeling, an unconscious voice which pushes us towards a course of action before the conscious mind is capable of analyzing the issue thoroughly. While some rely on this guide entirely, others prefer careful deliberation. I believe that instinct has its merits but must always be combined with experience and reason.  
Many of our instincts are based on experience. Though we may be largely unaware of it, our minds collect and register patterns from situations which we have previously faced. When a similar situation occurs again our instincts tell us how to act immediately. For example, we might meet a new person whom we feel a sudden sense of discomfort towards or perhaps an immediate affinity with. Though we cannot always pinpoint the exact cause of these feelings our subconscious mind might have picked up on something which our conscious minds failed to notice.  
Relying on instincts can be extremely helpful in cases where speed of action is of paramount importance. Athletes, firemen, doctors as well as everyday individuals, all sometimes rely on their instincts where they cannot afford to think about every single aspect of the situation. These instincts sometimes tell them the right thing to do and help them to avoid mistakes; at other times they might even provide an opportunity that reason might dismiss as a result of fear or caution.  
On the other hand, it is crucial to realize that instincts are not always correct. The way we feel at any particular time. By allowing ourselves to be ruled by fear we may turn down the chance of a lifetime whereas over-confidence might lead us into unnecessary danger. When judging people, over-reliance on instinct is fundamentally unfair, since appearances are notoriously deceiving and a first impression might turn into a lifelong friendship.  
Therefore, I believe instinct to be merely a useful, rather than absolute guide. It can give direction but should not replace our faculty for rational thought. Where it is feasible, instincts must be tested against evidence and facts. If both our instincts and our reasoning indicate the same conclusion, our faith in that decision must surely be justified.  
Ultimately, instinct is a human experience. It assists us when facing the unknown and forcing decisions without clear answers. Although they may not always be correct, our instincts are nonetheless an invaluable, albeit unreliability tool that must always be used in conjunction with wisdom and informed consideration.

links.title: Carabobo FC campeón del apertura de la liga FutVe - Fútbol con identidad y resistencia [SPA/ENG]
links.body:
<div class=text-justify>

Ayer se celebro la final del torneo Apertura de la Liga FutVe, entre Carabobo FC y Academia Puerto Cabello. Para quienes no están familiarizados con el futbol Venezolano, estos dos equipos pertenecen al mismo estado, El Carabobo tiene su sede en la capital Valencia y el Academia como su nombre lo indica, en la ciudad costera de Puerto Cabello. Para los habitantes del estado Carabobo, esta final representa una rivalidad que ha trascendido el fútbol y que resulta muy importante para un sector de la población ganar, déjenme les cuento porque.
>#### Carabobo FC, FutVe League Champions – Soccer with identity and resistance
>Yesterday, the final of the Liga FutVe Apertura tournament took place between Carabobo FC and Academia Puerto Cabello. For those who aren't familiar with Venezuelan soccer, these two teams are from the same state. Carabobo is based in the capital city of Valencia, and Academia, as the name implies, is in the coastal city of Puerto Cabello. For the residents of Carabobo state, this final represented a rivalry that transcends soccer and is quite significant for a segment of the population to win—let me tell you why.

<center>  
![1000412542.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/danielcarrerag/23tvgH6MMeqSTCBsMyT729txKF8WLRd29FN2NULWRrtRpdk4TzpvUT4Y5Ra9nxES1NEJF.png)
  </center>


#### Incidencias del partido 

Academia Puerto Cabello llegó cómodamente a esta final, todo lo contrario con Carabobo que hasta la última fecha y por diferencia de goles, fue que logró un cupo para disputarla. La victoria estaba para cualquiera de los dos equipos, sin embargo, el Carabobo se mostró dominante con una ampli posesión de la pelota, llegando el primer gol por penal de la mano de Erick Ramírez en el minuto 26. El segundo gol del Carabobo no tardó en llegar, habiendo transcurrido 52 minutos del encuentro Loureins Martínez marco un bonito gol tras un pase filtrado.
>Academia Puerto Cabello reached this final comfortably, which was quite the opposite for Carabobo, which only managed to secure a spot until the very last matchday, and thanks to goal difference. The victory was up for grabs for either team; however, Carabobo looked dominant with strong ball possession, and the first goal came from a penalty kick by Erick Ramírez in the 26th minute. The second goal for Carabobo didn't take long; 52 minutes into the match, Loureins Martínez scored a beautiful goal off a through ball.

<center>   
![1000412541.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/danielcarrerag/23xAe7wTSpwoBcd5bKRNsFDVEkmtEmkk7rEVrcGg66WuQJ5ofDRp7R7JTj5yjvqzVF4q8.png)
 </center>

El Academia pisó el acelerador en los minutos finales del encuentro, logrando marcor su único gol en el minuto 90+3 por parte de Edwuin Pernia, que tambien tuvo en sus manos el empate, pero gracias a una magistral salvada del loco Bruera, arquero del Carabobo, se mantuvo el marcador 2-1, para coronarse campeón el equipo granate. Todas está incidencia en los 10 minutos finales del encuentro, que tras varias intervenciones arbitrales y del VAR, se tuvo que añadir todo este tiempo.
>Academia stepped on the gas in the final minutes of the match, managing to score their only goal in the 90+3 minute through Edwuin Pernia, who also had the equalizer in his hands, but thanks to a masterful save by the \

Bruera, Carabobo's goalkeeper, the 2-1 scoreline held, and the Granate team was crowned champion. All of this action happened in the final 10 minutes of the match, which had to be added on due to several VAR and refereeing interruptions.
https://youtu.be/fLhrFfcSfzo?si=FsIIs2crCMShppX4
*** #### Afición Vs Gobierno Les decía al principio lo importante que era este juego para la afición granate. El juego se desarrolló en el estadio Misael Delgado de la ciudad de Valencia, una sede cuyo aforo no supera los 10.000 asientos. Normalmente en juegos donde estos dos equipos se enfrenta hay muy buena asistencia, Carabobo cuenta con una de las aficiones más fieles y constantes de la liga, se hacen llamar Granadictos, son una barra numerosa de jóvenes, con los canticos típicos del fútbol, pero que pueden ser algo radicales. >I mentioned earlier how important this game was for the Granate fanbase. The match took place at the Misael Delgado stadium in the city of Valencia, a venue with a capacity of less than 10,000. Normally, there is a great turnout for games between these two teams. Carabobo has one of the most loyal and consistent fanbases in the league. They call themselves the Granadictos—they are a large group of young people with typical soccer chants, though they can be a bit radical.
https://www.youtube.com/live/TnumdKKW_vY?si=7KqVOOiWhKExMZSU
Todo lo contrario con el Academia, que suele tener afición en sus juegos, pero se ha descubierto que son personas que trabajan en instituciones del estado, llevadas al estadio por transporte de dichas instituciones por ordenes del gobernador, Rafael Lacava, que se sabe es dueño del equipo. La mitad del aforo del estadio se reserva por ordenes del gobernador para la \

del Academia. Este accionar a elevado las tenciones entre los fanáticos, haciendo que los Granadictos le dediquen canticos ofensivos al gobernador y eleven pancartas alusivas mostrando personajes que cazan vampiros, ya que el gobernador se hace llamar a si mismo Drácula.\n>It is quite the opposite for Academia. While they usually have fans at their games, it has been discovered that they are often people who work for state institutions, brought to the stadium by state-provided transportation on the orders of the governor, Rafael Lacava, who is known to own the team. Half of the stadium's capacity is reserved by the governor's orders for Academia's \

This behavior has elevated tensions between the fans, leading the Granadictos to chant offensive songs at the governor and hold up banners depicting people hunting vampires, as the governor likes to call himself \

![1000412226.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/danielcarrerag/EpnDH3tF8Pz1XuCtyRHHXM5th8XqzCCVpSCjVYJUNoUmDPUpzQwXxqWrGBohbTfWArs.jpg)
De esta manera el Fútbol se ha visto envuelto en conflictos que trascienden las tribunas, lo que hace que estos partidos tengan una importancia para cierto sector de la fanaticada, ya que se siente que el todo poderoso gobierno no es infalible. Lo importante para mí es lo bonito del deporte y me agrada ver cómo un equipo como Carabobo se ha metido en 6 finales consecutivas y con este triunfo, el conjunto granate se ganó el derecho de disputar la Final Absoluta de la temporada 2026 y aseguró su clasificación a la Copa Libertadores. >In this way, soccer has become wrapped up in conflicts that transcend the stands, which makes these matches significant for a certain sector of the fanbase, as they feel the all-powerful government is not infallible. links.title: How Holozing can Win over Steam players - Some Changes
links.body:
![02ee321e-7e3b-4b22-b086-246bbc243a91.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/cocacolaron/23tS2SeYQoMDvwCYZMw6aqcHixPMNaFmkqNnwxHyuCgWMBbbsbZPuYpvbJcTg5THv1j3B.png)


---


I've been thinking a lot about the future of Holozing and the possibilities it would have if it ever sought to expand beyond the Hive community. Although the project already has its own identity thanks to its creature system, exploration, and blockchain-based rewards, the reality is that entering Steam presents a completely different challenge.

It's not enough to have a good idea; it's also necessary to meet the expectations of millions of players accustomed to the platform's standards.

One of the first changes Holozing should consider is strengthening its core gameplay. Many Steam users look for fun experiences even before thinking about reward systems or digital economies.

---


![d802dff0-24bc-44f8-b521-54a522f6419a.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/cocacolaron/23tviN3uM7vPC25mPhB4Hg6axVcBTTisLNBphyJv8dg3yfGgxtgR9EXbKikMaPoLVMwj7.png)


---

The game needs to prove that it can entertain on its own. If creature capture, combat, and exploration are appealing, the blockchain elements will become a complement, not the main reason to play.

Another important aspect is accessibility. Currently, many cryptocurrency-related projects require prior knowledge of digital wallets, tokens, and processes that can be complicated for the average user.

If Holozing wants to attract Steam players, it should simplify the registration process as much as possible. Ideally, a person should be able to download the game, create an account, and start playing in a matter of minutes without needing to understand how blockchain technology works.

---


![2b5dd5ba-c538-459b-9e49-081ff06c2426.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/cocacolaron/23tHCDC7uZ2SrXrBDF4S4hKMghg6oBYWRHe9rJ6MY29qMXqcXEhxnsjKab5iFNqphkS3e.png)



---

The visual presentation will also be crucial. Steam is a platform where competition is fierce, and players often decide whether to try a title in a matter of seconds.

Holozing will need a modern interface, fluid animations, and a consistent art direction that stands out among hundreds of weekly releases. The creatures already have interesting designs, but the game must convey a sense of quality from the first glance.

---


![werferferf.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/cocacolaron/23x1Fg7U2BST9afKAEZm2uHbZozQYU7QPV6BNFdv3MB7S27vSAmZ2sA9LRLs1C61opecS.png)



---

In addition, implementing more social content would be advisable. Collection and adventure games typically benefit greatly from features such as player trading, cooperative events, guilds, or competitive systems.

These features help build an active community and increase user retention, something that Steam highly values ​​because it's reflected in reviews and game activity.

Offering a clear roadmap will also be important. Steam gamers are often wary of projects that seem incomplete or promise too many features without concrete timelines. A transparent development plan would help build trust and demonstrate that the team has defined goals for the future.

---



![44bc31f1-41e8-404d-a475-4154d93a9e44.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/cocacolaron/23tbkpVZM2yvKALAz1qfhZAaAEZmsEDNESLez3Qbv58Dapb51C2PUpKHmS1twXTrqiD9j.png)


---

On the other hand, Holozing should carefully evaluate how it integrates its blockchain elements. Steam has maintained a complicated stance regarding certain cryptocurrency and NFT models. This means the project would have to find a way to highlight its gameplay experience without relying exclusively on those systems. The focus should be on fun, progression, and community.

---



![0e19ba18-123e-4515-8f9c-b90435ae67b5.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/cocacolaron/23u69BEmhUH2q6RYuFyLhWi4RdvWZYenvsC3nJ6xyekFvSZAhPqPMyCHDNfoSKfgLQq5M.png)



---

I have reservations about Steam, but I think it's the best opportunity the game has if it wants to reach a larger community. I don't know how those blockchain elements will be integrated, but I certainly think there's room for it.

body.title: 🚀 El hábito que separa a los ricos de las personas que siempre viven con deudas
body.body:
![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmXDg8L2F5fYSyBiVxbhdCSsfTjRLxv1bNuXxpCny1AfAv/img_6961.png)


Muchas personas creen que para ser exitosas financieramente necesitan ganar miles de dólares al mes. Sin embargo, la realidad es que la riqueza comienza con los hábitos diarios
![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmWbktjpcogKgryJkoHp7MKa2h9Lry1fszE9SnBwAbRqYP/img_6962.png)


Las personas que construyen riqueza entienden que cada dólar puede ser una herramienta para crear un mejor futuro. En lugar de gastar todo lo que ganan, buscan ahorrar, invertir y aprender nuevas habilidades que les permitan generar más ingresos.



![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmYih32Zmo3hMTNAzGZCYMEKF498XNy2Zfk7fft6hYauZ1/img_6965.png)
La disciplina es más importante que la cantidad de dinero que tienes hoy. Pequeñas acciones repetidas durante meses y años pueden producir resultados extraordinarios.
![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmRe4kfK6pDkY8Sqx8KfPHrySku7UU5byfTvVMtzfdZatV/img_6964.png)


Tres hábitos que pueden ayudarte a mejorar tus finanzas:

✅ Llevar un control de tus gastos.
✅ Ahorrar una parte de cada ingreso.
✅ Invertir tiempo en aprender sobre dinero y crecimiento personal.

Recuerda: no se trata de cuánto ganas, sino de cuánto eres capaz de conservar y hacer crecer.



La riqueza no se construye en un día, se construye con decisiones inteligentes tomadas cada día.

¿Qué hábito financiero consideras más importante para alcanzar la libertad financiera?

body.title: Is It Safe To Trust Instincts Alone?
body.body:
![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmXbv2ftdrz9cWA8zbfiRhh4SLBg4r9pGsN5ZSfDa9fLdE/1780931186540.jpg) The human mind is one of the most mysterious things I have ever known. I feel, somehow, our minds and bodies are designed to pick up signals of things that have already occurred or are yet to happen, as though there was a link between us and the supernatural. Many times, we experience situations where we had little to no idea about something, but our minds kept directing us on a path we can not explain about that very thing, and surprisingly, it will end the way we thought. It has been occurring so much that people commonly say “follow your heart” when one is about to make a crucial decision in their life, but they are confused about what to do. Sometimes we follow our heart, and it plays out well; other times it goes south. I can not tell why people are this confident about their instincts, but I know that nothing is 100% safe or accurate in life. If things go as we perceive, fine, we might be right, or we might be lucky. And if they don't, we might be wrong or there is something we are yet to discover. Whatever the case may be, I don't agree with totally depending on instincts alone to make major decisions in life. Instincts can be merely feelings or minor clues from past experiences, without sure and proven data; sometimes, it is dangerous to proceed. I don't trust my instincts 100% . It has failed me many times before. There were times I tried using my instincts in the crypto market, and I watched my assets turn into dust simply because my instincts told me to hold, and similarly, there were times my instincts said “sell,” and because I trusted it, I sold, and guess what? From the moment I sold, the price began going higher. Instincts are good, but they can be misleading, too. Your instinct can tell you someone is evil simply because you don't feel comfortable around them, only for you to dislike them and later discover they are good people. But don't get me wrong, as I said earlier, our bodies and minds are designed to pick up signals beyond even the physical realm. It is possible for us to perceive danger, and our instincts would immediately alert us. Yet we should also try to balance instincts with other data before taking action in order to avoid making critical mistakes, especially when dealing with people. There are times I am compelled to use my instincts to address issues, especially when I am clueless about something, and there is obviously no means of getting reliable information. I have no option but to follow my heart, yet I don't carelessly immediately. Sometimes, I hold and take it slow, watching the outcomes, and if I notice that the path I am on is likely not the right one, I don't hesitate to stop just where I am and look for another alternative before things completely go out of hand. ![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmPTfVnoZAcHvJEBpXYbFteUXGqkg6ogze4ZftxfQ53wXB/1780931213052.jpg) Instincts can be either right or wrong; one just has to be careful when making decisions. I know that life can be funny; sometimes you can make the most accurate decisions, yet they will fail, but it's better to fail right than to fail or win wrongly. ------ N.B: All Images Were Generated By Gemini AI ------

Thanks For Reading

body.title: Elegante brazalete con bola de fuego/Elegant bracelet with a fireball 💗😍
body.body: <div class=\

> Hello chicos, feli, día y feliz inicio de semana! Por aquí seguimos con un clima delicioso, así que nos despertamos de muy buen humor y con ganitas de crear algo lindo, así que realicé un brazalete precioso, muy elegante y súper combinable, para ocasiones especiales y la verdad es que es mut sencillo de hacer y, por supuesto, tenía que compartirlo con ustedes en mi blog.
Hello everyone, happy day and happy start to the week! The weather’s still lovely here, so we woke up in a great mood and raring to create something pretty. I’ve made a gorgeous, very elegant bracelet that goes with just about anything – perfect for special occasions. It’s actually really simple to make, and of course I had to share it with you on my blog.
![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmdRBGwcVXLaUpMYRZt9cd9sCJjyoDk9h8LCfxFrhMfqdV/1780931469037.png) *** Como saben me gustan los accesorios sencillos, y aunque mi idea era crear una pieza elegante, no quise perder mi estilo y mantenerlo lo más simple posible y para esto decide utilizar un aro dorado grande junto con una bola de fuego y cadenas delgadas, de hecho esto es lo unico que utilicé para este brazalete, pero miren qué cosa tan bella y tan delicada el resultado. Y si más vueltas, vamos con los materiales y el paso a paso.
As you know, I like simple accessories, and although my idea was to create an elegant piece, I didn’t want to stray from my style and wanted to keep it as simple as possible. So I decided to use a large gold hoop combined with a fireball and thin chains; in fact, that’s all I used for this bracelet, but just look at what a beautiful and delicate result it is. Without further ado, let’s get on with the materials and the step-by-step guide.
![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmZPwgpVt72p5ScbV7sVcbDENhHQRxpmsJN6NtwzVtrvN9/1780931469318.jpg) *** # Materiales Alfiler de ojo Cadena delgada Aro dorado grande Aros pequeños Bola de fuego blanca Broche para cerrar Dije rectangular Tenaza Pinza plana Pinza redonda
# Materials Eye pin Thin chain Large gold ring Small rings White fireball Closing clasp Rectangular charm Pliers Flat-nose pliers Round-nose pliers

# Paso a paso/Step by step Como ven son muy pocos materiales, y básicamente solo tenemos que armar una pieza, que sería nuestra bola de fuego, y esto lo haremos utilizando un alfiler de ojo, y lo que hacemos, pues es muy simple, pasamos nuestra bola de fuego por el alfiler cortamos el excedente y cerramos como ya lo hemos aprendido en el blog. Simplemente colocamos la pinza redonda en el extremo del alfiler y giramos sobre sí misma hacia adentro para crear nuestro aro. De esta manera ya tenemos lista una de las dos piezas que forman la pieza focal del brazalete.
As you can see, there are very few materials, and we basically just need to assemble one piece – our fireball – using an eye pin. It’s very simple: we thread the fireball onto the pin, cut off the excess, and close it as we’ve already learnt on the blog. We simply place the round clasp on the end of the pin and twist it inwards to create our ring. And there we have it: one of the two pieces that make up the central element of the bracelet is now ready.
![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmeP3rKFuiNtcaVtYyh1uD3pnWGM8J632Ukko5FacpYYiL/1780931469505.jpg) *** Lo que sigue es conectar la bola de fuego a nuestro aro grande, que como ven no es una simple forma redonda, sino que es ondulada dándole un poco más de vistosidad y movimiento a la pieza, y lo unico que tenemos que hacer es abrir un poco uno de los ojitos a los extremos de la bola de fuego y hacer pasar la argolla. Cerramos y tenemos lista la pieza focal de nuestro brazalete.
Next, we need to attach the fireball to our large ring, which, as you can see, isn’t just a simple round shape but is wavy, giving the piece a bit more visual interest and movement. All we have to do is open one of the small loops at either end of the fireball slightly and thread the ring through. We close it up, and the centrepiece of our bracelet is ready.
![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmXkRhwLwyjg6TzqEPmPLWWGHmnbdgNTkG1RGvDkowsA9X/1780931469679.jpg) *** El siguiente paso es cortar las cadenas que vamos a utilizar, y el largo como siempre les digo va a depender de cuán largo desean su brazalete, así que necesitamos dos piezas, una para cada extremo de nuestra pieza focal.
The next step is to cut the chains we’re going to use; as I always say, the length will depend on how long you want your bracelet to be, so we need two pieces, one for each end of our centrepiece.
![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmRWRaw7BdpMWnJwiQZNebgE5cN3g4Jf9VXY1WKwd1wLs2/1780931469831.jpg) *** Seguidamente vamos a conectar las cadenas a cada extremo de la pieza central, y del lado de la bola de fuego simplemente abrimos el aro que nos queda disponible, hacemos pasar la cadena, cerramos y sellamos con la pinza plana para asegurar que cierre completamente. Del otro lado donde se encuentra la argolla lo que vamos a hacer es colocar una argolla pequeña, así que la abrimos un poco y por ella hacemos pasar nuestra argolla grande además de la cadena, cerramos y tenemos de esta forma listo el largo de nuestro brazalete.
Next, we’ll attach the chains to each end of the centre piece. On the side with the fireball, simply open the remaining ring, thread the chain through, close it and secure it with the flat-nose pliers to ensure it closes completely. On the other side, where the ring is, we’re going to attach a small ring, so we’ll open it slightly and thread our large ring through it along with the chain, close it, and in this way we’ll have the length of our bracelet ready.
![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmRoiay2dHumr6A3fueep95VSFi2ZaL5arf7SQLQMu2Guo/1780931575700.jpg) ![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmNWZnNQ7MweSJSxUcRh3DXRAeMKf52r5qcLKhwJRCqstx/1780931575885.jpg) *** Para finalizar, debemos agregar las piezas que nos permiten cerrar nuestra pulsera, y para ello en ambos extremos vamos a colocar 2 argollas pequeñas y en uno vamos a colocar el cerrador junto con el pequeño dije que pueden ver en la imagen que me parece que le da un toque muy lindo al brazalete. Para colocar estas piezas lo único que tenemos que hacer es abrir la agolla que colocamos en uno de los extremos, y hace pasae el cerrador nuestro dije, cerramos y aseguramos con la pinza plana y listo, tenemos un hermoso brazalete para lucir en ocasiones especiales.
Finally, we need to add the parts that allow us to fasten our bracelet. To do this, we’ll attach two small rings to each end, and on one end we’ll attach the clasp along with the small charm you can see in the picture – I think it adds a lovely touch to the bracelet. To attach these pieces, all we need to do is open the jump ring we placed at one end, thread the clasp and our charm through it, close it and secure it with the flat-nose pliers, and there you have it – a beautiful bracelet to wear on special occasions.
![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmRCSzb3zPRsWkFEFLpmmFw97ERZuarGJZsUp8xXocjb8c/1780931576222.jpg) ![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmSb62V2LkyzBR2Qv9TRVVAtEx1qbey51LU8URk7HFTLx6/1780931576056.jpg) ![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmZS1LVMUFbvjXj3NgxnUN645ocBa86FFANx54Jntcs8fC/1780931576318.jpg) ![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmZPwgpVt72p5ScbV7sVcbDENhHQRxpmsJN6NtwzVtrvN9/1780931688752.jpg) ![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmZS1LVMUFbvjXj3NgxnUN645ocBa86FFANx54Jntcs8fC/1780931688882.jpg) *** Como pueden ver es un proyecto absolutamente sencillo y lo mejor de todo es que los pueden crear según su gusto, yo simplemente les dejo la idea, así que si a ustedes le gustan los accesorios con más volumen, pues utilicen una cadena más gruesa y piezas más llamativas, ya que esto es cuestión de gustos. La idea es crear algo que se adapte perfectamente a tí. >As you can see, it’s a really simple project, and best of all, you can tailor it to your own taste. I’m just giving you the basic idea, so if you prefer more statement pieces, go for a thicker chain and more eye-catching components – it’s all down to personal preference. The idea is to create something that suits you perfectly.

body.title: [카일의 수다#882]비파 또는 ’비와(びわ)’
body.body:
![B948F54B-8F9B-4B43-838A-1095AD597583.jpeg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmdAueyrwpFXrQEpLLzTuEU1gRUZdyKvpoH1SDbb49XRJm/B948F54B-8F9B-4B43-838A-1095AD597583.jpeg)

일본 마트에서 눈에 띈 비파.
뭔지 궁금해서 고가지만 하나 집어 봤다.

비파는 중국이 원산지인 과일로 일본에서는 ’비와(びわ)’라고 부른다. 노란빛이 도는 주황색 과일인데 살구나 작은 복숭아를 닮은 생김새가 특징이다. 말레이시아에서도 보기만 했었는데, 평소 자주 볼 수 있는 과일이 아니라 한 번쯤 먹어보고 싶었다.

가격표를 보고 잠시 망설였다. 크기에 비해 꽤 비싼 편이었기 때문이다. 알고 보니 비파는 추위에 약해 재배 지역이 제한적이고 수확 기간도 짧다. 게다가 과육이 무르고 상처가 잘 나서 수확과 유통 과정에 손이 많이 간다고 한다. 생산량도 많지 않아 자연스럽게 가격이 높게 형성된다고.

껍질을 벗겨 한입 먹어보니 과육은 부드럽고 과즙도 제법 많았다. 맛은 살구와 배, 복숭아를 조금씩 섞어 놓은 듯한 느낌. 달콤하면서도 은은한 새콤함이 있었다.

솔직히 가격만큼 엄청 맛있다는 생각은 들지 않았다. 씨가 커서 먹을 수 있는 부분도 생각보다 적었다. 그렇다고 맛이 없는 건 아니고, 한 번쯤 경험해볼 만한 독특한 과일 정도.

비싸서 자주 사 먹을 것 같지는 않지만, 궁금했던 비파를 직접 먹어봤다는 것만으로도 만족.

body.title: Do public figures have a moral obligation to take a political stance? | My take on the situation in Colombia [ENG/ESP]
body.body:
![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmZWBa2W4ZgggNJN21eAoFo1DPz5z7JBX4CGtGUcwxtjP7/1780843517194.png)
*Image Generated with Gemini Al*

Hello, Hive community. I hope you’re all doing well.
These days, it’s impossible to open social media in Colombia without feeling the immense political tension surrounding us. Polarization is at its peak, and unfortunately, it has brought with it a trend that worries me greatly: the pressure to force everyone to take sides. In particular, I see suffocating pressure on public figures—artists, athletes, content creators—to openly state who they’re going to vote for.
Today I want to share my opinion on this, because I’m firmly against requiring them to take a public stance, let alone judging them if they decide not to.
>Hola, comunidad de Hive. Espero que estén muy bien.
​Por estos días, es imposible abrir las redes sociales en Colombia sin sentir la inmensa tensión política que nos rodea. La polarización está en su punto más alto y, desafortunadamente, ha traído consigo una tendencia que me preocupa mucho: la necesidad de obligar a todo el mundo a tomar un bando. En especial, veo una presión asfixiante hacia las figuras públicas —artistas, deportistas, creadores de contenido— para que digan abiertamente por quién van a votar.
​Hoy quiero compartir mi opinión sobre esto, porque estoy firmemente en contra de que se les exija fijar una postura pública, y mucho menos de que se les juzgue si deciden no hacerlo.

It seems we’ve forgotten that voting in our country is, by law and by right, secret. Fulfilling our civic duty to go out and vote is a moral obligation to the country’s future—of course it is; but publicly campaigning is not. There’s a very fine line between encouraging people to vote and feeling forced to throw your support behind a candidate to avoid a digital lynching.
It really bothers me to see how the digital mob attacks an influencer or an athlete, labeling them “lukewarm,” a coward, or indifferent to the country’s reality just for keeping their opinion in the private sphere. Not taking a public stance doesn’t make you any less Colombian, nor intolerant, nor apathetic. It simply means that you understand the responsibility that comes with your reach and that you prefer to respect the diversity of your audience.
Demanding that someone who makes comedy videos, sings, or plays soccer take on the role of a political analyst is a mistake. Even worse is the culture of cancellation that erupts if that person decides to exercise caution. We live in a society fractured enough that we also seek to destroy the few remaining spaces for entertainment or sports, turning them into political battlegrounds.
>​Parece que hubiéramos olvidado que el voto en nuestro país es, por ley y por derecho, secreto. Cumplir con el deber ciudadano de salir a votar es una obligación moral con el futuro del país, claro que sí; pero hacer campaña pública no lo es. Existe una línea muy delgada entre invitar a la gente a participar en las urnas y verse obligado a colgarse la camiseta de un candidato para evitar el linchamiento digital.
​Me molesta mucho ver cómo la masa digital ataca a un influencer o a un deportista tildándolo de \

, cobarde o indiferente con la realidad del país solo por mantener su opinión en la esfera privada. No fijar una postura pública no te hace menos colombiano, ni intolerante, ni apático. Significa, simplemente, que entiendes la responsabilidad de tu alcance y que prefieres respetar la diversidad de tu audiencia.
​Exigirle a alguien que hace videos de humor, que canta o que juega al fútbol que asuma un rol de analista político es un error. Peor aún es la cultura de la cancelación que se desata si esa persona decide guardar prudencia. Vivimos en una sociedad lo suficientemente fracturada como para que también pretendamos destruir los pocos espacios de entretenimiento o deporte que nos quedan, convirtiéndolos en trincheras políticas.

In the end, democratic maturity isn’t demonstrated by forcing others to think like us, nor by demanding public declarations of loyalty to a cause. It is demonstrated by respecting others’ silence. Voting is an act of individual responsibility, and keeping that decision to oneself is a right that all of us—regardless of the number of followers we have—should be able to exercise in peace.
I’d really love to hear the perspectives of other creators on the platform: Do you think social pressure on social media has undermined the right to a secret ballot? Can one be a citizen committed to the country while remaining silent in public? I look forward to reading your comments. For now, I’ll sign off—thank you so much for reading, and I’ll see you soon in another post ❤️
>​Al final, la madurez democrática no se demuestra obligando a los demás a pensar como nosotros, ni exigiendo declaraciones públicas de lealtad a una causa. Se demuestra respetando el silencio del otro. Votar es un acto de responsabilidad individual, y guardarse esa decisión para uno mismo es un derecho que todos, sin importar el número de seguidores, deberíamos poder ejercer en paz.
Me gustaría mucho conocer la perspectiva de otros creadores en la plataforma: ¿Creen que la presión social en redes ha desvirtuado el derecho al voto secreto? ¿Se puede ser un ciudadano comprometido con el país desde el silencio público? Espero Leerlos en comentarios, yo por ahora me despido, muchas gracias por leerme y nos vemos luego en otro post ❤️

----

json_metadata.description: 我做了這個很奇怪的夢 我夢到家裡的廁所和浴室(相鄰但是分開的)前面挖了兩個小水池，池水很清澈，裡面有很多壟溝魚。我發現這兩個水池是由一根很大的地下水管連通到屋外的壟溝的。 那根地下水管和它上方的地板都是透明的，所以可以從地上看到水管裡面的情況。 我突然看到一隻很大的魚(差不多半個成人那麼大)病怏怏地往外游，當它游到大門下方時，它突然就化身變成了一隻豬出現在大門後面。 那隻豬仍然是病怏怏的樣子，很辛苦地站着想要開門。

body.title: The Battles of Chivalry 2 Are Truly EPIC and MASSIVE
body.body:
![1.gif](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/venapboyz/23tRzfXZT6DS4uLMmvYX12MfckvbW9mDt9UrBpdsp8FTYtHtBbzMZ79MgFhfZEDrLaUJT.gif)


Hey, how are you all doing gamers? Hope everyone is doing great! So I've been putting a lot more hours into Chivalry 2, and I have to say, my opinion on this game has become much more solid and well-formed compared to my first impressions. When you start playing a new online game, especially one with this kind of depth, the first couple hours are really just you stumbling around trying to figure out what's even happening. But now that I've logged considerably more time, I can really speak to what this game does and does well. This time around I was mainly exploring the big 64-player Team Objective mode, so that's what we're going to talk about today. And let me just say right out the gate — the battles in this game are genuinely something else.

**A Full-Scale Battle Between 64 Players**

![0423 (1)(7).jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/venapboyz/23tRxoVBkttJoeBDXKmUEfV738bscCDSYNwjfyPxiRi7G2F25Advet3vnzchiCcZfvTXB.jpg)

Alright, so let's talk about what it actually feels like to be dropped into one of these 64-player matches, because nothing I said in my first impressions article could have fully prepared me for it. You spawn in, you hear the roar of battle already happening around you, steel clashing, arrows whistling, players screaming their war cries — and then you realize there are 63 other people on this same map doing exactly what you're about to do. It is pure, absolute, beautiful chaos.

And the thing is, it doesn't feel like mindless chaos either. The developers over at Torn Banner Studios described it once as \

and honestly that's the most accurate way to put it. Yes, there are bodies and fire and swords everywhere, but underneath all of that madness there's a real battle happening with two factions pushing and pulling against each other. You've got the Agathians and the Tenosian Empire going at it across these sprawling maps, and every player on the field is contributing to the outcome whether they realize it or not. It genuinely feels like being in the middle of one of those massive medieval movie battle scenes, except you're actually controlling the guy and not just watching it from a cinema seat.

The scale of these maps is also really impressive. We're talking castle sieges, villages getting torched, ships getting blown up, fortresses being stormed. Each map tells a completely different story and takes you through multiple phases of the battle. It's not just one big arena you run around in — the fight progresses, the objectives shift, and you have to keep adapting. I had no idea this was the level of production and scale these maps operated on. I went in expecting something simpler and came out genuinely impressed.

**The Objectives During Battle**

![0423 (1)(2).jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/venapboyz/23y8jBSs66DaWysU6xNwURro8q7Tdh9dTjxBFisGLZiuCFNa9Jna4EasmvkdjhcUE4fvY.jpg)

So this is where the Team Objective mode really separates itself from your standard team deathmatch mentality, and also where I really started to understand what Chivalry 2 is doing differently. It's not enough to just kill people — there are actual things that need to happen for your team to win or lose, and if you ignore them you're basically useless no matter how many kills you rack up.

The objectives change depending on the map and the phase of the battle you're in. Sometimes the attackers need to capture a position by outnumbering the defenders and holding it long enough to fill a capture bar. Other times you've got to grab a torch from a pyre and go burn specific objects on the map while the other team tries to stop you. There are escort objectives where a character needs to be moved to a safe zone, destroy objectives where you're blowing something up with explosives, and elimination objectives where you need to wipe out the enemy before time runs out. Each phase of the map flows into the next, and if attackers can't complete an objective before the clock expires, the defenders win right there.

What I find really cool about this is that it forces you to make constant decisions. Do I chase down that guy who just hit me and get some payback? Or do I sprint toward the objective because my team is getting overwhelmed there? Do I hold this position and try to fight off three people by myself? Do I back up and wait for reinforcements? All of this is happening in real time with 63 other people making similar decisions around you. It's genuinely a lot to process when you're still learning the game, and there were definitely moments where I realized the match was lost because nobody on my team was focused on what actually needed to happen. Staying focused on objectives while everything around you is exploding and people are screaming — that's the real challenge.

**Actually Learning to Fight in Chivalry 2 Is a Whole Other Challenge**

![0423 (1)(3).jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/venapboyz/23tRveeYiHFb8aqoiUj6Zmk1m1BwFEKcghThDFSfRFrbmdZDv4x53hDYErKNewiSJrdM3.jpg)

Okay so beyond the scale of the battles and the objectives, let me talk about what is probably the steepest learning curve this game has thrown at me: the combat itself. And yes, I talked about this a little in my first impressions piece, but the more I play, the more I realize how deep this rabbit hole actually goes.

At first glance it seems like you just swing your weapon at people, but that is about as far from the reality as you can get. The combat system in Chivalry 2 has layers. There's blocking, which isn't just holding a button — you have to actually aim your block to match the direction of the incoming swing, like genuinely lining it up with your opponent's weapon. Then there's the riposte, which is when you successfully block an attack and immediately fire back with your own, and that counter-attack is faster than a normal swing and can catch people off guard if they're not ready for it. Then there's the counter, which is a well-timed parry that negates the attack without costing you stamina — landing those consistently is a completely different skill on its own.

![0423 (1)(4).jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/venapboyz/23tRvZwRCh8y8dba12V8ZVyvQUMhqENi9yjEPkemYWXbjzsiX5n5DoZmztNYSGZNNXBnj.jpg)

And then there's feinting, which is probably the sneakiest thing in this game. You start one kind of attack — say an overhead — and mid-motion you switch it to a stab, and your opponent who was already adjusting their block for the overhead now has to scramble to adjust for something completely different. When it works, it feels brilliant. When someone does it to you, it feels like you've been tricked by someone who's been doing this for years. And on top of all of that, there's the dragging mechanic, where you accelerate or extend the arc of your swing by turning your body into the attack, changing the timing of when the blade actually connects and making it harder for opponents to read. There's so much going on in every single duel that it honestly took me a while to even identify what was killing me and why. The combat is deep, it's demanding, and mastering it is going to take real time and patience.

**Slowly Leveling Up the Classes**

![0423 (1)(8).jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/venapboyz/23t7BBxkgbuefv9HKFpDDb4VwK2HNqX6CwGpuqeoFMMqkTE28Hdx65LeNRiiNDhaevs5J.jpg)

One thing I'm starting to appreciate more and more is the progression system tied to the classes. Each of the four classes — Knight, Footman, Vanguard, and Archer — has its own separate experience level, and leveling them up is how you unlock new subclasses and new weapons for that specific class. So the more you play a Knight, the more Knight stuff you unlock. Same for every other class. It makes sense from a design perspective because it rewards you for sticking with a class and learning it properly instead of just hopping between them every match.

Right now I'm mainly playing the Knight because as a beginner, that extra health cushion is genuinely valuable while I'm still figuring out the defensive mechanics. Taking damage while learning how to block and time ripostes correctly is just part of the process, and having 175 health as a Knight versus something much squishier like the Vanguard gives you more room to make mistakes and survive them. I've been leveling the Knight up steadily and starting to see new options open up, which keeps things feeling fresh. Eventually I want to seriously invest in the Vanguard and figure out how to use all that speed and stamina properly, because watching good Vanguard players fly around the battlefield is genuinely something special. But for now, the Knight stays on.

**I Want to Keep Playing and Explore the Other Game Modes**

![0423 (1)(5).jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/venapboyz/23uQfpnBn1kYcwhCYzDMmW5sUHAjiko23hmsuGJfYeDyiVoEvGrHUXR7sFd8m2QaTU6fn.jpg)

At this point I've put in enough hours to say with confidence that Chivalry 2 is a genuinely good time, and a game I want to keep exploring. The 64-player Team Objective mode alone has given me more than enough content to keep me busy, but I know there's a whole lot more waiting. There's Team Deathmatch, Free-for-All, Brawl mode — which is this ridiculous format where everyone fights with unconventional weapons like fish and chicken legs and rolling pins, and I absolutely cannot wait to experience that chaos. There's also Mounted combat through the mounted warfare queue which I haven't touched yet either.

The game has a genuine skill ceiling that is going to take a long time to approach, and that's a good thing. Every match I come out of knowing something I didn't know going in — whether it's a combat mechanic I finally understood, a map objective I finally figured out how to push, or just a class ability I learned to use at the right moment. It keeps pulling you back. So hey gamers, hope you liked this update on my Chivalry 2 journey — if you've been playing this game or want to jump in, drop a comment and let me know. See you in the next one!

Die Ameise hat auch einiges an Ideen zu dem Konzept geliefert. Die sind so schon faszinierend. Allerdings wollte ich das auf einen Levensraum übertragen der halt sehr lebensfeundlich ist. 

Die idee mit der Sternenutter hat mich viel zeit und grips gekostet. Einen natürlichen Weg zu finden die Schwerkraft eines Planeten zu überwinden ist eine challenge gewesen. Muskelkraft fällt physikalisch raus.  Da hat mir die KI dann den Tipp mit langer Lebensdauer gegeben. Wenn man lange genug Energie sammeln kann erreicht man irgendwann die Grenze des vielleicht möglichen. Das fand ich dann plausibel genug um es in das Konzept aufzunehmen. 

Starship Troopers ist ein guter Film, aber sollte nichts mit meiner idee zu tun haben. Ich wollte kein Science Fiction schreiben, sondern überlegungen wie es physikalisch und biologisch möglich sein könnte. Auf dem Mars wären keine Krieger nötig vermute ich. Aber wenn man das expansionsszenario dazu nimmt wird man sie vermutlich brauchen. 

Aber ja, ich erkenne wo du ähnlichkeit erkennst. 😁

body.title: Pollen: A Safer, Cleaner Path Forward for Hive JavaScript Developers
body.body:
Hey everyone,

I have been spending a lot of time lately looking at modernizing the available developer tools around Hive.

Its not really flashy work, at least not the kind of thing that gets a giant launch trailer.

But this kind of work does matter if we want people to keep building on Hive without fighting against decade-old tooling, stale dependency trees, and fragile build systems.

One of the biggest pieces of that work is **Pollen**, the modern TypeScript SDK for Hive.

Pollen started from a simple idea:

> What if developers could move forward from `dhive` without having to relearn how to build Hive apps?

That is the balance I have been trying to strike.

Pollen should feel familiar to anyone who has used `dhive`, but underneath it should be much safer, much cleaner, and much more in line with the JavaScript ecosystem we actually have today.

## First, Respect Where `dhive` Came From

Before I say anything else, I want to be clear about this:

`dhive` matters.

It helped define JavaScript development on Hive. A lot of apps, bots, scripts, and experiments were built with it. It gave developers a usable client, transaction signing, broadcast helpers, database helpers, Hivemind helpers, and a familiar way to talk to the chain from Node.js and the browser.

That work deserves respect.

But software ages.

The JavaScript ecosystem from the Browserify/Babel/Mocha era is not the same ecosystem we are using now. Some dependencies went unmaintained. Some cryptography packages became uncomfortable to keep around. Some build assumptions made sense years ago and are just baggage now.

So this is not about dunking on `dhive`.

It is about carrying the useful shape of it forward.

## The Security Difference Is Not Small

I ran both projects through CVE Lite, using the lockfiles as the source of truth.

For `dhive`, the report showed:

- **906 packages scanned**
- **82 findings**
- **117 CVEs**
- **16 critical**
- **35 high**
- **25 medium**
- **6 low**
- **3 direct vulnerable dependencies**
- **79 transitive vulnerable dependencies**

![Screenshot 2026-06-08 at 10-17-49 CVE Lite — dhive-cropped.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/thecrazygm/23t732e3Wvv1LUz89Yyr64ymLFifJxhUwcq1tXCHXGq9KtzivKyj5ceSMHr8ovPbb3btt.png)

The direct fixes suggested by the report were for:

- `node-fetch`
- `secp256k1`
- `karma`

But that only covered **3 of the 82 findings**. The rest were transitive dependencies buried in the old toolchain and dependency tree.

That is the real problem with old JavaScript projects. The visible dependencies are only part of the story. The bigger risk is usually the stack of packages underneath them.

For Pollen, the same scanner showed:

- **468 packages scanned**
- **0 findings**
- **0 CVEs**
- **0 critical**
- **0 high**
- **0 medium**
- **0 low**

![Screenshot 2026-06-08 at 10-17-18 CVE Lite — hive-pollen.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/thecrazygm/23t72k8A3hFz3eN2JZEXb61eECQXMeheR8tdmNDuSnuzVnvoS2DxuyWNJMqR1o2kjUJ98.png)

That does not mean \

No scanner can promise that.

The report itself is careful about this: CVE Lite checks package versions against OSV advisories. It does not prove runtime exploitability or guarantee that every advisory is reachable in your app.

But as a maintenance signal, the difference is huge.

One project is carrying a large amount of legacy dependency risk. The other has been rebuilt around a much smaller, modern dependency surface.

That is exactly what Pollen is aiming to achieve.

## What Changed Under the Hood

Pollen is not just a rename.

The internals have been modernized pretty aggressively:

- **pnpm** replaced the old yarn/npm workflow
- **Vitest** replaced the older Mocha/nyc test setup
- **esbuild** replaced the legacy Browserify-style browser build
- **oxlint** and **oxfmt** replaced slower legacy linting and formatting paths
- **Pure ESM** replaced older module assumptions
- **native `BigInt`** replaced `JSBI`
- **native `Uint8Array`** replaced the old byte-buffer style internals
- **native `fetch`** replaced fetch polyfill dependencies
- **`@noble` cryptography** replaced legacy crypto packages
- strict TypeScript work cleaned up the core library and protocol types

The big one for me is the cryptography and serialization layer.

Hive transaction signing is not a place where I want a pile of old dependencies doing mystery work. Pollen uses the modern `@noble` cryptographic stack and a native byte engine built around `Uint8Array` and `DataView`.

That means fewer moving parts, clearer code, better browser behavior, and less dependency risk.

## But the Developer Experience Is Familiar

The important part is that Pollen still feels like the SDK Hive JavaScript developers already know.

If you used `dhive`, this probably looks familiar:

```ts
import { Client } from \
;\n\nconst client = new Client([\
]);\nconst accounts = await client.database.getAccounts([\
;\n\nconst client = new Client([\
]);\nconst accounts = await client.database.getAccounts([\

More like:

> Keep the mental model. Replace the foundation.

Broadcasting is the same kind of story:

```ts
import { Client, PrivateKey } from \
;\n\nconst client = new Client([\
,\n    to: \
,\n    amount: \
,\n    memo: \

,
  },
  key,
);
```

The names are familiar:

- `Client`
- `PrivateKey`
- `client.database`
- `client.broadcast`
- `getAccounts`
- `getDiscussions`
- `transfer`
- `vote`
- `comment`

This is intentional.

Pollen is different where it matters most: dependency health, typing, crypto, build tooling, bundling, and maintainability.

It is familiar where developers need it to be familiar: the way you actually write Hive apps.

## The Honest Migration Notes

Most app code should be able to start by changing the import:

```diff
- import { Client, PrivateKey } from \
;\n+ import { Client, PrivateKey } from \

;
```

But there are a few honest notes:

- Pollen targets modern JavaScript and TypeScript.
- It expects **Node.js 18+**.
- It is **Pure ESM**.
- Older CommonJS-only projects may need a small module-system update.
- Very old browser build setups may need to move to a modern bundler.

I consider those tradeoffs worth it.

Supporting old build systems forever is one of the reasons JavaScript dependency trees become so risky in the first place. At some point, a project has to move forward.

Pollen tries to make that move as painless as possible without dragging the old risk along with it.

## Why This Matters for Hive

Hive needs good and modern developer tooling.

Not just tooling that technically works.

Tooling that feels maintained and documented.

Tooling that passes modern audits.

Tooling that can be used in production without making developers hold their breath every time they run a dependency scan.

That is the bigger reason I have been working on Pollen, Nectar, Anther, Xylem, and the rest of the SRBDE ecosystem.

Different languages, same idea:

- modern dependencies
- audited cryptography where possible
- cleaner serialization
- better tests
- better docs
- less legacy baggage

Pollen is the JavaScript piece of that.

## Where It Stands Now

Pollen is currently published as:

```bash
pnpm add @srbde/pollen
```

The package is at **v1.0.2** in the repo I scanned.

The CVE Lite scan showed **0 findings** against the `pnpm-lock.yaml`.

The API shape remains close enough to `dhive` that existing Hive JavaScript developers should not feel lost.

That is exactly where I wanted this project to land:

> modern on the inside, familiar on the outside.

## Closing Thoughts

![left_monitor.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/thecrazygm/23t773rbQjyoCB4Fenyd8YJM9Amk7Ea8uNzb9tr6LnhBzDZomioyAeNg4fpRRW354QBWY.png)

This kind of work is not always glamorous.

Sometimes it is deleting old polyfills.

Sometimes it is replacing byte buffers.

Sometimes it is chasing type errors until the compiler finally stops complaining.

Sometimes it is looking at a CVE report and deciding the right fix is not to patch one package, but to modernize the whole foundation.

That is what Pollen is.

It is not a rejection of `dhive`, dhive maintainers are welcome to pull from us for any of these changes, some more drastic than others.

This is the next branch growing from the same root.

For developers already building on Hive with JavaScript or TypeScript, I hope the switch feels boring in the best possible way:

change the import, run the tests, fix the few modern ESM edges if you have them, and keep building.

The difference is what you are building on top of.

As always,
**Michael Garcia** a.k.a. **TheCrazyGM**
