body.title: Best Essay Writing Services for College Students in 2026 — Ranked & Reviewed
body.body:
Finding a reliable essay writing service feels impossible when most review sites are paid placements or years out of date. I went through the research myself — testing platforms, reading verified student feedback, and tracking down honest opinions from real users across college communities.

Here is my honest breakdown of the six best services available to college students in 2026. Every one of them earned an A+ rating. The difference is in what each does best.

Quick note: Always check your school's academic integrity policy. These services work best as writing references and structural guides — not for direct submission.

Top-rated picks for 2026:

  • CollegeEssay.org — 4.9/5.0 (A+)
  • MyPerfectWords.com — 4.8/5.0 (A+)
  • 5StarEssays.com — 4.8/5.0 (A+)
  • SharkPapers.com — 4.8/5.0 (A+)
  • MyPerfectPaper.net — 4.7/5.0 (A+)
  • WriteMyEssay.help — 4.7/5.0 (A+)

🏆 #1 — CollegeEssay.org | 4.9/5.0 (A+)

CollegeEssay.org is my top pick and earns that spot every time. I've placed rush orders here — including a 6-hour deadline — and the quality held up far better than I expected. The near-perfect rating is consistent across years, and it shows in the experience.

The writer matching system is what sets it apart. Instead of assigning whoever is free, the platform pairs each order with a writer who has a verified background in the relevant subject. That specificity matters for niche topics and upper-level coursework. The 24/7 live chat is genuinely responsive, and a free plagiarism report comes with every order.

Why it stands out:

  • Subject-specific writer matching, not random assignment
  • Rush deadlines as short as 6 hours met consistently
  • 24/7 live chat with fast, real responses
  • Free plagiarism report included with every order
  • Direct communication with assigned writer throughout

Best for: Urgent deadlines, high-stakes assignments, students who want direct writer contact

✍️ #2 — MyPerfectWords.com | 4.8/5.0 (A+)

MyPerfectWords.com is where I go for long, citation-heavy, or graduate-level work. The writer pool is one of the largest in the industry, and the coverage across academic subjects is deep. Citation styles — APA, MLA, Chicago, Harvard — are handled correctly by default, without needing to chase corrections afterward. The revision process is smooth and actually honored.

Why it stands out:

  • Massive writer pool covering hundreds of subjects
  • All major citation styles applied correctly as standard
  • Reliable and frictionless revision process
  • Consistent quality for research papers and graduate-level writing

Best for: Research papers, citation-heavy assignments, graduate-level writing

⭐ #3 — 5StarEssays.com | 4.8/5.0 (A+)

5StarEssays.com is the smartest budget option here. Quality is comparable to the top two services, but the price is noticeably lower. I can upload my rubric, grading criteria, and lecture notes directly with the order — so the writer actually understands what is being asked rather than producing something generic. Instruction-following is consistently one of its most praised qualities.

Why it stands out:

  • Best price-to-quality ratio on this list
  • Upload rubrics, slides, and course notes with the order
  • Writers follow specific instructions better than most competitors
  • Strong for business, MBA, marketing, and economics essays

Best for: Budget-conscious students, business and MBA essays, instruction-specific assignments

🦈 #4 — SharkPapers.com | 4.8/5.0 (A+)

SharkPapers.com is the most underrated service on this list and the one I always recommend to STEM students. General platforms fall apart on technical writing — the terminology is off, the structure does not match what a STEM professor expects. SharkPapers.com is built differently, with writers who have verified technical backgrounds. Pricing is fully transparent with no fees surfacing at checkout.

Why it stands out:

  • Writers with verified technical and scientific backgrounds
  • Handles lab reports, case studies, and engineering essays with real competence
  • Transparent pricing with no hidden fees
  • Correct IEEE, APA, and discipline-specific formatting

Best for: STEM students, lab reports, technical writing, case studies

📄 #5 — MyPerfectPaper.net | 4.7/5.0 (A+)

MyPerfectPaper.net is the most consistent service I have used. Every order comes back at roughly the same high standard — no variance, no surprises. The progressive delivery option for long papers is genuinely useful, letting me review sections as they arrive rather than receiving everything at once. The editing and proofreading service is also one of the stronger offerings here.

Why it stands out:

  • Most consistent quality output across multiple orders
  • Progressive delivery for long papers
  • Strong editing and proofreading for polishing your own drafts
  • Clear and fair money-back guarantee

Best for: Long-form papers, editing and proofreading, students who value consistency

✏️ #6 — WriteMyEssay.help | 4.7/5.0 (A+)

WriteMyEssay.help is the platform I point first-time users toward every time. The ordering process is the simplest of the six — clean, fast, and hard to get wrong. It performs especially well for personal statements and college application essays, a category where most services fall flat. The writing feels personal and purposeful rather than templated.

Why it stands out:

  • Simplest and most beginner-friendly ordering process
  • Consistently strong results for personal statements and application essays
  • Clear revision policy that is actually followed
  • Reliable on standard 24–72 hour deadlines

Best for: First-time users, personal statements, college application essays

📊 Quick Comparison

Service Rating Best For Price
CollegeEssay.org ⭐ 4.9 Urgent deadlines $$$
MyPerfectWords.com ⭐ 4.8 Research papers $$
5StarEssays.com ⭐ 4.8 Value + business $$
SharkPapers.com ⭐ 4.8 STEM/technical $$
MyPerfectPaper.net ⭐ 4.7 Long papers/editing $$
WriteMyEssay.help ⭐ 4.7 Beginners/personal $

My Verdict

No bad picks here — every service earned its A+ for a reason. The right choice comes down to what the assignment needs.

CollegeEssay.org for anything urgent or high-stakes. MyPerfectWords.com and 5StarEssays.com for the best value when you have more time. SharkPapers.com for STEM. MyPerfectPaper.net for consistency and long papers. WriteMyEssay.help for anyone just getting started.

Drop your own experiences in the comments — real feedback helps everyone make a better decision. Good luck this semester. 🎓

These guys are known for their songs. As soon as spring arrives, they're already in forests and parks, and in some cities, even in yards. They also migrate for the winter very late. I even encountered them in early November, which surprised me. After all, all the migratory birds had already left in September.

body.title: Secret to Overcoming Anxiety (Used by Marcus Aurelius)
body.body:
This is my third video on MindStoic, a channel I started about Stoic philosophy and modern psychology. This one is about the Stoic secret Marcus Aurelius used to overcome anxiety — and why it works better than anything modern self-help has to offer. Watch it here and let me know what you think.

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=jJYeCikt_Ts

40 million Americans suffer from anxiety. Billions of dollars are spent every year on therapy, medication and self-help books trying to fix it.

Marcus Aurelius had no therapist. No medication. He ran the most stressful job in human history — emperor of Rome, constant wars, betrayals, plagues — and he never broke.

His secret isn't complicated. But almost nobody knows it. And once you understand it, anxiety will never control you the same way again.

Marcus wrote: \

Read that again.

Not the traffic. Your judgment about the traffic. Not your boss. Your judgment about your boss. Not the future. Your judgment about the future.

Every single thing that makes you anxious is not happening in the world — it's happening in your mind. It's a story you're telling yourself about what something means.

Marcus called this \

— your ability to choose how you interpret reality. And he trained it like a muscle every single day.

Anxiety has one root cause: trying to control things you cannot control.

Marcus divided all of reality into two categories. Things inside your control — your thoughts, your actions, your effort, your response. And things outside your control — other people, the weather, the economy, what happens to you.

His rule was absolute: give your energy only to what's inside your control. Everything else — complete acceptance.

This isn't passivity. It's precision. You stop wasting mental energy on things that were never yours to control, and redirect it entirely to the things that are.

Most anxious people spend 90% of their mental energy on the 90% of life they cannot control. Marcus spent 100% of his energy on the 10% he could.

Anxiety only exists in two places: the past and the future. It cannot exist in the present moment.

Marcus wrote constantly about this. \

Not tomorrow's battle. Not yesterday's mistake. This breath. This step. This decision.

Modern psychology calls this mindfulness. Marcus called it common sense.

When you feel anxiety rising, ask yourself one question: is this happening right now, in this exact moment? Almost always the answer is no. You're living in a future that doesn't exist yet, fighting battles that haven't happened.

Marcus trained himself to return to the present moment every time his mind drifted into fear. It became automatic. It can become automatic for you too.

This is Marcus Aurelius' most powerful weapon against anxiety.

Amor Fati means \

Not acceptance. Not tolerance. Love.

Marcus didn't just accept difficult things — he actively looked for what was good in them. Every obstacle, every setback, every painful moment — he trained himself to ask: what is this giving me that I couldn't get any other way?

The anxious mind sees threats everywhere. The Stoic mind sees fuel everywhere. Same reality, completely different experience.

This isn't toxic positivity. It's a trained cognitive reflex. And like every reflex, it gets stronger with practice.

Marcus didn't just think about these ideas. He practiced them every single day through his journal.

Every morning: what challenges will I face today and how will I respond with virtue? Every evening: where did anxiety control me today and what will I do differently tomorrow?

This daily practice of written reflection is now backed by decades of psychological research. Expressive writing reduces cortisol — the stress hormone — measurably and consistently.

Marcus was doing evidence-based anxiety therapy two thousand years before the evidence existed.

Anxiety is not a chemical problem. It's a thinking problem. And thinking problems have thinking solutions.

The Stoic secret is this: you cannot control what happens to you. You can only control your response. Train that response every single day, and anxiety loses its power over you completely.

Watch the full video here: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=jJYeCikt_Ts

body.title: After festival days
body.body:
Hi, guys!

After the festival, I gave myself a day to recover, but naturally, it wasn't enough. I can't afford to waste any more time on this, and I have to get back to work today. My brain is racing, desperately trying to film something and post it online. I have a ton of filming plans, and I'm currently stuck with a huge backlog of filming, so I need to do everything quickly and get it live.

I've started working with a new manga publisher; I hope I'll have many collaborations with them. Today, I'll message a girl I met at Fancon and show her my blog. Let her see if they'd like to work with me (I really hope so). Then I'll have regular reviews of not only books but also manga, and that's something I need to keep in mind.

Something interesting happened with the promo videos; one of them got twenty thousand views, assuming I get the same level of promotion as the others. So far, I'm assuming it's all about the cool editing, but I still need to test that theory. If that's true, then by changing the editing concept, I'll be able to get more views while reducing costs, and that's already good. But we'll see how it works in practice.

So now we're starting to change the filming concept and see what happens.

Have a great day, everyone!

body.title: My Mother’s Orchid Collection
body.body: <div class=\

> Happy Mondday Hivers! ## Since I was a child, my mother has always loved orchids. Even when she was very busy before with her business and taking care of us, she still found time to care for her orchids. I still remember how beautiful our yard used to be. It was full of different colors of orchids, especially when they bloomed at the same time. It looked so alive and colorful. ## ![IMG_4482.jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/kellyane/23yTd3sEV7qm3jfG4gViGqQc9xYHP5rUSkgVvirZQPbZ73676Jnu1uZjFZEKiBZAD6hQz.jpeg) ## But there came a time when most of her orchids died. She didn’t notice that the water she was using had become too salty, and it slowly damaged the plants. After that, she felt discouraged and stopped planting orchids for a while. Even when people offered her free orchids, she no longer wanted to accept them. It seemed like she was really hurt by what happened. ## ![IMG_4479.jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/kellyane/244ocy3F6ZtnfsjjwiYqEJp4S4Hv1uuHaDnR6pVko3JgtNqEdpBFmZeZBJDe25yBT2M7r.jpeg) ## But this year, I noticed something special. She slowly started planting again. For the past few months, she has been buying orchids and rebuilding her collection. I don’t really know the names of the orchids, but she knows them all very well. ## ![IMG_4480.jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/kellyane/243Bgd4Zxva6favMEFXUNkcC96aGYXdntd1QceEBHGtccJK3M6cfo4pgywx2GiMsYygda.jpeg) ## Just a few weeks ago, she came home from going out and I was surprised and happy because she brought home orchids that already had flowers. When she arrived, she immediately placed them carefully so they would not die. Maybe she has already healed from what happened before. Now, she is starting again, and I am happy to see her love for orchids coming back. ## ![IMG_4481.jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/kellyane/23zGcSJC4mKmyr1XQuZiiU8QEM47eXvcQzUpA6Dh6VkexfQpq9nWTwNbRG7dpm7HJtUcd.jpeg) ## ## ## ## ##

>

Thank you for reading and see you on my next blog. Cheers!

body.body: politics has become so nasty that it seems that nobody is actually interested in what is right, they just want their side to win no matter what.  I have my own opinions about who drew first blood in this, but I don't think elections are fair ever anymore.   \n\nI recall when I was in college that a very weak candidate ran against Bill Clinton.  his name was Bob Dole, he lost the election badly.  There was no bitching, no accusations of cheating, no recounts, no shady boxes of late votes coming in during the middle of the night.  It was just a concession.  Dole said \

and conceded.  Then he just kind of went away and didn't do a press tour or try to meddle in the affairs of Clinton from that day forward.   These days we see the losers just stick around and bitch for years and years after they have lost.   It's all so tiring.

The self-pairs all show high correlation (above 0.9 for deterministic augmentations like flip, gray, and blur, since the same operation applied to the same image is identical). Crop shows lower self-correlation because the random crop region varies between calls. The lowest overlap pairs involve grayscale combined with crop or brightness -- grayscale destroys all color information (our image's main distinguishing features are color-coded), and crop additionally changes spatial content. This directly illustrates why SimCLR uses aggressive composition of multiple augmentations: any single augmentation leaves too much mutual information, making the contrastive task too easy for the model to learn useful representations.

At m=0.9, the momentum encoder tracks the online encoder closely (low distance) but its parameters fluctuate heavily (high variance) because each update contributes 10% of the current online state. At m=0.9999, the target is incredibly stable (near-zero variance) but lags dozens of steps behind the online encoder -- it's essentially seeing a heavily smoothed version of where the online encoder was many updates ago. m=0.999 (MoCo's default) hits the sweet spot: the target encoder is stable enough to provide consistent representations for the negative queue, but fresh enough that its representations aren't completely out of date. This tradeoff is exactly why the momentum coefficient matters so much in practice -- too low and the target is noisy, too high and you're comparing against stale representations.

**Exercise 3:** Masking strategy comparator for MAE.

```python
import numpy as np


class MaskingComparator:
    \

def __init__(self, grid_size=8, seed=42):
        self.gs = grid_size
        self.total = grid_size ** 2
        self.rng = np.random.RandomState(seed)

    def _positions(self):
        return np.array([(r, c)
            for r in range(self.gs)
            for c in range(self.gs)])

    def random_mask(self, ratio):
        n_mask = int(self.total * ratio)
        indices = self.rng.permutation(
            self.total)
        masked = set(indices[:n_mask])
        return masked

    def block_mask(self, ratio):
        n_mask = int(self.total * ratio)
        side = int(np.ceil(np.sqrt(n_mask)))
        side = min(side, self.gs)
        r0 = self.rng.randint(
            0, max(self.gs - side + 1, 1))
        c0 = self.rng.randint(
            0, max(self.gs - side + 1, 1))
        masked = set()
        for r in range(r0, min(
                r0 + side, self.gs)):
            for c in range(c0, min(
                    c0 + side, self.gs)):
                masked.add(r * self.gs + c)
                if len(masked) >= n_mask:
                    return masked
        # Fill remaining randomly
        remaining = [i for i in range(
            self.total) if i not in masked]
        self.rng.shuffle(remaining)
        for idx in remaining:
            masked.add(idx)
            if len(masked) >= n_mask:
                break
        return masked

    def grid_mask(self, ratio):
        n_mask = int(self.total * ratio)
        step = max(1, int(1 / (1 - ratio + 1e-8)))
        visible = set(range(0, self.total, step))
        all_idx = set(range(self.total))
        masked = all_idx - visible
        # Adjust to exact count
        if len(masked) < n_mask:
            extra = list(visible)
            self.rng.shuffle(extra)
            for idx in extra:
                masked.add(idx)
                if len(masked) >= n_mask:
                    break
        elif len(masked) > n_mask:
            remove = list(masked)
            self.rng.shuffle(remove)
            for idx in remove:
                masked.discard(idx)
                if len(masked) <= n_mask:
                    break
        return masked

    def analyze(self, masked_set):
        positions = self._positions()
        visible = [i for i in range(self.total)
                   if i not in masked_set]
        masked = list(masked_set)
        n_vis = len(visible)

        # Average distance between visible
        vis_pos = positions[visible]
        if n_vis > 1:
            dists = []
            for i in range(n_vis):
                for j in range(i + 1, n_vis):
                    d = np.sqrt(
                        ((vis_pos[i] - vis_pos[j])
                         ** 2).sum())
                    dists.append(d)
            avg_vis_dist = np.mean(dists)
        else:
            avg_vis_dist = 0

        # Coverage uniformity (4 quadrants)
        half = self.gs // 2
        quads = [0, 0, 0, 0]
        for idx in visible:
            r, c = positions[idx]
            q = (0 if r < half else 2) + (
                0 if c < half else 1)
            quads[q] += 1
        uniformity = np.std(quads)

        # Reconstruction difficulty
        if n_vis > 0 and len(masked) > 0:
            vis_pos_arr = positions[visible]
            recon_dists = []
            for m_idx in masked:
                mp = positions[m_idx]
                d = np.sqrt(
                    ((vis_pos_arr - mp) ** 2
                     ).sum(axis=1))
                recon_dists.append(d.min())
            recon_diff = np.mean(recon_dists)
        else:
            recon_diff = 0

        return {
            \
: n_vis,\n            \
: avg_vis_dist,\n            \
: uniformity,\n            \
: self.random_mask,\n            \
: self.block_mask,\n            \

: self.grid_mask,
        }
        ratios = [0.25, 0.50, 0.75, 0.90]
        trials = 100

        print(f\
\n              f\
\n              f\
)\n        print(\
\n                    f\
\n                    f\
\n                    f\
\n                    f\

)
            print()


comp = MaskingComparator()
comp.run()
```

Random masking distributes visible patches evenly across the grid (low uniformity score, meaning the quadrant counts are balanced), which is why MAE uses it -- the model sees information from everywhere and has to reconstruct local structure. Block masking creates regions where many neighboring patches are all masked simultaneously, forcing the model to hallucinate large contiguous areas (high reconstruction difficulty locally), but leaves other parts of the image fully visible (poor coverage uniformity). Grid masking produces perfect uniformity (exactly the same number of visible patches in each quadrant) but trivially low reconstruction difficulty because every masked patch has a visible neighbor at a fixed, predictable distance -- the model can learn a simple interpolation shortcut instead of understanding semantics. At 75% masking, random is the clear winner for training a useful encoder, which is why Kaiming He's original MAE paper landed on exactly this combination.

That's what we're building today. A **visual content analysis API** that takes an image and returns: every object it detects, all the text it can read, a set of visually similar images from a database, and a natural language description of the scene. It's the kind of system that powers reverse image search, content moderation, visual commerce, and photo organization -- and we're building it from components we've already studied ;-)

```
|  2. OCR (text extraction)         | --> recognized text + positions
|  3. Visual Embedding (DINOv2)     | --> 384-dim feature vector
|  4. Image Captioning (BLIP)       | --> natural language description
+-----------------------------------+
    |
    v
Structured JSON response
  + similarity search results from FAISS index
```

Each component handles a different aspect of visual understanding. YOLO (episode #79) finds objects. OCR (episode #82) reads text. DINOv2 (episode #90) produces embeddings for similarity search. BLIP (episode #75) generates descriptions. Together, they extract far more than any single model could.

The key architectural insight: these four models are **independent**. Detection doesn't depend on OCR results. Captioning doesn't need the embedding. This independence means we can run them concurrently -- a big deal for latency.

## Component 3: visual embedding and similarity search

This is where self-supervised learning from last episode becomes practical. **DINOv2** produces powerful visual embeddings without any fine-tuning, and **FAISS** (we used it in episode #63 for text embeddings) enables efficient similarity search:

```python
import torch
import faiss
import numpy as np
from torchvision import transforms
from PIL import Image


class VisualSearchEngine:
    \

)
        self.model.eval()
        self.transform = transforms.Compose([
            transforms.Resize(256),
            transforms.CenterCrop(224),
            transforms.ToTensor(),
            transforms.Normalize(
                mean=[0.485, 0.456, 0.406],
                std=[0.229, 0.224, 0.225]),
        ])
        # Inner product on normalized vectors
        # = cosine similarity
        self.index = faiss.IndexFlatIP(
            embed_dim)
        self.metadata = []

    def embed(self, image):
        tensor = self.transform(
            image).unsqueeze(0)
        with torch.no_grad():
            features = self.model(tensor)
        features = features / features.norm(
            dim=1, keepdim=True)
        return features.numpy()

    def add_to_index(self, image, meta):
        embedding = self.embed(image)
        self.index.add(
            embedding.astype(np.float32))
        self.metadata.append(meta)

    def search(self, query_image, k=5):
        query = self.embed(
            query_image).astype(np.float32)
        scores, indices = self.index.search(
            query, k)
        results = []
        for score, idx in zip(
                scores[0], indices[0]):
            if idx < len(self.metadata):
                results.append({
                    \
: self.metadata[\n                        idx],\n                    \

: float(score),
                })
        return results
```

The `IndexFlatIP` computes exact inner product (which equals cosine similarity for L2-normalized vectors). For a database of thousands of images, this is fast enough. For millions, you'd swap to `IndexIVFFlat` or `IndexHNSW` for approximate nearest neighbor search -- a tradeoff between search speed and recall that we covered in episode #63.

Why DINOv2 specifically? Because it was trained with self-supervised learning on 142 million curated images (the LVD-142M dataset) and produces representations that generalize to virtually any visual domain without fine-tuning. A DINOv2 embedding captures _what_ is in the image at a semantic level -- it knows that two photos of dogs in different poses are similar, even though their pixel values are completely different. That's the power of the self-supervised pre-training we just studied.

## Performance optimization

The naive pipeline runs each model sequentially. For production, several optimizations matter -- and the most impactful one is **concurrent execution**.

Detection and OCR are independent. Captioning doesn't need the embedding result. So why run them one after another? We can run all four concurrently and wait for the slowest one:

```python
import asyncio
from concurrent.futures import (
    ThreadPoolExecutor)

executor = ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=4)


async def analyze_concurrent(pipeline,
                              image_path):
    \

loop = asyncio.get_event_loop()
    image = Image.open(
        image_path).convert(\

)

    # All four tasks are independent --
    # run them in parallel
    det_future = loop.run_in_executor(
        executor,
        pipeline.detector.detect,
        image_path)
    ocr_future = loop.run_in_executor(
        executor,
        pipeline.ocr.extract,
        image_path)
    cap_future = loop.run_in_executor(
        executor,
        pipeline.captioner.caption,
        image)
    search_future = loop.run_in_executor(
        executor,
        pipeline.search.search,
        image, 5)

    objects, texts, caption, similar = (
        await asyncio.gather(
            det_future, ocr_future,
            cap_future, search_future))

    return {
        \
: objects,\n        \
: texts,\n        \
: caption,\n        \

: similar,
    }
```

Sequential latency = detection + OCR + search + captioning. Concurrent latency = max(detection, OCR, search, captioning). If each component takes roughly 50ms, that's 200ms sequential vs ~50ms concurrent. A 4x improvement from pure parallelism, no model changes needed.

Having said that, there's a caveat with GPU-based models: if all four models run on the same GPU, concurrent execution doesn't help because the GPU can only process one model at a time anyway (the requests queue up on the GPU). Concurrency helps most when models run on CPU, or when you have multiple GPUs, or when some models are I/O-bound (like FAISS search, which is primarily memory-bound).

## What this system can NOT do

I want to be honest about limitations, because knowing what a system can't do is as important as knowing what it can:

- **YOLO detects 80 categories.** It won't find \
or \

Fine-tuning or a different detection model is needed for domain-specific objects.\n- **OCR fails on handwriting and artistic fonts.** It's reliable for printed text, street signs, and product labels. body.body:
不知道是什么原因，现在的我，越来越喜欢一个人独处。独处的时候，除了会思考一些事情，也常常会想起以前一些有趣的时光。

我想起自己以前一些欢乐的时候，有些事情现在看起来可能觉得很平凡普通，但对于无论是当时的我，还是现在多年后再追忆起往事，都是很开心的。

我小学的时候，放学从学校到家里，大约有一里多路。我们班上有个外号叫老牛的同学，不但力气非常大，而且跑的也特别快。每当放学的时候，老牛常常会让我抓住他的书包，或者抓住他的衣服，一声准备好之后，老牛就开始带着我往村子回跑。哇！我现在都记得，老牛跑的可真快啊，我耳朵边都有风吹的呼呼响，跟着老牛，仿佛从学校回到村子里，就是很短暂的时间。

夏天暑假的时候，我通常会花大约一星期不到的时间，将暑假作业提前写完。之后嘛，就是每天都出去玩，白天跟着村里的伙伴，去逮知了，碰上黄河灌溉，还会去水渠里下水。傍晚的时候，带着手电筒，去村子后边的树林里捉知了猴，摸到知了猴后，回家用盐水泡着，次日早晨天刚亮，还没起床，鼻子就早已闻到了我妈在厨房里给我炸知了猴的香味，哇！现在想起来都觉得美极了！

读书的时候，有一阵子追女孩子，追到自己喜欢的女孩子，一起去食堂，去图书馆，去自习室，一起出去逛街，也是非常的开心。

body.title: Michael Saylor Tweeted ( 32 and Dots)
body.body:
What does Michael Saylor want? With this tweet, he has put investors into confusion.

Investors are already worried about many problems in the world. On one side, there is fear of a global war. On the other side, there is unemployment, rising FED interest rates, and many other economic challenges.

Then Michael Saylor posts a tweet with just “32”. But what does it mean? Is he suggesting that Bitcoin will move toward $32K? Is that the message he wants to give? This tweet has created a lot of discussion and excitement among investors.

![Screenshot 2026-06-08 113358.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/aliakbar2/Eo2BM1YUXvinKkhgiQQ6Kipx5KufS7BSgoxdBo2uCukmrZ4igDcqabGrzqCYhn8t8Pz.png)

As far as I understand, this looks like a bullish tweet. Usually, when the market is preparing to move upward, such tweets are posted to confuse investors and create a sense of fear among them.

A short time later, he posted another tweet saying, “A good time to add more dots.” Does he mean investors should invest in DOT? Is he giving preference to Polkadot?

![Screenshot 2026-06-08 113135.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/aliakbar2/48tsNhFing1jzCyH2pmnDNh9cyqhh4gmAnaQ1aySVXsEj9vKcBgd1SPD73ABEpcybR.png)

On one hand, he seems to be creating a bearish atmosphere, while on the other hand, he is talking about investing in DOT. This makes me think that Bitcoin may soon enter a recovery phase.

What do you people think about BTC? What he is trying to convey? Will be glad to see your answers in the comment section.


I hope you find this post useful and informative.. If you do, please remember to reblog it so that it reaches as many people as possible and that they can benefit the most from it. Also remember to upvote which will help me financially and grow my account.

For us we are up quite early today as there is much work to be done in the farm at this time. I appreciate going to farm early in the morning so that one can work with much enthusiasm and energy before the sun comes up. Even though the weather doesn't get too hot like those of the dry season, it is usually discomforting to work in the Sun.
alt=\

/> Talking about the bulk of work to be done in the farm you can see the massive progress that has been achieved with these first sets of planted corn. All of the corns that have been planted in the month of May must have grown to this level is proper care were giving to them
alt=\

/> Due to the scanty nature of rainfall during the month of May when the rains started, alot of people here are yet to plant their corn but for anyone who had taking care to plant theirs, they are at this stage of growth. And because the land here is fertile the corn are dark green and growing fast. Not all the lands in this location in which we farm on are fertile, only a few community members have the privilege to the fertile locations, whenever farming activities commence here we all farm and those who do not have very good soils supports their farms with fertilizers and animal dungs.
alt=\

body.title: ‎LOH #292 || Rainy Days: The Best and Worst Part of This Season
body.body:
‎Hi Hive,
‎
‎Right now, we are in the rainy season here in Nigeria, and honestly, I have a love-hate relationship with it. Some days, I find myself enjoying the weather so much, while on other days, I can't wait for the rain to stop.
‎
 https://img.leopedia.io/DQmZYKBdwnokHwexfTB33WNQs38E8pTzWErb1Y1JQcPVdWr/IMG_20260430_161548_761.jpg 


‎One thing I really love about this season is the break from the intense heat. During the dry season, especially when the sun is at its peak, stepping outside can feel like walking into an oven. The rainy season changes that. The air feels cooler, the nights are more comfortable, and sometimes the sound of rain falling on the roof creates a peaceful atmosphere that helps me relax.
‎
‎Another thing I enjoy is how fresh everything looks after a rainfall. The trees appear greener, the grass looks healthier, and the environment feels cleaner. There is something refreshing about waking up in the morning and seeing dark clouds in the sky instead of the scorching sun. It reminds me that nature has its own way of restoring balance.
‎
‎The rainy season is also important for farmers and food production. Many crops depend on rainfall to grow properly, so this period is often a welcome one for people involved in agriculture. Whenever I think about that, it makes me appreciate the season even more.
‎
‎That said, there are definitely things I don't like about it.
‎
‎The biggest problem for me is the condition of the roads after heavy rain. In many areas, roads become flooded or muddy, making movement difficult. A journey that should take twenty minutes can easily turn into an hour-long struggle because of traffic or waterlogged streets. Getting caught in the rain unexpectedly is another experience I don't enjoy, especially when I don't have an umbrella nearby.
‎
‎Mosquitoes are also a major annoyance during this season. After rainfall, stagnant water tends to collect in different places, creating perfect breeding grounds for them. The result is more mosquito bites and more reasons to keep doors and windows closed.
‎
‎Even with these challenges, I still appreciate the rainy season. The cooler weather, fresh environment, and benefits it brings to farming make it worthwhile. No season is perfect, but I believe that each one has something unique to offer. For me, the rainy season may be inconvenient at times, but it's also one of the most refreshing periods of the year.
‎
‎So, what's the current season like where you live, and what do you love or dislike most about it?

A [portable agricultural sprayer pump](https://www.chandakagro.com/) is an essential farming tool that helps farmers spray pesticides, herbicides, fungicides, and liquid fertilizers efficiently. Its lightweight design and easy portability make it suitable for farms of different sizes. Here are some of the top benefits of using a portable agricultural sprayer pump:

1.  Easy to Carry and Use – The compact design allows farmers to move easily across fields and reach different crop areas.

2.  Saves Time and Labor – Spraying large areas becomes faster compared to traditional manual methods, reducing physical effort.

3.  Uniform Spray Coverage – It helps distribute chemicals evenly, improving crop protection and reducing wastage.

4.  Improves Crop Health – Proper application of pesticides and nutrients helps protect crops from pests, diseases, and weeds.

5.  Cost-Effective Solution – Efficient spraying reduces chemical consumption and lowers farming costs over time.

6.  Suitable for Multiple Applications – It can be used for pesticides, fertilizers, disinfectants, and plant growth solutions.

7.  Increases Farm Productivity – Faster and more accurate spraying allows farmers to manage crops more effectively.

A quality portable agricultural sprayer pump is a smart investment for modern farmers looking to improve efficiency, crop protection, and overall farm productivity.

body.title: Loud Thai parties get shut down by police: organizers blame foreigners
body.body: This is about something that has recently hit the social media complaints about foreigners living in Thailand and on this particular one, I am actually going to side with the foreigners because they are correct.\n\nThe story goes that Thai people are saying that foreigners are ruining their \

by alerting police and having the events shut down because of noise complaints.   

<center> 
![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/jack.russelle/23vi1oG9csWGtrcMZ8T8ktR2zKMBR31TRijXLXZu1WdngZLqFyd59dDkcZWqUmxNTHsYe.png)
[src](https://thethaiger.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/06/koh-phangan-foreigner.jpg)</center>

The social media campaign hasn't really taken hold as of yet but there has been a lot of \
going on as far as locals kind of having a problem with the large expat populations are concerned.   \n\nThis new campaign claims that the Thai events are \

by foreigners to have them shut down but not having foreign events shut down for the same reason.

yeah, I'm gonna call bullshit on that.

Let me tell you a little bit about what the average Thai party is like.  

<center> https://media.mstdn.social/media_attachments/files/112/638/342/835/279/597/original/ac259f9867bb09e0.jpeg</center>

I don't know what compels them to do so but almost any Thai event involves a sound system that would probably be ok at a Metallica concert, but otherwise is much more powerful than an event of that size would ever need.  This could be anything, a festival, a birthday party, a wedding, or even a funeral.  These sound systems get carted in and the absolutely blast it, normally with something particularly awful like karaoke.  This continues until everyone gets too drunk or the police are inundated with complaints, whichever happens first.  

The social media posts, which were intentionally (I think) made in English as well, go like this.

> “Thais hold events and foreigners come to shut down almost every one of them, calling the police. If this keeps up, there will be no more open-air Thai-style events left, only foreigner parties. It wasn’t even 10pm and it hadn’t reached midnight

This is in relation to a recent open-air event that took place in Koh Pha Ngan, an island with a very high expat population compared to the rest of the country.   

I don't believe them when they say that it wasn't that loud because after nearly a decade of living here, I can assure you, it was *very very loud* and I can say that with certainty even though I was not there personally.  

The Thais are claiming that these are cultural experiences that the Thai people have practiced for generations but once again, I have to call BS on that.   Generations ago we didn't have massive speakers to blast in all directions at explosive volumes.   I also seriously doubt the claim that it wasn't even 10pm.   

I was once at a wedding and there were many other foreigners there and we were all complaining to one another that we had to shout to even be able to hear one another at the same table.  The Thai people, for some reason, seem to be immune to this excessively loud party that is going on.   Since one of the people getting married was a foreigner, we were able to politely ask if they could maybe turn it down a touch so that we didn't have to have our ears bleeding while attempting to hang out and celebrate our friends' wedding.   

When it was turned down nobody really even noticed.  It's not like the Thai people were insulted.  I don't think they wanted it to be that loud either but they are just accustomed to it always having been that loud at any of the events they had attended in the past.  

I think that this is one of those things that actually annoys everyone, Thai and foreigner alike, but to some people, it has always been this way.   I don't think it is too much to ask for people to be respectful of their neighbors and maybe keep the party at a reasonable volume.  

There are noise laws in this country as well as a certain time where the noise has to stop without a permit.   This push on the part of the people who are putting this on social media that foreigners are somehow interested in shutting down \

is pure nonsense.   What the foreigners are doing is quite sensible actually, they just want to have some peace and quiet in their lives.  If the people organizing these events were less selfish, there would be no reason for the police to get involved.  \n\nI am reminded about the time that I was in college and loud parties would get shut down by the police on a regular basis.   There was no \

going on, the residents were just wanting us to be sensible, but we were young and selfish so the police needed to get involved.

I don't like that everything these days seems to spiral into an internet campaign to spread hate towards something and in this case that is exactly what the people making these posts are doing.  

While some people are taking the rage-bait, there is also a counter-argument that states that amplification at a level that disturbs the peace is something that people are entitled to complain about regardless of nationality.   

I don't believe this is a cultural thing at all.  I believe it is just that some people don't take into account that what they are doing might be fun for them but at the same time it is an annoyance to anyone not involved and to me, that transcends nationality.  I don't think that culture has anything to do with it.   

If it did, you can be assured that the police would definitely side with the Thais if they could.   The fact remains that these people having the parties were breaking the law, if they weren't, the police wouldn't be able to do anything.  

Thus far the police have taken a neutral public stance on this, and I think they are correct in doing so.

><strong>Until now, I had always played exclusively in Modern mode; looking at my performance over the last few seasons, I typically hovered between Silver League Tier 2 and Gold League Tier 2. Take today, for instance: I’ve played perhaps only one or two battles in Modern mode—despite having plenty of energy left—whereas I’ve played over two dozen battles in Frontier since this morning. It has a unique appeal! Just two minutes ago, I unlocked Bronze League Tier 1 in this mode for the first time—and I did it using only those basic cards. It’s truly an achievement, and with this milestone, I received a total of 10 chests as \

body.body:

Many people ask whether a [mini chainsaw safe for beginners](https://chandakagroequipment.weebly.com/chandakagro/is-a-mini-chainsaw-safe-for-beginners-and-home-use ) is available for home and garden use. The answer is yes. A mini chainsaw is designed to be lightweight, compact, and easy to handle, making it suitable for first-time users.

Unlike larger chainsaws, mini chainsaws require less physical effort and offer better control during branch trimming, pruning, and light wood-cutting tasks. Most models include safety features such as chain guards, safety locks, anti-slip handles, and protective covers to enhance user protection.

Before operating the tool, wear protective gloves, safety glasses, and sturdy footwear. Always inspect the chain condition and ensure the tool is functioning correctly. Maintaining proper handling techniques can significantly improve safety and performance.

A good-quality mini chainsaw can help homeowners complete gardening and maintenance work quickly and conveniently. With proper operation and regular maintenance, it becomes a practical and dependable tool for everyday cutting tasks around the home and garden.

body.title: Захищаємо черешню від шпаків
body.body:
Вс садівники знають, що сорти ранньої черешні, які достигають в кінці травня на початку червня, є об'єктом полювання шпаків. Ці ненажерливі птахи літають зграями з десятків чи навіть сотні особин і шукають, де поласувати достиглою черешнею. 

З нашого сумного досвіду, коли така зграя сідає на черешню, достатньо 10 хвилин, аби вони з'їли весь врожай ягід на дереві.

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmXckkC2MePd5vt87PGXxEHgS4WWBgq9d8VKRZXCE2TT3e/1780893970110.jpg)

Але цього року ми знайшли дійсно працюючий четод захисту врожаю черешні від шпаків - це звичайна затіняюча сітка, якою слід вкрити дерево зверху, не обов'язково навіть щоб спускалась вона аж донизу. З цим методом ми цього року насолоджуємось врожаєм солодкої черешні.

body.title: Finding Rest for the Soul: A Viewscape Retreat
body.body:
Time to write a post about our soulful escape to Viewscape last June 5 and 6. 

![Viewscape.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/rzc24-nftbbg/EpnCpe5GEBjyTExbQjiBZFGz22zUfuk5hYimcGrnBhBfMwtY2EDqxnsc6xUdQg2dNBq.jpg)

Among 20 photos, I selected the above as the most captivating because of the unusual color of the sky.

![Viewscape17.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/rzc24-nftbbg/EpxriVbTUP8y4qbAbKyYK6LDU8CF2igBYNxzSyEomaQxpDiYdKjA6TKtk9yQE9oprsw.jpg)

The weather is not as good as last year. You will see the sky is cloudy. Upon arrival, we were greeted by rain. Thinking that tents could not protect us from rain, we decided to rent rooms. 

![Viewscape20.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/rzc24-nftbbg/Ep9ujwdSiUqHzJAcWWjBzdd3oVHm7aTB7P47ixdzzfzBGNeVceM3N7gjkVff28e6Ckr.jpg)

Last year, the sky was different. Every passing minute, we witnessed the changing colors of the sky. 

![Viewscape4.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/rzc24-nftbbg/EoGrZdG1erekdMvPFWL3YJEDuit2dXcnW2UnzQXQAAYeRYpys8tdeDLNtzGteNaPQGu.jpg)

The above photo was taken after our dinner. While waiting for dinner, our president shared his reflection on Mark 6:30-31. He appreciated the employees' services and emphasized the importance of rest and the beauty of God's revelation both in nature and Scripture.   

![Viewscape2.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/rzc24-nftbbg/Eo44Nx7tooz4cbDAXCDf7LDvCm914YMK4YrUGL9eYcEL4SDLpd6ksBMBzeFpeYzcPPg.jpg)

![Viewscape3.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/rzc24-nftbbg/EoCgaivLZRvGb1aedTSKZQG7yuHJ3FXqHHGRuZb6JB24LhC7hwKYJp7uNNRRaQhTd5z.jpg)

![Viewscape5.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/rzc24-nftbbg/23ynWg5DSQwWng6UArTXminZfYVcgt5kxAL8siHZZaRJxoMJxkidG9fweeqpEWxBFWhpC.jpg)

Both my brother-in-law and my sister were uncomfortable with the Nipa hut that we rented. The comfort room is too far, and so they decided to change rooms. 

![Viewscape6.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/rzc24-nftbbg/23ynQWShgTTAeq948iFptRFiRDNpRjhAKi4LQiJmGJtc1zGrujwdZbNf57zWS42nr6TkN.jpg)

We transferred to the Edge. The room is pricey but very comfortable. There were free slippers, a toothbrush, and toothpaste, and the towels were provided. 

![Viewscape7.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/rzc24-nftbbg/23sUF6Msr6LVSMvxbAPwhXcAzwhfJWHhvT8ECXmB5TEXt8EsQ3PisD24KQpAhceWuzkKJ.jpg)

![Viewscape8.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/rzc24-nftbbg/23vPGqVagwsjjLatMCx2b7mXMEyvqgB8Cj1LPMDwGD5QVhG6KW5vMngJ8jVFjDcLvV34Y.jpg)

The handsome gentlemen above are our hardworking maintenance team: Gerry and Jose. 

![Viewscape16.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/rzc24-nftbbg/EqL7kvnfNNTKTGjjT3UWe5F3N3w2Sq9hLp4AyiHUD7jJB2imYCnN8g2ecPuchFxBPHz.jpg)


![Viewscape18.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/rzc24-nftbbg/EpVBceJsLZdtFAhU4NrKAEW2WKRP1kcTHuunGRib9SjG6yTAkiJiJyheLCUEiUdMqGG.jpg)

![Viewscape19.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/rzc24-nftbbg/Eq5CyujV9aw8qjcWLs5o4oQKqWqXwWQkbX5XAtU2JxJGoDrQninnhJ2ZmTKXkXjXac4.jpg)

The following day, we enjoyed swimming and sharing stories for more or less two hours. 

![Viewscape13.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/rzc24-nftbbg/EoGxSUtwCKu7ZSuGDfLK2cqPL8VjU2iGWsTqLHXmFFfmF8M2Ex6fSqeJu16T76GDox9.jpg)

![Viewscape15.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/rzc24-nftbbg/EoyQuNK1EzTUwyfmht5c96BZMWfzTjuLQz9rVwNEefA6twC29YYKZLbJ8p8884DALnE.jpg)

![Viewscape14.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/rzc24-nftbbg/Ep5nDqnN6nQxH44XJjxndiG2bxQDasi7tScMmxbQnbBs82saB1vj1bSZgL9akpzYpCF.jpg)

![Viewscape10.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/rzc24-nftbbg/EowGbM8nay83uoL6L7GmVSEEYxphMXw6WUouczc9p8yA36UE9UsiQo9TsLjwmSzGQ3n.jpg)

After swimming, we rested for an hour and then packed up our things and went ahead to BNK Cafe and Resto for our lunch.

![Viewscape12.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/rzc24-nftbbg/EowGeGRgAwYth4VjnFweWL4o8KqKNeevpo1zZExvDBvZH63ywe6mLHZYoJWoCEhHi3T.jpg)

This is our last group photo before going back home to Bulacan and Cavite. 

Let me conclude this post with an extended reflection about the importance of rest. I intend to use this message for our school prayer meeting this coming Thursday. The text is from Matthew 11:28-30:

> 28 Come to me, all you who are weary and burdened, and I will give you rest. 29 Take my yoke upon you and learn from me, for I am gentle and humble in heart, and you will find rest for your souls. 30 For my yoke is easy and my burden is light.

I first published this message in my WordPress blog on [October 14, 2012](https://onlybygracerzc.wordpress.com/2012/10/14/rest-in-jesus/).

To introduce my topic, I mentioned inflation. That's the beauty of autobiographical blogging; you will gain a historical perspective. Imagine the time I updated this devotion, I was complaining for an 11 reduction in the number of HIVE (from 45 to 34) that my 1,000.00 PHP could buy. That shows a huge drop in the value of the Philippine peso.     

This time it's different. Last night, when I bought HIVE, the same amount could purchase 316 HIVE. For those who still believe in the long-term prospect of the network, this is an occasion for celebration. Imagine 282 additional units of HIVE with the same amount of PHP. This tells a different story. Cryptocurrency like HIVE is dropping faster than fiat money such as PHP. No wonder many are restless and despondent now.  

The point is financial devaluation, either in fiat or in crypto, is depressing and causes anxiety. 

I asked the same question that I asked before:   

> In a time when many people are stressed (financially, mentally, emotionally, and psychologically), where can we find rest?

Even though this message is old, I still find it very relevant to me personally and I think to many who also suffer financial distress.   

Let me share an old article about stress:
    
> On November 16, 2010, Kevin Spak of Newser wrote an article, “And the World’s Most Stressed People Are…\
gods.\

body.title: Herramientas básicas para crecer en Hive [ESP-ENG]
body.body:
![1001325933.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/ajolote/23xp6h3SNybSCLdyjEstVRRpkVg69CAV2Dj5aWTHuQy2iWhzCCHh5TspdmfZxbYLVHoJt.png)

---

<div class=text-justify>

### ¡Saludos querida Comunidad! 👋🏼🪸

Soy Ajolote, la Mascota del Proyecto @aliento. Mi fin es guiar a los usuarios que publican en la Comunidad Aliento y darle la bienvenida a los nuevos usuarios.

El motor del Proyecto Aliento es su gente, por eso nos entusiasma muchísimo recibir a quienes dan sus primeros pasos en la Web3, así como seguir ofreciendo nuestro respaldo y recomendaciones a los usuarios que mantienen su constancia y construyen su trayectoria en esta red.

​La educación y el aprendizaje nunca se detienen aquí; por ello, sin importar en qué etapa de tu viaje te encuentres, estamos seguros de que los consejos prácticos que hemos preparado para hoy te darán una perspectiva fresca para optimizar tu blog y sacarle el máximo provecho a la plataforma:

---
#### 5 Herramientas básicas para crecer en Hive:
***

#### 1️⃣ El peligro del plagio y la IA:
La autenticidad es la moneda más valiosa en la Web3. Intentar hacer pasar por propio un texto, una idea o una imagen que no te pertenece (o que fue generada enteramente por IA sin aclararlo) destruye tu reputación en segundos y puede hacer que tu cuenta termine silenciada.

**📌Tips:** Usa tu propia voz y comparte tus experiencias reales. Si te apoyas en herramientas de IA para traducir o corregir estilo, o si usas imágenes de stock, sé siempre transparente y colócalo en tus fuentes al final del post. Los curadores premian la honestidad por encima de la perfección.

#### 2️⃣ Seguridad de tus claves y contraseñas:
A diferencia de las redes tradicionales donde puedes recuperar tu cuenta con un correo, en Hive tú eres el único responsable de la seguridad de tus fondos. Si pierdes tu Master Key o tu Owner Key, o si caes en un enlace engañoso (phishing), puedes perder tu cuenta para siempre.

**📌Tips:** Jamás uses tu clave maestra o tu clave activa para iniciar sesión diariamente. Para eso existen extensiones y aplicaciones seguras como Hive Keychain. Guarda tus claves en un bloc de notas físico o en un dispositivo desconectado de internet y trátalas como el tesoro más preciado de tu blog.

#### 3️⃣ Usa la maquetación bilingüe:
Escribir solo en español está genial porque nuestra comunidad es gigante, pero Hive es un ecosistema global. Al presentar tu contenido de forma bilingüe en las demás comunidades (Español/Inglés), abres una ventana enorme para que curadores e inversores de otras partes del mundo entiendan y valoren tu trabajo. Es cierto que ya contamos con herramientas que nos permiten traducir al instante en algunas dApps, pero no te confíes de eso, muchos curadores no tienen el tiempo suficiente o se puede malinterpretar lo que quisiste compartir, por eso es mejor cuando tú mismo corriges tu traducción.

**📌Tips:** No uses bloques de texto mezclados. Organiza tu post en dos columnas limpias (usando códigos HTML de tablas) o coloca primero la versión completa en un idioma y luego el otro, separándolos con un buen banner. ¡Haz que la lectura sea cómoda para ambos públicos!

#### 4️⃣ Comparte en redes Web2:
Hacer clic en \

es solo la mitad del trabajo. Si quieres que tu blog crezca y atraiga a más personas, necesitas tender puentes con el exterior. Llevar tus posts de Hive a plataformas tradicionales te ayuda a construir una audiencia más sólida y más amplia.\n\n**📌Tips:** Aprovecha iniciativas como el \

o simplemente comparte el enlace de tu post en tus cuentas de X (Twitter), Instagram o threads, usando etiquetas relevantes. Esto no solo le da visibilidad a tu marca personal, sino que ayuda a traer nuevos usuarios al ecosistema.

#### 5️⃣ Mantén tu billetera en movimiento:
A veces nos concentramos tanto en crear contenido que olvidamos revisar la billetera. Hive tiene un mecanismo increíble donde tus ganancias en HBD pueden generar un rendimiento pasivo mensual si las colocas en la sección de \
(Ahorros).\n\n**📌Tips:** No dejes tus HBD estancados en la cuenta corriente de tu monedero si no los vas a usar de inmediato. Pasarlos a \

te permite proteger parte de tus ganancias y verlas crecer mes a mes con la tasa de interés vigente de la red. ¡Aprender de finanzas dentro de la blockchain también es parte del crecimiento!

***
¡El conocimiento es tu mejor escudo y tu mejor vela para navegar Hiver! Sigue cuidando tu contenido y tu seguridad, y el océano de Hive te recompensará. ¡El equipo de Aliento te deja estas nuevas coordenadas para que sigas conquistando la blockchain con paso firme! 🪸✨

>![ENGLISH VERSION]
>**Greetings dear Community!** 👋🏼🪸
​I am Ajolote, the Project @aliento Mascot. My goal is to guide users who post in the Aliento Community and to welcome new users.
>
>​The driving force behind Proyecto Aliento is its people; that is why we are thrilled to welcome those taking their first steps in Web3, as well as to continue offering our support and recommendations to users who maintain their consistency and build their journey on this network.
>
>Education and learning never stop here; therefore, no matter what stage of your journey you are in, we are sure that the practical tips we have prepared for today will give you a fresh perspective to optimize your blog and make the most out of the platform:
>
>**5 Basic tools to grow on Hive:**
>
>**1️⃣ The danger of plagiarism and AI:**
Authenticity is the most valuable currency in Web3. Trying to pass off text, ideas, or images that do not belong to you as your own (or that were generated entirely by AI without clarifying it) destroys your reputation in seconds and can cause your account to end up muted.
>
>**📌Tips:** Use your own voice and share your real experiences. If you rely on AI tools for translation or style correction, or if you use stock images, always be transparent and list them in your sources at the end of the post. Curators reward honesty over perfection.
>
>**2️⃣ Security of your keys and passwords:**
Unlike traditional networks where you can recover your account via email, on Hive you are the sole person responsible for the security of your funds. If you lose your Master Key or your Owner Key, or if you fall for a deceptive link (phishing), you can lose your account forever.
>
>**📌Tips:** Never use your master key or active key for daily login. Secure extensions and applications like Hive Keychain exist for that purpose. Keep your keys in a physical notebook or on a device disconnected from the internet, and treat them as your blog's most precious treasure.
>
>**3️⃣ The magic of bilingual formatting:**
Writing only in Spanish is great because our community is huge, but Hive is a global ecosystem. By presenting your content in a bilingual format (Spanish/English), you open a massive window for curators and investors from other parts of the world to understand and value your work. It is true that we already have tools that allow us to translate instantly on some dApps, but do not rely blindly on that; many curators do not have enough time, or what you wanted to share might be misinterpreted. That is why it is always better when you correct your translation yourself.
>
>**📌Tips:** Do not use mixed blocks of text. Organize your post into two clean columns (using HTML table codes) or place the full version in one language first and then the other, separating them with a nice banner. Make the reading experience comfortable for both audiences!
>
>**4️⃣ Share on Web2 networks:**
Clicking \

is only half the job. If you want your blog to grow and attract more people, you need to build bridges with the outside world. Bringing your Hive posts to traditional platforms helps you build a stronger and broader audience.\n>\n>**📌Tips:** Take advantage of initiatives like \

or simply share your post's link on your X (Twitter), Instagram, or Threads accounts, using relevant tags. This not only gives visibility to your personal brand but also helps bring new users into the ecosystem.
>
>**5️⃣ Keep your wallet moving:**
Sometimes we focus so much on creating content that we forget to check our wallet. Hive has an incredible mechanism where your earnings in HBD can generate monthly passive yield if you place them in the \
section.\n>\n>**📌Tips:** Do not leave your HBD sitting idle in your wallet's liquid account if you are not going to use them immediately. Moving them to \

![ChatGPT Image Jun 8, 2026, 11_09_14 AM.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/asgharali/23wqc4VzZB3a8D5SxjdDM6CtvgQypdo9EGhfwkyEr7xULMAT5XKpBLrwBJFcwaVnEvcWk.png)

Right now I have about 45,000 HIVE in liquid. I started investing at different levels (0.06, 0.055) and still buying to bring down my average.

When I looked at Hive in detail I understood that Hive is not just a coin but a complete ecosystem. It has social media platforms, games (Splinterland will be the reason for hive growth), communities and most importantly we have #HBD technology. That might be lagging for now but all will be well.

In 2021, many projects came and disappeared but Hive is still running and its community is still active. There is no need to worry about its price.


My biggest concern is not the technology but adoption... Today people in the crypto market mostly talk about AI narratives. Specially AI technologies are more preferred..

 Hive has good technology but it needs new users and developers. If user growth does not come, it becomes difficult for the price to move higher in a sustainable way. We have to wake up the DHF. Any further spending will no longer be acceptable nor affordable..

![HIVEUSDT_2026-06-08_11-06-09.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/asgharali/23t8CfKPuV4fdcBqQC4gU89eHc67oHqiYnhReEPtUaF7ukUMEkzhgtqqaKSj8M4pFaRbg.png)
![download.gif](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/asgharali/23xyw2uM74x6qu1Azy69rKZG79ou4jF3nQsKJLyBS1qWHb497tsKuZDt64M4Qy69snSx4.gif)

If we talk about price, HIVE's all-time high was around $3.40. Going back to that level is possible but it would require not only a bull market but also real adoption and ecosystem growth. 

In my view the $0.10 to $0.15 range looks like a more realistic target if market conditions remain favorable and Hive can expand its community. This is possible. #hive is right now at $0.048. If it reaches $0.03 or even $0.015, we will bear loss. But what if it recovers back to $0.15? 5X growth possible.. We are currently at very low and this price brings not hard concerns.

---
# What I did? 
---

I start buying #hive at $0.06 and keep on averaging till now..

This loss is very small compared to people who bought HIVE around $0.50, $1 or $3. Respect for them and sorry to them. 

What will I do with this #hive? I am waiting for the 25% recovery.. If in case the scenario gets worse, I will straight away powerup and will start earning curation rewards. I will surely hold for long term and will escape after price reaching $0.15 which is possible. Small market cap can go anywhere.


![HIVEUSDT_2026-06-08_11-08-33.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/asgharali/23t8DBnQF7Rohg6HaSTRF5pQ3x6iJYMUtM8jPp4PKYWWk5VrMkb4g299J5XkibqM6xXep.png)
![download.gif](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/asgharali/23xyw2uM74x6qu1Azy69rKZG79ou4jF3nQsKJLyBS1qWHb497tsKuZDt64M4Qy69snSx4.gif)


If someone asks me today what the future of Hive is?  my answer would be...

Hive has a good chance of surviving but its real success will depend on whether it can attract new users and developers... We need more and more new users. We need better technologies that attract people.  If adoption increases, reaching $0.15 is not difficult..

At this moment my focus is not on panic selling but on a long term strategy. We are already at all time low. Investors who did buying at these levels, needs not to be worry. It would be concerned if you had bought at $0.5 or around. But buying at all time low is always juicy.. 

Dont worry, Good times will surely come. Support your DHF and the witnesses that are surerly working hard for the betterment of ecosystem. United we stand and #hive rocks...

I hope you guys will like this post and is interesting as well. If you find it informative then dont forget to give me a support. Share you reviews in the comment section below. Thank you all for your time reading the content.

body.title: Are Podcast Networks becoming Creator Networks? | Greg Wasserman #666
body.body:
by @geeknewscentral on New Media Show w/Rob Greenlee 
View my bio on Blurt.media: https://blurt.media/c/newmediashow [![Are Podcast Networks becoming Creator Networks? | Greg Wasserman #666](https://blurt.media/lazy-static/previews/06a3059a-293c-40ff-9ce2-f3d09f1e491b.jpg)](https://blurt.media/w/3mZhjUea2tVBg2rPu1WAEz) 
 
 ![New Media Show with Rob Greenlee and guest Greg Wasserman](https://newmediashow.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/06/NMS-666-300x300-Episode-Art.jpg)In episode 666 of the New Media Show, hosted by **2017 Podcast Hall of Famer Rob Greenlee**, Rob talks with **Greg Wasserman, Head of Relationships at RSS.com and host of _Podcast Network Insights_**, for a _**deep conversation about one of the biggest questions** facing podcasting, video, creator media, and digital networks right now:_

**Podcast networks were originally built for an audio-first industry, but audiences have already moved the definition of a podcast beyond audio.** Today, a podcast can be a YouTube show, a Spotify video, an Apple video podcast, a livestream, a short clip, a newsletter, a community, or part of a larger creator-led media brand.

**Greg brings a unique perspective from his work at RSS.com and from interviewing the leaders behind podcast networks, collectives, production companies, and niche media groups on _Podcast Network Insights_**. He explains that podcast networks are no longer one simple model. Some are media-sales businesses. Some are community-driven groups. Some operate more like production companies, collectives, or full creator networks.

> _**Rob and Greg explore how the network model is shifting as video, live streaming, AI, Apple Podcasts, HLS video, YouTube, Netflix, Spotify, FAST channels, private communities, and creator monetization reshape what podcasting can become.**_

**The conversation also asks whether independent podcasters should join networks**, what creators need to understand before making that decision, and why the future may depend less on downloads alone and more on trust, audience relationships, collaboration, niche value, and direct monetization.

body.title: Heat is a strange thing. Sometimes it's excessive...
body.body:
Heat is a strange thing. Sometimes it's excessive, and sometimes there's a shortage of it, and it's very difficult to say what constitutes ideal warmth. Boiler workers, who supply the coolant to the pipes that, in turn, heat our homes, know best what constitutes ideal warmth. Although, I remember once renting an apartment in another city, and the building manager there was in charge of the heating system, regulating the temperature at his own discretion, which was completely at odds with my idea of ​​what warmth should be in winter. LOL. The feeling you experience when you're lacking warmth can, in principle, be tricked. For example, by tensing all your muscles and then suddenly relaxing them. This provides a few seconds of warmth when your hands are numb from the cold. ![DSC02783.JPG](https://cdn.steemitimages.com/DQmYN15KcgNtPfuxgjN36Lqx6XhaNtPjdaoaKzjJPswtRYZ/DSC02783.JPG) But sometimes, there's also mental warmth. It's enough to look at the photograph in which I see a warm summer and my soul becomes warmer. ![DSC04931.JPG](https://cdn.steemitimages.com/DQmUkS5PYQqW2hh8SZC3oi4DyrWgv6idPBoDarCUBKrP6qp/DSC04931.JPG) Zoom in on a photo for a closer view. *** Below you can see my containers with data that I collect in INLEO and always have quick access to them it is very convenient. body.body:
https://play.3speak.tv/embed?v=angelmitu/18hgfsjy

The evil monsters of the underworld have taken Jack's family captive, so Jack will embark on a mission to rescue them.Hey this is a game line.The name of the game is Incredible Jack.The game is so beautiful that I really like it and this is the first time I have played this game.Jack as the main character and me on the mobile screen.

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmU91TrguHaCoUVS9vgruxTAZhXk41cF38UBonXakDsZ2Y/screenshot_20260608_082754_2.png)

Hey friends, I forgot to say good morning.Good morning friends, how are you? I hope you are all doing well.Everyone gather around because I have an interesting game today.It is a very interesting and fun game.This is not only a fun game, but it also shows a father's duty and love for his family.A father will risk his life to save his family.Let's talk more about this classic and action adventure game!🎯 

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmfF4Bs2FTaCsFmxSe7gdqCEPid94oUGPPpUWSEFAwXSu7/screenshot_20260608_082905_2.png)

How well known are the evil demons of underworld? Because I used to listen to their stories as a child, playing this game reminded me of the past.I used to listen to stories like the demonic old woman or the underworld when I was a child.However today's game is very similar to that story.

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmZGLHNZhggTwD2xGEEwiBN8SZW66qE5XSed74zZQ4KQRn/screenshot_20260608_083018_2.png)

The game teaches us how much a father's love for his family is.This is a classic action adventure 2D platformer game.The game is set in the olden days.However the main character is brave Jack and I am on the mobile screen above.The biggest advantage I found here is that the game can be played offline.Let's find out how Jack rescues his family.Lets walk.

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmVMqYmzMLzBdCLR66HgatEboZSn328CEhTJXPgpkvcbGw/screenshot_20260608_083143_2.png)

The main goal is for Jack to enter the monster kingdom and rescue his family because the monsters have captured his family.Jack has started his journey.He will face many problems on this journey because the roads are not good.There are dangerous places like hilly areas and sandy tombs or ice caves and these places have to be crossed.But I don't want to lose here.

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmVFRvcSzFZQqGSHgjBKXbwX4LAFtmUVHyEVdT9MVtdMHb/screenshot_20260608_083241_2.png)

But the best news is that I passed the first level and found my child, means Jack's child.Getting Jack's child back first is his first big success.Then, leaving her child safe, she set out again to rescue the rest of her family.But then disaster struck.

body.title: Up the steps of Menton to a great view
body.body: While I was watching the Grand Prix Porsche race on Sunday, before the main [F1 race in Monaco](https://ecency.com/@duskobgd/monaco-f1-championship-formula-1) (a race of cars that, even when it is not a race, are driven on the streets of Monte Carlo), one comment of the presenter while the shot above Monte Carlo, overlooking the sea, caught my attention.\n\n\

I was lucky enough to visit Monte Carlo and several cities on the Cote d'Azur, and one of the most interesting views I had was in Menton.
And in order to get to the position where such a view is offered, it was necessary to overcome several hundred steps🙂


![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmX48jUeiUwZ98G7uUjQyDGN4hgLCrSzXQExGNc3J3e635/1780897089786.jpg)




You can reach the stairs by walking along the promenade along the coast, when you pass by restaurant gardens, buildings with beautiful facades, and by beautiful parks and tree-lined streets.

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmVKyto9EaFuwc5tDEdDDvm7zRG6dFj8rgpgp9eKBU5HXT/1780897123288.jpg)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmSPi1tbQb3yVNWnX2L4aJV134va6RWbVvwjKP8XBrBViC/1780897123375.jpg)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmNpCASc5Pp6hiq67PxRdrBcwwDdAmZ6Sb1UVLdgPfFEYt/1780898235687.jpg)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmPUBBwtGGbMRZU2iCUHR9Yx2EnupMSVqSDTVtrGKRqWWX/1780897123458.jpg)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmXG9cUpbWrQ3QtPmcdRFoFXoJnVQAEzwH3VZcDL6qVDqk/1780897123526.jpg)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmfYABQ5nZSiiQkSsiwtkX3ynfoiSQo3gwLUhXbsa9JxLx/1780897123610.jpg)

When it breaks out on the beautiful and wide beach, which I wrote about in the previous post, where I immortalized myself next to the name of the city and a big yellow lemon, in the background you can see those steps leading to the top.

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmVKyto9EaFuwc5tDEdDDvm7zRG6dFj8rgpgp9eKBU5HXT/1780897185558.jpg)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmXG53xdc6qPRM6ektMjGyxq76bPdQzSVpCUFVQPciwtTv/1780897185633.jpg)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmXBxh3scoVKzBRZ1R6AYDCUsewmvC25ytqyCmgiB79mbR/1780897185742.jpg)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmPUaCnnxyhohZEfBEc4JzDUJTYKkXsBM83TogS4Dp65Bj/1780897185824.jpg)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmSw7PJKkZuTN5owL2HR2yDpCqXmVEWB5tHe9kBKgFT7DP/1780897185889.jpg)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmZ7QbaLDorv4Cum8LxJqJSuQkLGhk26y4Nq3kVRJAk1jH/1780897199879.jpg)

There are no elevators or escalators (or we didn't find them), so we walked slowly up the hill, through the gate, step by step.
We stopped at each level of stairs, not only to take a break, but to enjoy the view that unfolded before our eyes.

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmVRotfLwJXi9JL9wGLNSwZSV6xKPqLqotDdu5QshjVJny/1780897260738.jpg)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmX4kCHPqBMuoKqnoH3axeraCewyccUtXZe8wZfMEnWKiW/1780897260804.jpg)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmY96gcL9kB5qSP94czQdaR64NUKn91YBvsb7TYcWmtAVo/1780897260891.jpg)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmbdNgcXG2fGKmyM4haMtSpaoHVsFgbykMSaQbuym4HXji/1780897260964.jpg)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmcgU43mKytLDMTepsPzH2gQJwyrz2mCsArou2ZurZFMwb/1780897261032.jpg)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmQZSErZG5gHVE8ezmt6MrPdQW62jhGARh327TZnsUin2J/1780897218831.jpg)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmSJkEbrsVkUAv5n4H1mkFChqrHTcfYTTV7EmA6VvLdHea/1780897289398.jpg)


At the top of the stairs is a small square, in front of the entrance to the two cathedrals.

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmdMz3o6kRQonSVnGxcuhLSE1QJvsXYKJfQVhaCdoHx8bi/1780897314207.jpg)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmeN9p2VCutWvCcE1Jd6BXsjuF4eYmVxPsP41UCeMHkDR4/1780897314278.jpg)

Basilique Saint-Michel Archange de Menton, built in the period 1619-1675, with two towers, a 53-meter high belfry that dominates the city and a lower clock tower that is 35 meters high.

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmbGt7fRcZwPy15TSJ2TjTVGUmi7PwXo4qJeGNJa3EUTXw/1780897340588.jpg)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmaQ7j2Mp5NL24peVKqpehLaTWdhS5i2RCpby6dt9pL7hg/1780897340666.jpg)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQme7era9LY6YPTR6SGXyuc5umgMvWmSUGBrUrijPhtJvMT/1780897340746.jpg)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQme3j2cjUPX48dqFhqS95e1mmydUtjD81tbDvgrhAhijHM/1780897340815.jpg)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmZhHmR4XcK7KAms3RQYLPt5VdrGNo2FmdH8cEtwRLkoC6/1780897340881.jpg)

Like the Chapelle des Pénitents-Blancs, built in the period 1680-1689, it was the home of the White Penitents, a brotherhood founded in Menton for the care of the elderly, sick persons and abandoned children, who were responsible for the proper burial of the deceased. The brotherhood of penitents was dissolved in 1970 because the last member of the brotherhood died in 1969. This chapel was built in a luxurious baroque style with a tower and beautiful statues on the facade.



We didn't manage to enter those two places of worship, but we took a break on the steps in front of one of them and then enjoyed the view from the plateau.



![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmUBHR9XtLHEWjuax9kuCrE9PMZinWuDpkTK7S7xFCdzH3/1780898159502.jpg)

The view is beautiful, but it is a little narrower because of the buildings that frame it, so we started to climb a little more. Passing through the so-called donkey steps, a narrow passage that leads from the plateau in front of the chapel to the upper town (they were called donkey steps because they used to supply the upper town with food on donkeys).

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmRPvV6TyMCoM3BqF77gMy39uSEqk5hL2CZJqG2Rs7SMrP/1780898184187.jpg)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmUy4LeGzRW2ZiDorxSiGtGFdiN8DzsBUVUFMizWD6zeqW/1780898184272.jpg)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmac7yi8qV1E7C3E26R8bRJfb8yp4J1bCtG45yTXEn2r3p/1780898184335.jpg)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmYM8DMVXiARYb3c7ohhv13fN1e6CU5Xf6oW2qGYKn2WnN/1780898184387.jpg)


The history of the old town of Menton can easily be checked on wikipedia: founded at the end of the 12th century by the rulers of Genoa, in the 14th century taken over by the Grimaldi family, until the middle of the 19th century, when the town was annexed to France.
An interesting thing that I discovered only after visiting the old, upper town of Menton, was discovering that the mosaic in the square in front of the cathedral (a combination of 250,000 stones of different colors) represents the coat of arms of the city of Menton and the Grimaldi family.
But, if we ignore the historical facts, the interesting story is the one written on the board next to the entrance to the upper town.
Founded by three pirates from the island of Lampedusa, the upper town was built as a fortress with low houses that were built over time. For this reason, it is not surprising that the houses are narrow but tall.
There was also a castle in the upper town that was demolished over the centuries and from the remains of which a cemetery was formed on the very top of the hill, perhaps the most beautiful in all of France (about that in the next post 🙂 ).

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmZANvD9ypJG1xDhgTmnnVnfigMJ1XhJ4u84HXwHXLqE5K/1780898216498.jpg)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmT5tUdm8ae1jfugH6SGMxAARefmrWoa5vEFxCEH7VC94E/1780898216563.jpg)

Walking through the narrow picturesque streets, with a very steep ascent, I passed a fountain from the end of the 19th century with drinking water, where I refreshed myself a bit and continued the ascent.

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmYwg6BXyHx7djhSBKyRr2QNkwpEPwhybdJotvb6bKHF5j/1780898401703.jpg)
 Ascending as if through a labyrinth (following the road signs to get to where I was headed), I understood parts of the story that the upper town with the houses was built in such a way that it resembled a labyrinth, so that the attackers of the town would be as confused as possible and that the residents would be able to defend themselves as easily as possible.
And the view, when I passed through all these beautiful narrow streets, was worth every step.

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmXUDC8u6vZDpWy7oju4WmfSPC3pjBtf8z6U3KbHnhPXFU/1780898432543.jpg)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmS8mvm6YrZYwYgN9kjYs9HocgFGhcH2G9T233BGkHbuZT/1780898432681.jpg)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmczJ19vriK788AE2apxaVtgELLMt2rUra3Bnfvbcwf1yf/1780898432732.jpg)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmepr8LPHUHXU74cJXAsRRgfpApYQXZPCvvTZKUcZWHjPd/1780898432788.jpg)

At first I was surprised when I saw cyclists pushing their bikes along these narrow streets. 

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmQiNgo7PRjdJ3ye9RfCkWqcS1UuWXTYkq47ckC2XyAYDV/1780898587383.jpg)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmes4AK8yqqXSqJwxD2W4UsFVie4fRZgXtvGK4nma4oLB6/1780898599480.jpg)

But when I saw the road where cars and cyclists go at the entrance to the cemetery, it was clearer to me, maybe I could have reached this point by transport. I feel like this, a pawn in the ascent. was much more authentic.
The top of the stairs and the square in front of the cathedral can be reached from the lower town, also through very narrow streets, but we passed them in the opposite direction, going down the same to the lower part of the old town, when we came out on the beach again.

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmXCHAXmU77NZ1HueYtQE5UhHCt346wWN5epZNT8LHAtDv/1780898632861.jpg)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmTr44oWSH8BCobb2mkX1N6ZYXWBBsafMG1W3WEK1j9iME/1780898632951.jpg)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmbPprvseZEJXZVaUW1Hpd1zzEKAnQfjEpcgojnJEKWyJj/1780898633034.jpg)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmTdsSukGTLbL98Cixv5uhZTFXUJPTR5EGpa6FbSn4B1iQ/1780898648449.jpg)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmbkEaL3jJZ9ZmmnUaDrmeiq18YKLGP7M9ADfg56PXEkfR/1780898648529.jpg)


![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmP4vvVNFDZLA78XGpXzreabmoai4j3mM1cPgA1g74Aj1m/1780898757005.jpg)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmNLmFvL6EsZnbZy9soGbzRFBs3mBfBHRPB6UB2onPo6bn/1780898757080.jpg)

After we arrived in the lower town and found the ice cream fridge, our Menton adventure ended there.
